children.translated_text: The section on <s>kāñcanāra</s> is textually damaged.

children.text: kāñcanāro vṛkṣaviśeṣaḥ pratseddhaḥ ātasthapaśaṣmaṃtvacovārasaḥ svarasaḥ sūtakaḥ pāra daḥ gandhakaśca samānastayoḥ kaktī kāryeti sambandhaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kāñcanāra</s> is a well-known particular tree; its fresh juice is the expressed juice of the bark. <s>Sūtaka</s>, that is mercury, and sulphur are to be in equal quantity, and from the two a <s>kajjālī</s> is to be made: this is the connection.
The gold leaves, the leaves of gold, are to be in equal measure.

children.text: tayā kajjalyāvabhayā svarṇapatrapāraīmāṇayā śeṣaṃ vidhānaṃ pūrvavat
children.translated_text: With that black <s>kajjālī</s>, in the measure of the gold leaf and mercury, the remaining procedure is as before.

children.text: kotkaīlaumīti śuṣkagomayasaṃjñaiḥ aṅgārairvā yataḥ vahniṃ khara tara kuryāditi grahaṇāt evamityamunā prakāreṇa puṭatra yatmatyatrāgnerboddhavyam
children.translated_text: The phrase about dung-cakes means by what are called dry cow-dung cakes, or by coals; since the instruction is that one should make the fire very intense, in this manner the fire in the <s>puṭa</s> heating is to be understood.
Alternatively, from the procedure for <s>kāñcanāra</s> one should also understand the procedure for <s>lāṅgalī</s>.

children.text: lāṅgalī kalihārī athavāntalāmukhīprakāramapi kāñcanāraprakāradboddhavyamā jyā amumī jayantī sā catukhairdhā bhavāta śvetā raktā tathā pītā kṛlyāā jvālatyukhī bhavet iti
children.translated_text: <s>Lāṅgalī</s> is <s>kalihārī</s>. Or the procedure for <s>antalāmukhī</s> too should be understood from the <s>kāñcanāra</s> procedure. This <s>jayantī</s> is of four kinds: white, red, yellow, and a dark, flame-faced variety.

children.text: etajjā ticatuṣṭayaṃ śvetā raktā raktāādaīkusumaiḥ kṛtvā jānī yāt ||
children.translated_text: One should recognize this set of four species by their flowers, such as white and red flowers.
Now he states the proper nature and activity of the <s>doṣa</s>s.
On the words 'of the hand'.

children.text: jīvasākṣiṇī yā dhamanī sa karasyāṅguṣṭhe'stīti kriyāpadaṃ yojyaṃ tacceṣṭayā kṛtvā kāyasya śarīrasya sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca jñeyaṃ paṇḍitairiti śeṣaḥ dhamanīti ||
children.translated_text: The artery that is witness to life is in the thumb of the hand; the verb 'is' should be supplied. By its activity the body's comfort and pain are to be known by learned experts: this is the remainder. As to the word 'dhamanī':

children.text: śabdavāhinī nāḍī dhamanī jīvanaṃ tanau ityato dhamanī jīvasākṣiṇīti prāṇavāyoḥ sākṣibhūtā ata eva kutracij jīvanāḍīti kathitā ||
children.translated_text: A channel that carries sound is a <s>nāḍī</s>; a <s>dhamanī</s> is life in the body. Therefore the <s>dhamanī</s> is the witness of life, since it is the witness of the vital wind; for that very reason it is elsewhere called the life-pulse.
For so it is said:
The life-pulse displays the <s>doṣa</s>'s own form, separately, together, and in paired combinations,

children.text: mūkasya mugdhasya vimohitasya dīpaḥ padārthāniva jīvanāḍī
children.translated_text: for the mute, the dull, and the bewildered, just as a lamp displays objects.
Thus.
And the definition too is as follows:
On the outer side of the forearm bone, resting on the middle and ring fingers,
that is called the life-pulse, <s>Nandinī</s>, the knower of reality.
Thus.
In the phrase 'pain by its activity,' pain is the state consisting in the imbalance of the <s>doṣa</s>s and so on.
For there is the statement and the like: 'Disease is the disequilibrium of the <s>doṣa</s>s.'
By 'learned experts' is meant skilled persons, that is, those who know the particular times for taking the pulse.
For:
In one who has just bathed, one who has eaten, or one habituated to hunger, thirst, and heat,
and in one whose body is exhausted by exercise, the pulse is not properly understood.
Thus.
Now he states the activity of the pulse in <s>sannipāta</s> and <s>saṃsarga</s>, combined and associated disorders.
On the word 'pulse'.

children.text: marutkope vātaprakope jalaukāsarpayor gatiṃ gamanaṃ dhatte nāḍīti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When <s>marut</s>, that is <s>vāta</s>, is aggravated, the pulse assumes the movement of a leech and a snake.
The intended point is that the leech and snake move transversely; so too here.

children.text: pittaprakopatastu kuliṅgādīnāṃ gatiṃ dhatte kuliṅgo gṛhacaṭakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But from aggravation of <s>pitta</s> it assumes the movement of the <s>kuliṅga</s> and the others; a <s>kuliṅga</s> is a house sparrow.
The crow and frog are well known; the meaning is that these have a leaping movement.

children.text: eke kuliṅgasthāne kalāpīti paṭhanti vyākhyānayanti ca ||
children.translated_text: Some read <s>kalāpī</s> in place of <s>kuliṅga</s> and explain it accordingly.
A <s>kalāpī</s> is a peacock.
From aggravation of <s>śleṣma</s> it assumes the movement of a goose and a pigeon.
Here too 'the pulse' is to be supplied.
By this the intended meaning is that it becomes a slow-moving current.
For the goose and the pigeon too have a slow gait.
On the word '<s>lāva</s>'.

children.text: sannipātatastridoṣakopāt lāvādīnāṃ gamanaṃ nāḍī dhatte iti pūrvād anuvartate ||
children.translated_text: From <s>sannipāta</s>, the aggravation of the three <s>doṣa</s>s, the pulse assumes the movement of the <s>lāva</s> and the others; this is carried over from the preceding statement.
The <s>lāva</s> and the <s>tittira</s> are well known; <s>varti</s> is what is denoted by the word <s>vartikā</s>.
Others call it <s>gaḍūruka</s>.
For these, an agitated, jumping movement is indicated.
Even from the aggravation of two <s>doṣa</s>s, the pulse is sometimes slow-moving and sometimes swift-flowing.
Now he states the mark of an incurable condition.
On the word 'it kills'.
A pulse displaced from its place, moved from its own proper place, is to be supplied.
'It kills' means 'it kills the patient'; this is to be supplied.

children.text: yā sthitvā sthitvā calati gacchati sāpi prāṇanāśinī jñeyā ||
children.translated_text: The pulse that moves only after stopping again and again should also be known as destructive of life.
By this the intended point is that at times it flows and at times it does not flow.

children.text: atikṣīṇā ceti bisatantuvat atiśītā ceti himasparśavat ||
children.translated_text: 'Extremely weak' means like a lotus fiber; 'very cold' means like the touch of snow.

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ niścayena jīvitaṃ prāṇān hanti nāḍīti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Without doubt, certainly, the pulse destroys life, that is, the vital breaths.
From the word 'and,' one should also understand a crooked pulse, and one habitually moving upward and downward, as destructive of life.
And so it has been said:
The pulse that runs in the middle and leaps greatly at the root of the thumb,
moving slowly upward and downward in a crooked manner, kills a human being.
Thus.
Now he states the signs of the artery in fever and the like.
On the phrase 'by aggravation of fever'.

children.text: jvarakopeṇa sāmānyajvarasya prakopeṇa kṛtvā dhamanī nāḍī soṣṇā uṣṇayuktā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Through aggravation of fever, that is, through aggravation of fever in general, the <s>dhamanī</s>, the pulse, becomes warm, endowed with heat.
Because fever is of the nature of heat, it is not only warm but also swift.
This is because fever heats the body, the senses, and the mind.
From desire and anger too it flows swiftly, endowed with speed; because it lacks heat, it differs from the pulse of fever.

children.text: kāmo'bhimatakāminyādyaprāptiḥ krodho hiṃsātmakādirūpaḥ cintābhayapluteti cintābhayayuktā nāḍī kṣīṇā susūkṣmā jñeyā ||
children.translated_text: Desire is the non-attainment of a desired woman and the like; anger has a form beginning with violence. A pulse overcome by anxiety and fear should be known as weak and very subtle.
Anxiety has the form of mental agitation; fear is fear of enemies and the like.
Some read 'from anxiety, fear, and fatigue'.
From anxiety, fear, and fatigue the pulse should be known as weak and very subtle.
Anxiety should be known as having the form of mental agitation.

children.text: tatra śramād glāneḥ mandāgneḥ kṣīṇadhātośca puruṣasya nāḍī mandatarā bhavet atyarthaṃ mandagatir ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, from fatigue, exhaustion, weak digestive fire, and depleted bodily elements, a person's pulse becomes slower still, that is, extremely slow in movement.

children.text: asṛkpūrṇā rudhiraprakopāt pūritā nāḍī koṣṇā gurvī ca bhavet ||
children.translated_text: A pulse filled with blood, because of the aggravation of blood, becomes warm and heavy.

children.text: koṣṇā īṣaduṣṇā gurvī gurutarā pāṣāṇavad ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Koṣṇā means slightly hot; gurvī means very heavy, that is, like a stone.
Some read soṣṇā, 'with heat'.

children.text: sāmā āmayuktā nāḍī garīyasī syāt atyarthaṃ gurvī bhavatīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A sāmā pulse, one joined with āma, should be very weighty; the sense is that it becomes extremely heavy.

children.text: āmena saha vartata iti sāmā āmo'paripakvarasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sāmā means that which exists together with āma; āma is unripe rasa.
For example:
The rasa which, because of weakness of the gastric fire, is not digested
is called āma in the body and aggravates all the doṣas.
Thus.

children.text: athavā āmagrahaṇena āmāditrayam annajamajīrṇaṃ gṛhyate tena tairyuktetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Alternatively, by the mention of āma, the triad beginning with āma, namely indigestion produced from food, is understood; therefore the meaning is 'associated with those'.
Among these are āma, vidagdha, and viṣṭabdha.
Some read sāmā garīyasī, 'the sāmā pulse is heavier'.
Sāmā means that which exists together with āma.
And these are the doṣas, the dūṣyas, and so on.
For:

children.text: āmena tena saṃpṛktā doṣā dūṣyāśca dūṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: The doṣas mixed with that āma, and the dūṣyas that have been vitiated,
are taught as sāmā, as are the diseases that arise from them.
Thus.

children.text: etena kim uktaṃ bhavati sāmadoṣāt sāmadūṣyāt sāmadūṣitāt sāmarogācceti ||
children.translated_text: By this, what is stated is: from a sāmadoṣa, from a sāmadūṣya, from what is vitiated by āma, and from a sāmaroga, a disease involving āma.
The dūṣyas.
First, he states their number with the words 'gold' and so on.
The seven dhātus, beginning with gold and ending with tīkṣṇa, should be understood.
In particular, seven dhātus are to be known.

children.text: yatastantrāntare aṣṭa dhātava iti manyante tatrāṣṭadhā lohasaṃjñā ||
children.translated_text: For in another tantra they consider there to be eight dhātus; there the designation loha is eightfold.
Thus:

children.text: svarṇaṃ tāraṃ tāmranāgaṃ raṅgaṃ kāntaṃ ca tīkṣṇakam
children.translated_text: Gold, tāra, copper, nāga, raṅga, kānta, and tīkṣṇaka,
with muṇḍa as the last, make loha eightfold; kāṃsya, āra, and ghoṣaka are declared to be the three upalohas,
and so forth.
After that, the wise man who knows their distinctions should purify those below.

children.text: tān svarṇādīn atra svarṇaṃ prasiddham tāraṃ raupyam āraṃ pītalohaṃ tacca tāmraghoṣabhedābhyāṃ saṃjātamityeke bhāṣante ||
children.translated_text: Those beginning with gold: here gold is well known; tāra is silver; āra is yellow metal, and some say that it is produced from varieties of copper and ghoṣa.

children.text: atraiva ghoṣabhedo loke jasada iti vācyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this context, the ghoṣa variety itself is to be called jasada in ordinary usage.
But in the view of <s>Śiva</s>, only six are to be accepted, because they are born from gods.
Thus:

children.text: śivasya tejaḥ prathito rasendro devībhavaṃ gandhamathābhrakaṃ ca
children.translated_text: The energy of <s>Śiva</s> is famed as rasendra; also gandha and abhraka born from <s>Devī</s>,

children.text: śulvaṃ tu sūryasya sahasraraśmeścandrasya raupyaṃ parameśvarasya ||
children.translated_text: copper from the thousand-rayed <s>Sūrya</s>, and silver from <s>Candra</s>, the supreme lord.

children.text: hemaṃ tu viṣṇoḥ prabhavaṃ vadanti nāgaṃ ca nāgasya tu vāsukeśca
children.translated_text: They say that gold has its origin from <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and nāga from the serpent <s>Vāsuki</s>.

children.text: lohaṃ yamasyaiva tu kālamūrtervaṅgaṃ ca śukrasya purāvido budhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Iron is from <s>Yama</s>, whose form is Time, and vaṅga from <s>Śukra</s>, say the wise knowers of ancient lore.
Thus.
Therefore the item called āra is secondary and dependent on conditions.
'Gold', and so on.

children.text: suvarṇādīnāṃ caturṇāṃ patrāṇi kṛtvā tāni cāgnau punaḥ saṃtaptāni kṛtvā vakṣyamāṇadravyeṣu tridhā trivelaṃ yathā syānniṣiñcayet pratyekamiti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After making leaves of the four beginning with gold, heating them again in fire, one should quench them in the substances to be mentioned, three times each; 'individually' is to be supplied.

children.text: evaṃ suvarṇādīnāṃ caturṇāṃ viśuddhirbhavati svarṇādilohānāmiti grahaṇena tīkṣṇādīnāmapi śuddhirevaṃ boddhavyā ||
children.translated_text: In this way the purification of the four beginning with gold takes place; by the mention of metals beginning with gold, the purification of tīkṣṇa and the others should also be understood in the same way.

children.text: atra tailaṃ tilasaṃbhavaṃ ca takraṃ tribhāgabhinnaṃ kāñjikaṃ prasiddham kulattho'nnaviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the oil is sesame oil; takra is divided into three parts; kāñjika is well known; kulattha is a particular kind of grain.
Now, showing the special purification of nāga and vaṅga, he says 'nāga' and so on.

children.text: prataptāvityagnau saṃtāpitau ata eva gālitāviti dravībhūtau kṛtvā tairniṣiñcayediti taiḥ pūrvoktatailatakrādidravaiḥ tridhā tridheti pratyekaṃ tailādibhirniṣiñcayed ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Prataptau means heated in fire; therefore, after making them gālitau, that is, liquefied, one should quench them with those, namely with the previously stated liquids such as oil and takra, three times each; the intention is that each is to be quenched in oil and the others.

children.text: viśeṣamapi na kevalaṃ pūrvoktadravyair niṣiñcayet kiṃtu ravidugdhenārkakṣīreṇāpi tridhā kṛtvā śodhayediti pūrvaśodhanādayameva viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Not only should one quench them specially in the previously stated substances, but one should also purify them three times with ravidugdha, that is, the latex of arka; this alone is the special feature beyond the earlier purification.
Now, among the metals, he states the incineration of gold, saying 'from gold' and so on.

children.text: sūtaṃ pāradaṃ tacca suvarṇaparimāṇāt dviguṇaṃ grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: Sūta means mercury, and it should be taken in twice the quantity of the gold.

children.text: amlena bījapūrādinā tadgolakasamaṃ gandhamiti tat svarṇapāradakṛtena golakena sāmyaṃ śodhitagandhakaṃ saṃgṛhya tadgolakasyādhaḥ upari ca dattvā śarāvasaṃpuṭe saṃdhārya puṭediti granthābhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With an acid such as bījapūra; and 'gandha equal to that pellet' means that, after taking purified sulfur equal to the pellet made from the gold and mercury, placing it below and above that pellet, and sealing it in a pair of earthen saucers, one should subject it to a puṭa heating; this is the intention of the text.

children.text: sampradāye kiṃcid gandhakaṃ dattvā golakaṃ kāryaṃ paścāt śeṣaṃ gandhamupari deyam ||
children.translated_text: In the tradition, after adding a little sulfur one should make the pellet; afterwards the remaining sulfur should be placed above.
'A firm sealed capsule'.

children.text: dṛḍhagrahaṇena mṛtkarpaṭakaṃ sūcyate tena mṛtkarpaṭake nātra dṛḍhatā kāryā ||
children.translated_text: By the word 'firm', a clay-covered cloth is indicated; therefore firmness is not to be produced here apart from the clay-cloth covering.

children.text: evaṃ caturdaśapuṭaiḥ kṛtvā nirutthaṃ jāyate suvarṇamiti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, after being treated with fourteen puṭas, the gold becomes niruttha; this is to be supplied.

children.text: nirutthatātrātyarthamūrchanā kathyate na tu svarṇasya mṛtirbhavati ||
children.translated_text: Here nirutthatā is said to be an extreme mūrchanā, not that the gold actually becomes dead.
The puṭa here should be given with thirty forest-cow-dung cakes.
And that is prescribed under the name kukkuṭapuṭa.
Vanopala means dried cow dung, and that is denoted by the word karaṇḍa.
'Gandha should be added again and again.'

children.text: śuddhagandhakaṃ ca pūrvoktavidhānena pratyekaṃ puṭaṃ yojyamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This means that purified sulfur should be applied in each puṭa by the previously stated method.
He states another incineration of gold, saying 'kāñcana' and so on.

children.text: kāñcane svarṇe gālite drāvite sati tatra nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ nikṣipet ṣoḍaśāṃśena kāñcanaparimāṇāt nāgaṃ grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: When kāñcana, gold, has been melted and liquefied, one should put nāga, lead, into it in a sixteenth part; nāga should be taken as one-sixteenth of the measure of the gold.
Amla is represented by mātuluṅga.
'Below and above.'
Gandhaka should be placed both above and below the pellet.
And the procedure for sealing should be done as before.

children.text: kecidatra vanopalair viṃśatisaṃkhyakaireva manyante evamityanena prakāreṇa saptapuṭaiḥ kṛtvā hemabhasma bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Some here understand it as being with exactly twenty dried cow-dung cakes. By this method, after performing seven <s>puṭa</s> heatings, gold <s>bhasma</s> (calcined ash) is produced.
On "<s>kāñcanāra</s>":
<s>Kāñcanāra</s> is a well-known particular tree.

children.text: tasya patrāṇāṃ tvaco vā rasaḥ svarasaḥ sūtakaḥ pāradaḥ gandhakaśca samānastayoḥ kajjalī kāryeti sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The juice of its leaves or bark is the fresh juice. <s>Sūtaka</s> is mercury; sulphur equal to it should be made into <s>kajjalī</s> with it. That is the syntactic connection.
"Gold leaves" means leaves of gold; "in equal measure" is to be supplied.

children.text: tayā kajjalyā samayā svarṇapatraparimāṇayā śeṣaṃ vidhānaṃ pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: With that <s>kajjalī</s>, equal in amount to the gold leaves, the rest of the procedure is as before.

children.text: kokilairiti śuṣkagomayasaṃjñaiḥ aṅgārairvā yataḥ vahniṃ kharataraṃ kuryāditi grahaṇāt evamityamunā prakāreṇa puṭatrayam ityatrāgner boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: By "<s>kokila</s>" are meant what are called dried cow-dung cakes, or else embers, since the text says that one should make the fire very intense. Thus, in the phrase "three <s>puṭa</s> heatings by this method," the fire is to be understood.
Alternatively, one should understand the <s>lāṅgalī</s> method too according to the <s>kāñcanāra</s> method.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s> is <s>kalihārī</s>; or the <s>jvālāmukhī</s> method too should be understood just like the <s>kāñcanāra</s> method.

children.text: jvālāmukhī jayantī sā caturvidhā bhavati śvetā raktā tathā pītā kṛṣṇā jvālāmukhī bhavet iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jvālāmukhī</s> is <s>jayantī</s>. It is of four kinds: white, red, yellow, and black; such is <s>jvālāmukhī</s>.

children.text: etajjāticatuṣṭayaṃ śvetā raktā raktādikusumaiḥ kṛtvā jānīyāt ||
children.translated_text: This set of four varieties should be known by their white, red, and other flowers.
On "<s>śilā</s>":

children.text: śilā manaḥśilā sindūraḥ prasiddhaḥ samayoḥ samānamānayoḥ bhāvanāparimāṇaṃ ca yāvad dravyaṃ plutaṃ bhavati gālite pradrāvite hemni suvarṇe kalko'yamiti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śilā</s> means <s>manaḥśilā</s>; <s>sindūra</s> is well known. "Of equal" means of equal measure. The quantity for levigation is until the substance is soaked. When the gold, that is, the gold metal, has been melted and liquefied, this paste is to be used.
This paste is produced from <s>śilā</s> and <s>sindūra</s>.
By the word "paste," it is indicated that a thick one should be applied.
On "equal":

children.text: svarṇamānasamaḥ kalka evamityamunā prakāreṇa velātrayaṃ trivāramityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The paste is equal to the measure of the gold. "By this method" means three times, that is, on three occasions.
On "<s>pārāvata</s>":

children.text: pārāvataḥ prasiddhaḥ malaṃ purīṣaṃ limpet iti hemapatrāṇītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pārāvata</s> is well known; "mala" means excrement. "One should smear" refers to the gold leaves.

children.text: athavā kukkuṭodbhavairiti kukkuṭastāmracūḍaḥ tadudbhavairmalairiti sambandhaḥ teṣāṃ svarṇapatrāṇām antarāntarāntaraṃ yathā syāt tathā svarṇapatrasamaṃ gandhakacūrṇaṃ deyaṃ tāni ca śarāvayugmasaṃpuṭe dhṛtvā tatsaṃpuṭaṃ kukkuṭapuṭavidhānena pācyam pañcabhirgomayopalairiti pañcasaṃkhyākaiḥ śuṣkagomayaiḥ evamityanena prakāreṇa navasaṃkhyākāni puṭāni dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Alternatively, in the phrase "with what is produced from the cock," <s>kukkuṭa</s> means the copper-crested cock, and "with the wastes produced from it" is the connection. Sulphur powder equal to the gold leaves should be placed so that it lies between each of those gold leaves. Then, having placed them in a pair of earthen saucers used as a covered vessel, that closed vessel should be cooked according to the <s>kukkuṭa-puṭa</s> method. "With five cow-dung cakes" means with five dried cow-dung cakes. By this method, nine <s>puṭa</s> heatings should be given.

children.text: daśamaṃ ca mahāpuṭamiti mahāpuṭaṃ triṃśadvanopalaiḥ kṛtvā deyam ||
children.translated_text: "And the tenth as a <s>mahāpuṭa</s>": a <s>mahāpuṭa</s> should be given using thirty dried cow-dung cakes.
On "one part":

children.text: tālakaṃ haritālaṃ bhāgaikaṃ tārapatrabhāgādityarthaḥ jambena jambīrakarasena amlagrahaṇaṃ madhurajambīraniṣedhārthaṃ kenacidityanena kenāpyamlena vā kutaḥ jambīrābhāvāt tena cukrādikamapi grāhyam tena tālakena saha bhāgatrayamiti tārapatrāṇi raupyapatrāṇi pralepayet bhāgatrayaṃ tālakaparimāṇāt puṭavidhānaṃ pūrvavat triṃśadvanopalairityanena mahāpuṭaṃ darśitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tālaka</s> is <s>haritāla</s>; "one part" means one part in relation to a part of silver leaf. "With <s>jamba</s>" means with the juice of <s>jambīraka</s>. The mention of "sour" is for excluding sweet <s>jambīra</s>. By "with some [sour liquid]" it means with any sour liquid too, because <s>jambīra</s> may be absent; therefore <s>cukra</s> and the like may also be taken. With that <s>tālaka</s>, "three parts" means that one should smear the silver leaves with three parts in relation to the quantity of <s>tālaka</s>. The <s>puṭa</s> procedure is as before. By "with thirty dried cow-dung cakes," a <s>mahāpuṭa</s> is indicated.
Thus, by the stated <s>puṭa</s> procedure, fourteen <s>puṭa</s> heatings should be understood.
On "with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>":

children.text: pūrvoktaharitālavidhānavan mākṣikavidhānena kṛtvā caturdaśapuṭāni yāvad bhavanti tāvat tāraṃ raupyaṃ bhasma syāt ||
children.translated_text: Having done it by the <s>mākṣika</s> method, as in the previously stated <s>haritāla</s> procedure, until fourteen <s>puṭa</s> heatings have been completed, <s>tāra</s>, that is, silver, becomes <s>bhasma</s>.
<s>Mākṣika</s> means <s>dhātumākṣika</s>. In "with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>," <s>snuhī</s> is a variety of <s>sehuṇḍa</s>.
On "with the milk of <s>arka</s>":

children.text: āraṃ pītalohaṃ tacca tāmrasaṃbhavaṃ vadantyeke tena gandhakakalkena samenārasamānena śuddhānyamladravairmuhuriti pūrvam ārapatrāṇi amladravairjambīraprabhṛtikaiḥ muhuriti velātrayaṃ viśuddhāni kṛtvā paścādgandhakakalkena lepayedityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āra</s> is yellow metal; some say that it is produced from copper. The sulphur paste is equal to it, equal to the <s>āra</s>. The phrase "purified repeatedly with acid liquids" means that first the <s>āra</s> leaves are purified repeatedly, that is, three times, with acid liquids such as <s>jambīra</s>, and afterwards they should be smeared with the sulphur paste. This is the intention.

children.text: gajapuṭaṃ pūrvaṃ darśitameva evamityamunā prakāreṇa puṭadvayaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>gajapuṭa</s> has already been shown before. By this method two <s>puṭa</s> heatings should be performed.
On "like <s>āra</s>" and so forth:
<s>Kāṃsya</s> is well known.
By "like <s>āra</s>," it should be understood that both its purification and its calcination are just the same as for that.
By the word "thus," <s>ghoṣa</s> too should be known to be like <s>āra</s>.
In purification and calcination.
For so it is said:
One should smear the leaves of <s>kāṃsya</s>, <s>āra</s>, and <s>ghoṣa</s> with that paste.
Having sealed them and cooked them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, they certainly attain purification.

children.text: tāmravacca mṛtiṃ teṣāṃ kṛtvā sarvatra yojayet
children.translated_text: And, having made their <s>mṛti</s> (calcined state) as with copper, one should apply them everywhere.
So the quotation says.
<s>Ghoṣa</s> is a variety of <s>kāṃsya</s>; in common speech it is called <s>jasada</s>.
On "like <s>arka</s> milk" and so on:
As in the method with <s>arka</s> milk, the sulphur paste should be made with goat's milk.

children.text: tathānena prakāreṇa nirguṇḍīsvarasena gandhakakalkaṃ kāryamiti prayogāntaram ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, by this method, a sulphur paste should be made with the fresh juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>; this is another procedure.
For the killing, that is, calcination, of copper and the others,
the text says: "Copper, <s>āra</s>, <s>rīti</s>, <s>āra</s>, <s>dhvani</s>, and <s>kāṃsya</s> are treated by combination with equal sulphur."
The intention is that sulphur equal to the metal should be taken.
On "fine copper leaves":
Here fineness is what is called "pierceable by a thorn."

children.text: saṃsvedayedbudha iti amlena kāñjikādinā vāsaratrayaṃ dinatritayaṃ yāvaddolāyantreṇa svedanaṃ kuryāditi bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "The learned person should steam" means that with an acid such as <s>kāñjika</s>, for three days, that is, for a period of three days, one should perform steaming by means of a <s>dolāyantra</s>. This is the sense.
The omitted word is "of the leaves."
The inclusion of the word "properly" indicates the removal of copper's excessive defects.

children.text: yadyapi śuddhirasya pūrvaṃ kathitā tathāpi punaḥ śodhanamasya viṣanivṛttyarthaṃ kālimāpagamārthaṃ ca vihitam ||
children.translated_text: Although its purification was taught earlier, nevertheless a further purification of it is prescribed in order to remove toxicity and to remove blackness.
For:
They say that poison is not poison; copper itself is the great poison.
Poison has only one fault, but the fault of <s>śulba</s> (copper) is considered eightfold.

children.text: tadyathā viṣaṃ mūrchā vidāhaśca chardiḥ kledanabhedane
children.translated_text: Namely: toxicity, fainting, burning, vomiting, moistening, and purging,
as well as feverish heat and loss of appetite: the fault of copper is like poison.
Thus.
Even though it is free from blackness.
It has the appearance of a parrot's beak or a <s>kiṃśuka</s> flower; when cut it is red, and likewise soft and unctuous.
Copper that is blackish becomes, when purified, free from blackness.

children.text: ata evāmlena punaḥ śodhanamabhihitaṃ na doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that very reason purification again with an acid has been stated; there is no fault in this.
Here 'wise' means one who knows the distinctions of its class and so forth.
For that copper is of two kinds.
One is called <s>mleccha</s>, and the other <s>Nepāla</s>.
Accordingly:
Copper is <s>mleccha</s> and <s>Nepālaka</s>; of the two, <s>Nepāla</s> is best.
Copper produced in a country other than <s>Nepāla</s> is remembered as <s>mleccha</s>.
That which has white, black, and reddish hues and causes vomiting and purging,
and which becomes black again from washing, is called <s>mleccha</s> copper.
That which is very smooth, soft, red, capable of purification, and heavy,
the best, removing the three <s>doṣas</s>, and not undergoing alteration through alkalis and acids,
that is called <s>Nepālaka</s>, an agent for bodily and metallic preparations.
It removes vomiting, dizziness, and fever, and dispels moistness, purging, and giddiness.
Thus.
'Then' means afterwards.
'A quarter-part of <s>sūtaka</s>' means this:

children.text: sūtakaṃ pāradaṃ pādāṃśaṃ tāmramānacaturthāṃśaṃ yāmaṃ praharamekaṃ yāvad amlena jambīranimbukaprabhṛtirasena mardayet iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that <s>sūtaka</s>, that is mercury, in a quarter-part, namely a quarter of the measure of the copper, should be triturated with an acid, with the juice of <s>jambīra</s> lemon, <s>nimbūka</s>, and the like, for one <s>yāma</s>, one <s>prahara</s>.

children.text: punastenaivāmlena ghṛṣṭena dviguṇagandhakena kṛtvā lepayet patrāṇīti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, with that very acid ground together with double sulphur, one should coat the sheets; this is to be supplied.
The doubling is with respect to the quantity of mercury.

children.text: na tu tāmramānāt asmatsampradāye tu gandhakaṃ bahutaraṃ yojyaṃ tena tāmramānāddviguṇamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is not with respect to the measure of the copper; but in our tradition more sulphur is to be added, and therefore the meaning is that it is double the measure of the copper.
Elsewhere also it is stated:
One should coat the sheet together with mercury equal to a quarter of the copper,
and again with sulphur twice the copper, ground with acid.
Having coated it, one should place above and below the sour leaf-paste, well ground.

children.text: tat piṇḍaṃ bhāṇḍagarbhe tu ruddhvā cullyāṃ vipācayet
children.translated_text: Having sealed that lump inside a vessel, one should cook it on the hearth.
And so on.

children.text: tasya kuryācca golakamiti tasya tāmramayadravyasya mīnākṣī machechī śabdavācyā ||
children.translated_text: In the expression 'he should make a ball of it,' 'of it' refers to that copper-containing substance; <s>mīnākṣī</s>, denoted by the word <s>machechī</s>, is meant.

children.text: cāṅgerī amlapatrikā prasiddhā tatkalkeneti trayāṇāṃ dravyāṇāṃ vyastānāṃ militānāṃ vā kalkaṃ vadanti tajjñāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṅgerī</s> is the well-known sour leaf; by 'its paste,' experts mean a paste of the three substances, either separately or combined.

children.text: aṅgulonmitam iti aṅgulotsedhaṃ trayāṇāmekasya vā aṅgulamatra madhyamāṅgulimadhyaparvasaṃjñam ||
children.translated_text: 'Measuring a finger' means having the height of a finger; it may be the measure of the three together or of one alone, the finger being the middle joint of the middle finger.

children.text: rodhayedityanena vibhūtilavaṇāmbubhiḥ kṛtvā śarāvasandhau mudrāṃ kārayediti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By 'one should seal,' the meaning is that, using ash, salt, and water, one should make a seal at the joint of the two earthen saucers.
And one should make one at the mouth of the vessel.
The ash is cow-dung ash; the salt here is earthy salt.

children.text: ambu pānīyaṃ kramavṛddhāgnineti mṛdumadhyakharāgninā śeṣaṃ subodham ||
children.translated_text: Water is drinking water. 'With gradually increased fire' means with mild, medium, and intense fire; the rest is easy to understand.

children.text: atha ca māritasyāsya śuddhyarthaṃ vidhimapyāha svāṃgaśītalamuddhṛtyetyādi tattāmraṃ svāṅgaśītalaṃ saṃgṛhya paścāt sūraṇadravaiḥ kṛtvā dinamekaṃ saṃmardya paścādgolakaṃ kṛtvā saghṛtenārdhagandhakakalkena golakaṃ lepayitvā tadanu mūṣāntardhṛtvā nirodhya ca gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: Now, for the purification of this after it has been calcined, he also states the procedure beginning 'having taken it out when cooled by itself': one should collect that copper when it has cooled by itself, then triturate it for one day with the juices of <s>sūraṇa</s>, afterwards make a ball, coat the ball with a paste of half sulphur together with ghee, then place it inside a crucible, seal it, and cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: anena tat kṣaṇena bhakṣaṇayogyaṃ bhavati ardhagandhakaṃ tāmraparimāṇāt ||
children.translated_text: By this it immediately becomes fit for consumption. 'Half sulphur' is with respect to the measure of the copper.
Thus the meaning is that the copper is two parts and the sulphur one part.
The ghee too is equal to the sulphur.
'<s>Tāmbūlī</s>' means this:
<s>Tāmbūlī</s> is the well-known betel creeper.
<s>Nāga</s> is lead.
<s>Śilā</s> is <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar), and according to the tradition it is one quarter.
'Again and again' means this:
At each <s>puṭa</s> one should smear it with <s>manaḥśilā</s> and subject it to the <s>puṭa</s>.
In this way thirty-two <s>puṭas</s> are recognized.
But this does not mean smearing again and again within each separate <s>puṭa</s>.
Rather, the meaning is that the smearing is once for each <s>puṭa</s>.
'Powder of the bark of <s>aśvattha</s> and <s>ciñcā</s>' means this:

children.text: aśvatthaḥ pippalaḥ ciñcā amlikā caturthāṃśaṃ bhasmataḥ sīsakaparimāṇāt etena vāraṃvāraṃ bhasmanaḥ kṣepaṇam uktam natu ekavāraṃ yato vakṣyamāṇavaṅgamāraṇe proktaṃ kṣiptvā iti tadvadatrāpi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvattha</s> is <s>pippala</s>; <s>ciñcā</s> is tamarind. The quarter-part, with respect to the ash, is according to the measure of the lead. By this, repeated addition of the ash is taught, not a single addition, because in the forthcoming calcination of tin the expression 'having thrown in' is used; here too it is the same.

children.text: tena yāvannāgasya bhasma bhavati tāvatkṣāraṃ deyaṃ paścānnāgabhasmanaḥ śilāṃ ca kāñjikena samaṃ piṣṭvā saha dṛḍhapuṭe gajapuṭasaṃjñake pacet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, until the lead becomes ash, alkali should be applied. Afterwards the lead-ash and <s>śilā</s>, ground together equally with <s>kāñjika</s>, should be cooked together in a firm <s>puṭa</s> called a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
Thus, by means of sixty <s>puṭas</s>, calcination occurs.

children.text: ṣaṣṭipuṭānyatra śilayaiva saha kāryāṇi natu ciñcāśvatthayor bhasmanā bhasmasaṃskāras tvekadaiva ||
children.translated_text: Here the sixty <s>puṭas</s> should be performed together with <s>śilā</s> alone, not with the ash of <s>ciñcā</s> and <s>aśvattha</s>; the treatment with ash is only once.
'In an earthen vessel' means this:

children.text: mṛtpātraṃ kharparaṃ ciñcā amlikā aśvatthaḥ pippalaḥ rajaścūrṇamanayorvalkalasya kṣiptvā kṣiptvā iti vāraṃvāraṃ caturthāṃśamiti vaṅgaparimāṇāt valkalacūrṇasya etat parimāṇamekavāraṃ kṣepaṇārtham atastāvat kṣipedyāvadbhasma bhavati tena vaṅgaparimāṇasamaṃ valkalarajaḥ kāryamiti sampradāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A clay vessel is a potsherd. Ciñcā is amlikā, and aśvattha is pippala. The word rajas means the powdered bark of these two. 'Having added again and again' means repeatedly. 'One fourth' means that this is the measure of bark-powder, relative to the quantity of <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), for a single addition. Therefore one should add that much until it becomes ash; thus, according to tradition, bark-powder equal to the quantity of <s>vaṅga</s> should be prepared.

children.text: ayodarvyā lohamayadaṇḍena atheti paścāt kāryakarmāha bhasmasamam ityādi ||
children.translated_text: With an iron ladle, that is, with an iron rod. Then, with the word 'now,' he states the subsequent operation to be done, beginning with 'equal to the ash'.

children.text: tālaṃ haritālaṃ tadvaṅgabhasma sāmyaṃ bhavati tena kimuktaṃ vaṅgabhasma haritālaṃ ca samamātraṃ saṃgṛhya amlena kāñjikādinā vimardya tadgolakākāraṃ kṛtvā śarāvasampuṭe dhāryaṃ saṃpuṭanirodhaṃ ca kṛtvā gajapuṭe pacet tatpaścāt tamuddhṛtya punardaśamāṃśena tālakena saha saṃmardyāmlarasaiḥ kṛtvā tataḥ puṭet ||
children.translated_text: Tāla means haritāla; it is equal in amount to that <s>vaṅga</s> ash. What is said by this? One should take <s>vaṅga</s> ash and haritāla in equal quantities, triturate them with an acid such as kāñjika, make that into the shape of a ball, place it in a covered pair of earthen saucers, seal the enclosure, and cook it in a gajapuṭa. After that, one should take it out, again triturate it with tālaka in one-tenth quantity and with acidic juices, and then subject it to a puṭa.
'Ten' is to be supplied: thus, in accordance with the procedure of enclosing in the sealed vessel.

children.text: agnipuṭaṃ tu kiṃcin nyūnam iti sampradāyaḥ evaṃ daśapuṭaiḥ kṛtvā vaṅgo mṛto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: According to tradition, the fire-puṭa should be somewhat less. When it has thus been treated with ten puṭas, <s>vaṅga</s> becomes killed, that is, calcined.
The word is 'purified'.

children.text: śuddhaṃ śodhitaṃ jātyutkṛṣṭaṃ vā śodhanamasya pūrvaṃ kathitameva ||
children.translated_text: 'Purified' means refined, or else excellent in kind. Its purification has already been stated earlier.
The differences of some varieties are written down for the sake of instruction, as follows:
When the great ocean was being churned by the assembly of the gods,
there arose in it, long ago, the amṛta, the life of the gods.
As that was being drunk by the gods, tiny drops sprang up from it.

children.text: jñātvā tān bhūgatān bindūn yogamāsādya dhūrjaṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing that those drops had gone to the earth, <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>, resorting to yogic power,
made them, on the surface of the earth, into the form of metallic stones,
so that those human beings who are overcome by sin and disease might resort to them.

children.text: ityevaṃ śivaguptā ye sudhāyā bindavaḥ param
children.translated_text: Thus those drops of nectar, supremely hidden by <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: teṣāṃ mayā samāsena kathyate sādhanaṃ sphuṭam ||
children.translated_text: their clear preparation is now briefly explained by me.
Thus.

children.text: atha jātibhedā yathā yadyapi nāgārjunamate aṣṭādaśa lohajātayaḥ santi tadyathā māṇḍūraṃ māṇḍūkaṃ sāraṃ lohaṃ madhyasāralohaṃ sthūlasāralohaṃ cakramardalohaṃ bandhalohaṃ vajrakalohaṃ surāyasaṃ kaliṅgaṃ bhadralohaṃ garalasthitalohaṃ vajraṃ pāṇḍiniravam arbudakam kāntaṃ kuliśamiti tathāpyanyeṣāṃ mate tvaṣṭaiva śreṣṭhatamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now the varieties are as follows. Although, in the opinion of <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, there are eighteen kinds of iron, namely māṇḍūra, māṇḍūka, sāraloha, madhyasāraloha, sthūlasāraloha, cakramardaloha, bandhaloha, vajrakaloha, surāyasa, kaliṅga, bhadraloha, garalasthitaloha, vajra, pāṇḍinirava, arbudaka, kānta, and kuliśa, still, in the opinion of others, only eight are the very best.

children.text: tathā hi sāmānyāddviguṇaṃ sāraṃ tasmād aṣṭaguṇaṃ kaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus: sāra is twice as good as ordinary iron, and kali is eight times as good as that.
Bhadra is a hundred times as good as kali, and vajra is a thousand times as good as bhadra.
Pāṇḍinirava is sixty times as good as vajra, and by ten further degrees beyond that,

children.text: tataḥ koṭiguṇaṃ tasmādayasaḥ kāntakaṃ matam iti ||
children.translated_text: then beyond that, kāntaka iron is regarded as ten million times as good.

children.text: eteṣāṃ vyañjanaṃ ca tantrāntarādeva likhyate lakṣaṇaviśeṣaṃ vinā śreṣṭhamaśreṣṭhaṃ na jñāyate tasmāllikhyate ||
children.translated_text: The distinguishing marks of these are written from another tantra itself. Without specific marks, the superior and the inferior cannot be known; therefore they are set down.
As follows:
When it is treated with acid, there are signs shaped like earth, clay, and peaks,

children.text: dṛśyante yatra sūkṣmāṇi sāraṃ ca tadudāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and where these are seen in minute form, that is declared to be sāra.
Where, in black iron, there are twenty white marks,
small and shaped like sprouts, the learned call that kṛṣṇavajraka.
Where the ground is very black and all the features are round,

children.text: rekhā syāddhemavarṇā ca tatpiṇḍī ca vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: and there is a line of golden color, that is designated piṇḍī.
Kali has a swift, even whorl, as the discerning have said;
when a little of it is placed in water, a drop of oil does not spread there.

children.text: api kenāpi kālena nirmalatvaṃ na muñcati
children.translated_text: Even after any length of time, it does not lose its purity,

children.text: bhraśyate yanna kālena nirdravaṃ tadayo matam ||
children.translated_text: and what does not deteriorate with time and is without fluidity is considered iron.
That mountain-essence by which other mountain-essences are split like dry wood
is called sharp kānta.
The mark of kānta has also been stated elsewhere.

children.text: pātre yasmin praviśati jale tailabindurniṣikto hiṅgurgandhaṃ visṛjati nijaṃ tiktatāṃ nimbakalkaḥ
children.translated_text: In a vessel of which, when water is present, a drop of oil poured in enters the water; asafoetida releases its own smell, and neem paste its bitterness;

children.text: pāke dugdhaṃ bhavati śikharākārakaṃ naiti bhūmau kāntaṃ lohaṃ bhavati tadidaṃ lakṣaṇoktaṃ nacānyat ||
children.translated_text: when cooked, milk becomes peak-shaped and does not go down to the ground: that is kānta iron, according to this stated mark, and not anything else.

children.text: iti tasmādeteṣāṃ madhye kāntalohaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ yataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, among these, kāntaloha is the best, because:
Muṇḍa is ten times as good as kiṭṭa, and tīkṣṇa is reckoned a hundred times as good as muṇḍa.
Kānta is a hundred thousand times as good as tīkṣṇa; when eaten, it produces benefit.

children.text: tasmāt kāntaṃ sadā sevyaṃ jarāmṛtyuharaṃ nṝṇām
children.translated_text: Therefore kānta should always be used, for it removes old age and death from human beings.
Thus.
And that kānta is of four kinds.
Namely:

children.text: bhrāmakaṃ śakaṭaṃ caiva cumbakaṃ drāvakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: bhrāmaka, śakaṭa, cumbaka, and likewise drāvaka;
kānta is fourfold, and each one is regarded as twice as good as the preceding one.
Thus.
The differences of varieties have been stated briefly.

children.text: samprati māraṇavidhirapi teṣāṃ kathyate lohabhavaṃ cūrṇamityādi
children.translated_text: Now their method of incineration too is explained, beginning with 'powder produced from iron'.

children.text: pātālagaruḍī pātālamūlī prasiddhā sā ca chinnaruhākṛtistadbhedaśca tadabhāve chirahaṇṭaiva grāhyā puṭamatra gajapuṭam ||
children.translated_text: Pātālagaruḍī is the well-known pātālamūlī. It has the form of chinnaruhā and is a variety of it. In its absence, chirahaṇṭā itself should be taken. The puṭa here is a gajapuṭa.
Kumārī is well known. The phrase is 'with the juices of kuṭhāra and kulattha'.

children.text: kuṭhāraḥ kuṭhāracchinnā kuṭajabheda ityanye tadabhāve jambūtvak gṛhṇantyapare asmatsampradāye kuṭhāracchinnā loke tipānītiśabdavācyo dravyaviśeṣo grāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As for kuṭhāra, some say it is kuṭhāracchinnā, a variety of kuṭaja. In its absence others take the bark of jambū. In our tradition, kuṭhāracchinnā, a particular substance known in common speech by the word tipānīti, should be taken.
Kulattha is a well-known kind of grain.
By the expression 'a group of six <s>puṭas</s>,' three <s>puṭas</s> for each are to be understood as before.
'One should add it.'
<s>Darada</s> is <s>hiṅgula</s>.
The <s>darada</s> is one tenth of the measure of the iron powder.
<s>Kanyakā</s> means <s>kumārī</s>.
Here the <s>puṭa</s> is the procedure of the <s>gajapuṭa</s>; 'two <s>yāmas</s>' is the measure of grinding.
By 'in this way,' it becomes perfected after being treated with seven <s>puṭas</s>.

children.text: athavā kuṭhāracchinnāyā rasaiḥ kṛtvā daradaṃ lohacūrṇaṃ ca pūrvavat saṃmardya puṭet ||
children.translated_text: Alternatively, using the juices of <s>kuṭhāracchinnā</s>, one should triturate <s>darada</s> and iron powder as before and subject them to a <s>puṭa</s>.
By this method also, with seven <s>puṭas</s>, this becomes perfected.

children.text: athavā pātālagaruḍīrasaistadvad eva vā athavā stanyena pūrvavadyogaḥ kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or the procedure should be done in just the same way with the juices of <s>pātālagaruḍī</s>; or it should be done as before with breast milk.
With the latex of <s>arka</s>, the procedure is just the same.
This set of four procedures pertains to <s>darada</s>.
Or it should be understood as pertaining to the seven <s>puṭas</s>.

children.text: atra kuṭhāracchinnā prasiddhā tipānīśabdavācyetyapare pātālagaruḍī chirahaṇṭaḥ stanyaṃ strībhavaṃ nānyat prayogāntaradarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: Here <s>kuṭhāracchinnā</s> is well known; others say it is denoted by the word <s>tipānī</s>. <s>Pātālagaruḍī</s> is <s>chirahaṇṭa</s>. Breast milk is that produced by a woman, not anything else, since another application shows this.

children.text: tathā ca hiṅgulasya palān pañca nārīstanyena peṣayet
children.translated_text: And accordingly: one should grind five <s>palas</s> of <s>hiṅgula</s> with a woman's breast milk,
and with that one should coat iron sheets amounting to five <s>palas</s>,
and so on.
Now, the phrase beginning with '<s>sūtaka</s>'.

children.text: sūtaṃ pāradaṃ gandhaṃ gandhakaṃ dvayor iti pāradagandhakayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> means mercury, and <s>gandha</s> means sulfur; 'of the two' means of mercury and sulfur.

children.text: kanyakā kumārī yāmārdhenoṣṇatā bhūyādityanena taddravyapiṇḍaṃ ghaṭikācatuṣṭayaṃ yāvadgharme dhārayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kanyakā</s> is <s>kumārī</s>. By the statement 'there should be heat for half a <s>yāma</s>,' the meaning is that the lump of those substances should be kept in the heat for four <s>ghaṭikās</s>.
'Then' means afterwards.
By the statement 'having placed a saucer above,' the meaning is that first the lump of those substances

children.text: eraṇḍapatrairveṣṭayitvā paścāttāmrasaṃpuṭe mṛṇmayasaṃpuṭe vā saṃnidhāya tadanu dhānyarāśau sthāpayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be wrapped in castor leaves, then placed in a copper capsule or an earthen capsule, and after that set in a heap of grain.
For thus it is said:

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ dvidhā gandhaṃ kṛtvā khalvena kajjalīm
children.translated_text: Having made purified mercury and twice as much sulfur into <s>kajjalī</s> in a mortar,
one should grind iron powder equal to the two with the juices of <s>kanyakā</s>.
After two <s>yāmas</s>, one should lift that ball into a copper vessel,
and, covering it with castor leaves, there should be heat for half a <s>yāma</s>,
and so on.

children.text: evamiti pūrvoktavidhinā sarvāṇi lohāni kāntatīkṣṇamuṇḍaprabhṛtīni svarṇādīni api anayā yuktyā ca mārayediti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By 'in this way,' the intention is that by the previously stated method all metals, such as <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍa</s>, and also those beginning with gold, should be incinerated by this procedure.
Because the word 'and so on' is used, silver, copper, and the others are included.
The further statement beginning 'smeared with <s>śilā</s>, <s>gandha</s>, and <s>arka</s> latex' is easy to understand.
By the word 'truly,' the meaning is that it should become <s>vāritara</s>, able to float on water.
Here it should be understood according to the teacher's instruction.

children.text: etena kimuktaṃ mṛtaṃ lohaṃ tu paścāt saṃskāritaṃ kuryādityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is stated by this? The intention is that the incinerated metal should afterwards be further processed.
For thus it is said:
One should cook the incinerated metal, together with an equal amount of ghee, in an iron vessel.
When the ghee has been assimilated, one should take it and employ it among the <s>yogavāhas</s>.
And so on.
Now, '<s>mākṣika</s>'.
<s>Mākṣika</s> means <s>dhātumākṣika</s>.

children.text: tad dvividham ekaṃ svarṇamākṣikam aparaṃ tāramākṣikaṃ kāṃsyamākṣikamiti ||
children.translated_text: It is twofold: one is <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>, and the other is <s>tāramākṣika</s>, called <s>kāṃsyamākṣika</s>.
<s>Tutthaka</s> is well known.

children.text: abhram abhrakaṃ nīlāñjanaṃ prasiddham śilā manaḥśilā tālakaṃ haritālaṃ rasakaṃ kharparakaḥ sa ca tutthakabhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Abhra</s> means <s>abhraka</s>; <s>nīlāñjana</s> is well known; <s>śilā</s> is <s>manaḥśilā</s>; <s>tālaka</s> is <s>haritāla</s>; <s>rasaka</s> is <s>kharparaka</s>, and that is a variety of <s>tutthaka</s>.
These are said to be the seven <s>upadhātus</s>.
Now he states the purification and incineration of each individually, beginning with 'atha'.
The phrase 'of <s>mākṣika</s>' is clear.
Now, '<s>karkoṭī</s>'.

children.text: vimalā svarṇamākṣikabhedaḥ karkoṭī vandhyākarkoṭī grāhyā meṣaśṛṅgī vallīsaṃjñā prasiddhā etayordravaiḥ sadyorasaiḥ patrāṇāmiti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vimalā</s> is a variety of <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>. As <s>karkoṭī</s>, barren <s>karkoṭī</s> is to be taken. <s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, known by the name <s>vallī</s>, is well known. With the fluids of these two, that is, with fresh juices, 'of the sheets' is to be supplied.

children.text: jambīrajairiti jambīraphalarasaiḥ dinamiti mardayet iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Produced from <s>jambīra</s>' means with the juices of <s>jambīra</s> fruits; at 'for a day,' the words 'one should grind' are to be supplied.

children.text: tena pratyekarasena kṛtvā dinaikaṃ mardayed ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the meaning is that one should grind for one day with each juice separately.
'In intense sun' means in strong heat.
When strong sunlight is absent, the tradition also says that one should purify it over fire.
And it has been said:
Cooked with the juices of <s>jambīras</s>, or with the juice of <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>,
or cooked with the water of <s>rambhā</s> for a day: this is the purification of <s>vimalā</s>.
Thus.
'One should grind with <s>viṣṭhā</s>': <s>viṣṭhā</s> means excrement.

children.text: mārjārakakapotayoriti mārjārako biḍālaḥ kapotaḥ prasiddhaḥ anayoḥ purīṣaṃ tvanumānato grāhyam ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyakṣāraṃ daśāṃśamiti tutthakaparimāṇāt ||
children.translated_text: In the phrase 'of the <s>mārjāraka</s> and the <s>kapota</s>,' <s>mārjāraka</s> is a cat, and <s>kapota</s> is well known. The excrement of these two should be taken according to estimation. <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgyakṣāra</s>; 'one tenth' means in relation to the measure of <s>tutthaka</s>.

children.text: mṛdupuṭaṃ tu kukkuṭapuṭaprabhṛtikaṃ paścād dadhnā kṛtvā puṭamekaṃ deyam ||
children.translated_text: A mild <s>puṭa</s> means a <s>kukkuṭapuṭa</s> and similar heatings. Afterwards, after preparing it with curd, one <s>puṭa</s> should be given.
After that, one should also give one <s>puṭa</s> with honey; this is the meaning.
Now he states the purification of <s>abhraka</s>, beginning with '<s>kṛṣṇa</s>'.
Black <s>abhraka</s> is said to have the designation <s>vajrajāti</s>.
For <s>abhraka</s> is of four kinds.

children.text: tathā hi tantrāntarād utpattiprabhṛtikaṃ likhyate yathā
children.translated_text: Thus, from another tantra, its origin and the like are written as follows:
Long ago, for the killing of <s>Vṛtra</s>, <s>Vajrin</s> raised his thunderbolt.
Then sparks from it moved through the sky.
With a thunderous cloud-like roar, they fell upon the peaks of the mountains.
From those very sparks, <s>abhraka</s> arose on those various mountains.
Therefore it is called <s>vajra</s> because it is born from the thunderbolt, and <s>abhra</s> because it arose from cloud-roar.
Because it was born from what had fallen from the sky, the gods called it <s>gagana</s>.
It is fourfold through the divisions of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, and <s>śūdra</s>,

children.text: krameṇaiva sitaṃ raktaṃ pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca varṇataḥ ||
children.translated_text: being, in order, white, red, yellow, and black in color.

children.text: pinākaṃ darduraṃ nāgaṃ vajraṃ ceti caturvidham ||
children.translated_text: It is fourfold: <s>pināka</s>, <s>dardura</s>, <s>nāga</s>, and <s>vajra</s>.
The three beginning with <s>pināka</s> are to be rejected; one should collect the <s>vajra</s> variety.
When <s>pināka</s> is thrown into fire, it releases a mass of flakes.
When <s>dardura</s> is placed in fire, it makes a frog-like sound.

children.text: nāgaṃ cāgnau vinikṣiptaṃ phūtkāraṃ ca vimuñcati
children.translated_text: And when <s>nāga</s> is thrown into fire, it emits a hissing sound.

children.text: vajrābhrakaṃ tu vahnisthaṃ na kvacidvikṛtiṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: But <s>vajrābhraka</s>, while in fire, does not undergo any alteration anywhere.
Therefore <s>vajrābhraka</s> should be used; it conquers disease, old age, and death.
Among these, that from the southern mountain is indeed of lesser quality because of the remaining effect of the sun.

children.text: alpasattvaṃ tadā dhatte abhre sattvaṃ guṇapradam
children.translated_text: Then it holds little essence; in abhraka, essence is what gives qualities.
But what is produced from the northern mountain has much essence and superior qualities.

children.text: śaṃsanti munayaḥ sarve prayoge kṛṣṇam abhrakam
children.translated_text: All the sages praise black abhraka for practical use.
Thus.
And he states the purification with the words "in <s>taṇḍulīya</s> and sour liquid."

children.text: taṇḍulīyo meghanādaḥ amlaḥ kāñjikaṃ tadabhāve jambīraprabhṛtikaṃ grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Taṇḍulīya</s> is <s>meghanāda</s>; the sour liquid is <s>kāñjika</s>. If that is absent, <s>jambīra</s> and the like should be taken.
"For eight yāmas in the two substances" means four yāmas in each separately.
Now the incineration, with the words "having made <s>dhānyābhraka</s>," and so on.
The procedure for <s>dhānyābhraka</s> should be understood from another tantra.
It is as follows:
After tying it in a cloth together with grain, one should grind it with <s>kāñjika</s>.
Taking what has gone down below, the purified, bright material becomes <s>dhānyābhraka</s>.
Thus.
That which has passed through a blanket and is fine is commended for incineration and the like.
Thus.
Alternatively,
powdered abhraka, mixed with rice, should likewise be tied in a small blanket.

children.text: trirātraṃ kāṃjike sthāpyaṃ tat klinnaṃ mardayeddṛḍham ||
children.translated_text: It should be kept in <s>kāñjika</s> for three nights; when soaked, one should grind it firmly.

children.text: veṣṭayed arkapatraiścetyanena cakrākāraṃ dravyaṃ patrair veṣṭayitvāgnau puṭet ||
children.translated_text: By the phrase "one should wrap it in arka leaves," the meaning is that, after wrapping the disk-shaped substance in leaves, one should heat it in fire with a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: samyagiti grahaṇena tat patraveṣṭitaṃ cakrākāraṃ dravyaṃ kharpare nidhāya upari ca kharparaṃ dattvā tadūrdhvādhaḥ āraṇyakopalāni ca dattvāgniṃ prajvālya gajapuṭe puṭediti tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the inclusion of "properly," the intended meaning is this: placing that leaf-wrapped, disk-shaped substance in an earthen saucer, putting another earthen saucer on top, placing forest cow-dung cakes above and below it, kindling the fire, one should subject it to <s>gajapuṭa</s> heating.
In this way one should heat it as many as seven times.
The meaning is: with arka latex alone.
After that, having treated it with decoctions of banyan aerial roots, exactly three <s>puṭas</s> should be given.
Now he states the purification even of incinerated abhraka, beginning with "equal" and so on; it is easy to understand.
Now he also states the property of incinerated abhraka, with the word "incinerated."
Some do not read this verse, because it is not current in many places.
"Purified <s>dhānyābhraka</s>."
The purification was stated earlier.
The procedure for <s>dhānyābhraka</s> has already been shown above.
<s>Musta</s> and dried ginger are each added in a sixth part.
Here the status of being a sixth part is relative to the measure of abhraka.
And the grinding with <s>kāñjika</s> is for one day; that is the meaning.
"With <s>triphalā</s> water" means with a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>.
"One should heat it likewise" means by the <s>gajapuṭa</s> procedure.

children.text: evaṃ puṭais tribhiriti triphalākvāthena puṭatrayaṃ dadyād ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Thus with three <s>puṭas</s>" means that one should give three <s>puṭas</s> with <s>triphalā</s> decoction.

children.text: evamiti gajapuṭavidhānādinā balāprabhṛtīnāṃ pañcadravyāṇāṃ dravaiḥ kṛtvā pratyekena trivelaṃ marditaṃ pañcād vahnau puṭitaṃ cābhrakaṃ mṛtiṃ vrajed ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By "thus," with the <s>gajapuṭa</s> procedure and so on, the meaning is that abhraka, treated with the liquids of the five substances beginning with <s>balā</s>, ground three times with each separately, and afterwards heated in fire, reaches incineration.

children.text: eke cātra yogatrayaṃ manyante tanmate tu mustaprabhṛticitrakāntair eko yogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some consider there to be three formulas here; in their view, one formula consists of <s>musta</s> and the others ending with <s>citraka</s>.
The second consists of <s>triphalā</s> alone.
The third consists of <s>balā</s> and the others ending with <s>sūraṇa</s>.
Now he states the method for purifying <s>nīlāñjana</s>, with the word "nīlāñjana."
<s>Nīlāñjana</s> is well known.
Its variety is <s>sauvīrāñjana</s>, because of the distinction between white and black color.
Lead is also produced from this.
"Treated with <s>jambīra</s> liquid" means treated with the juice of the <s>jambīra</s> fruit; the rest is easy to understand.
"Thus," and so on.
In this same way, by the method for purifying <s>nīlāñjana</s>, <s>gairika</s> and the others should be purified.
<s>Gairika</s> is well known.
There are <s>gairika</s> and <s>svarṇagairika</s>.
"<s>Kāsīsa</s>."
And that is twofold.
<s>Kāsīsa</s> and <s>puṣpakāsīsa</s>.

children.text: kāsīsaṃ bhasmavadalpamṛt puṣpakāsīsaṃ tadbhedaḥ kiṃcit pītaḥ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyakṣāraḥ varāṭikā kapardikā śeṣaṃ prasiddham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāsīsa</s> is like ash and has little earth; <s>puṣpakāsīsa</s> is a variety of it, slightly yellow. <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgyakṣāra</s>; <s>varāṭikā</s> is <s>kapardikā</s>; the rest is well known.
The words <s>taurī</s>, <s>sphaṭikā</s>, and <s>phiṭkārī</s> denote a type of earth or mineral.

children.text: kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ suvarṇakṣīrī asya bhedaḥ coka iti prasiddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is <s>suvarṇakṣīrī</s>; its variety is well known as <s>coka</s>.
And it is recognized as the red-latex <s>sehuṇḍa</s>.
By the word "certainly," even another purification should not be expected.

children.text: yatastantrāntareṣvapi nānāprakāreṇa śodhanamasti tasmādanenaivātra śodhanameteṣāṃ pratipāditam ||
children.translated_text: For although in other tantras there are purifications in many forms, here the purification of these is taught by this method alone.
Now he states the purification of <s>manaḥśilā</s>, beginning with "one should cook."
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is well known.
And the procedure for the <s>dolāyantra</s> is written according to the tradition.

children.text: manaḥśilāṃ kaṇaśaḥ kṛtvā kadalīdalaiḥ saṃveṣṭya tadanu caturguṇena vastreṇa ca poṭṭalīṃ baddhvā mūtrapūrite bhāṇḍe vidhivat svedayet yāvaddinatrayaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: After breaking <s>manaḥśilā</s> into particles, wrapping it in banana leaves, and then tying it into a bundle with fourfold cloth, one should steam it properly in a vessel filled with urine until three days have passed.
By the mention of days, the night too is included.

children.text: tenāhorātramapi svedayet ityabhiprāyaḥ eke tu dinatrayameva na tu rātrau svedanaṃ vihitam yato rātrāvadṛḍhatve dagdhādibhayāt tathā hi
children.translated_text: By that, the intended meaning is that one should sweat it even for a day and night. But some hold that sweating for just three days is prescribed, not sweating at night, because at night, if it is not firm, there is danger of burning and the like. Accordingly:
On a very firm plantain leaf and on a piece of cloth folded four times,
having placed them in the middle of that, one should tie up a good bundle.
One should sweat it for three days with the group of alkaline, sour, and urinary liquids.

children.text: tathā svedaḥ prakartavyo majjayet poṭalī yathā ||
children.translated_text: The sweating should be performed in such a way that the bundle is immersed,
and that it never at any time touches even the bottom of the vessel.
So they think.
Then also comes the definition of the <s>dolāyantra</s>.
In a vessel half filled with a liquid substance,

children.text: mukhe tiryak kṛte daṇḍe yaddravyaṃ sūtralambitam
children.translated_text: when a rod is placed crosswise over its mouth, the substance suspended by a cord
is sweated while situated in the middle of it; this is remembered as the <s>dolāyantra</s>.
Thus.
The phrase is, 'One should levigate it seven times with biles.'

children.text: tadanu sveditā manaḥśilā ajāyāḥ pittadravaiḥ kṛtvā saptadhā gharme bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: After that, the sweated <s>manaḥśilā</s> should be levigated seven times in the sun with liquid biles of a goat.

children.text: bhāvanārthadravastu yāvad dravyaṃ drāvitaṃ bhavati evaṃ śuddhimṛcchatīti ||
children.translated_text: The liquid used for levigation is only so much as makes the substance liquefied; in this way it attains purification.
Some
read, 'One should wash it in <s>āranāla</s>, or apply it in all preparations,'
and they explain it in that way.
Now, setting forth the purification of <s>tālaka</s>, he says, '<s>tālakam</s>'.

children.text: tālakaṃ haritālaṃ sacūrṇakāñjike kṣipediti cūrṇaṃ kaṇikābhāvamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tālaka</s> is <s>haritāla</s>; 'one should place it in powdered <s>kāñjika</s>' means that the powder is in the state of small particles.

children.text: kathaṃ yathā īṣaccūrṇayuktaṃ kāñjikaṃ bhāṇḍe kṣiptvā dolāyantravidhānena svedayet ||
children.translated_text: How? Having put <s>kāñjika</s> slightly mixed with powder into a vessel, one should sweat it according to the procedure of the <s>dolāyantra</s>.
The procedure of the <s>dolāyantra</s> has already been shown earlier.
By the word 'then', sweating for one <s>yāma</s> is indicated.
'With liquids from <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>' means with fresh juices or decoctions of the <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s> fruit.
The phrase is, 'with <s>triphalā</s>-water.'
That is, with water decocted with <s>triphalā</s>, with water in which <s>triphalā</s> has been boiled.
The rest is easy to understand.
Now he explains the purification of <s>rasaka</s>, beginning with 'with human urines'.
<s>Rasaka</s> is <s>kharparaka</s>, and that is a variety of <s>tuttha</s>.

children.text: naramūtrairgomūtraiśca pṛthak pacet na tu militamūtradvayaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be cooked separately with human urine and with cow urine, not with the two urines mixed together.

children.text: naramūtraṃ saptāhaṃ yāvat cet dolāyantreṇa athavā gomūtraiḥ
children.translated_text: With human urine, if by means of a <s>dolāyantra</s>, this is for up to seven days; or else with cow urine,
'<s>Rasaka</s>, sweated for seven days with human water, is purified,'
because of statements such as this.
The word is '<s>lākṣā</s>'.
<s>Lākṣā</s> is well known.
<s>Śigru</s> means the bark, or else the root, of <s>śobhāñjana</s>.
<s>Guñjā</s> fruits, wool, that is sheep's hair, and jaggery and rock salt are well known.
<s>Yavatiktā</s> is <s>sarpākṣī</s>.
'According to availability' means that they may be taken separately or all together.

children.text: sarve dhātava iti dhātugrahaṇena upadhātava uparasāśca grāhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'All metals': by the word 'metals', secondary metals and <s>uparasa</s> minerals are also to be included.
For:
Whatever, in the treatment of <s>rasa</s>, is above the apparatus in its own proper portion, all that is to be put in the vessel;
because of the superiority of its qualities, this is settled by those who know <s>rasa</s>.
Thus.
The phrase is, 'blown in a crucible with a strong fire.'

children.text: tena pātālayantreṇa vā yathāyogyaṃ sattvanirgamaṃ kārayed ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By that he means that, as appropriate, one should cause the extraction of <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence), whether by a <s>pātālayantra</s> or otherwise.
Accordingly:

children.text: sarvatulyaṃ ca dhānyāmlaṃ bhūnāgaṃ mṛttikā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Equal parts of <s>dhānyāmla</s>, <s>bhūnāga</s>, and again clay,
and likewise stone powders and whatever hard <s>uparasa</s> minerals there are,
one should mix with the five buffalo products, beginning with milk and ending with dung.

children.text: dṛḍhaṃ mardya vaṭīṃ kuryāt karṣamātraṃ ca śoṣayet ||
children.translated_text: After grinding firmly, one should make pills of one <s>karṣa</s> measure and dry them.
With <s>koṭīyantras</s> one should blow them in the fire, using coals produced from <s>khadira</s> wood.
When they are blown three times in this way, the pure <s>sattva</s> falls out.
It would release <s>sattva</s> even from something impossible to process; what need is there to speak of <s>abhraka</s> and the like?
This <s>koṭīyantra</s> is well known.

children.text: pātālayantranalikāyantrayoḥ svarūpaṃ likhyate eteṣāṃ sattvanirgamaḥ sampradāyato yathā gurusaṃkāśaṃ dṛṣṭvā vā kāryo na doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The forms of the <s>pātālayantra</s> and the <s>nalikāyantra</s> are being written down. The extraction of <s>sattva</s> from these should be performed according to tradition, or after seeing it in the presence of a teacher; there is no fault.

children.text: ratnānāṃ śodhanamāraṇamapyāha tāvat pūrvaṃ vajrasya śodhanamāha kulatthaketi ||
children.translated_text: He also states the purification and incineration of gems; first, he states the purification of diamond with the word '<s>kulatthaka</s>'.
<s>Vajra</s> is <s>hīraka</s>, diamond.
And that is of four kinds.
As follows:
The varieties of diamond are fourfold: white, red, yellow, and black.
The white one is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, useful in <s>rasāyana</s>, and grants the eight accomplishments.
The red one, a <s>kṣatriya</s>, conquers death and removes wrinkles, gray hair, and disease.
The yellow one, a <s>vaiśya</s>, gives wealth and makes the body firm.

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ śūdro rujāṃ hantā vapuḥstambhaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: The black one, a <s>śūdra</s>, destroys illnesses and makes the body rigid.
These are to be identified as male, female, and neuter by their characteristics.
Those that are well rounded, full in form, lustrous, and larger,
and that are free from lines and spots, are called male.
Those endowed with lines and spots and having six corners are remembered as female.
And that whose body is triangular and long is indeed neuter.

children.text: pūrvapūrvaṃ tu te śreṣṭhāḥ puruṣā rasabandhakāḥ
children.translated_text: The earlier ones in the sequence are superior; the male diamonds bind <s>rasa</s>.
Female diamonds produce beauty of the body and bestow enjoyment.
Neuter ones, however, have little potency, are without desire, and are devoid of <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: striyaḥ strīṇāṃ pradātavyāḥ klībe klībaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Females should be given to women, and likewise a neuter to a neuter person.
Males, being stronger, are always suitable for everyone.
Thus.

children.text: anyatrāpi pañca doṣā guṇāḥ pañca chāyā caiva caturvidhā
children.translated_text: Elsewhere also: there are five defects, five qualities, and four kinds of luster.

children.text: śvetā raktā tathā pītā kṛṣṇā caiva nigṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: White, red, likewise yellow, and black are recognized.

children.text: ṣaṭkoṇaṃ laghu tīkṣṇaṃ ca bṛhadaṣṭadalaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: A diamond that is hexagonal, light, sharp, and large, and has eight facets,
and floats on water: that diamond is to be accepted in <s>rasakarma</s>.
Thus.
He also states its purification and related procedures, beginning with "with <s>kulattha</s>" and so on.
<s>Kulattha</s> is the well-known particular kind of grain.
<s>Kodrava</s> too is a particular kind of grain.
The intended meaning is that, after making a decoction, one should cook it thoroughly in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus).

children.text: taptamiti dolāyantrasveditaṃ tadvajraṃ paścādagnau saṃtaptaṃ kṛtvā tadanu kharamūtre niṣecayet ||
children.translated_text: "Heated" means that, after that diamond has been steamed in the <s>dolāyantra</s>, it should afterwards be heated in fire and then quenched in ass's urine.

children.text: evaṃ trisaptadhā kṛtvā mṛtaṃ vajraṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that, when this has been done twenty-one times, the incinerated diamond becomes excellent.

children.text: kecit tu dolāyantre svedanam ahorātreṇaiva bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Some, however, say that the steaming in the <s>dolāyantra</s> is completed in just one day and night.
And accordingly, in another tantra:
One should cook it in a decoction of <s>kulattha</s> and <s>kodrava</s> by means of a <s>dolāyantra</s>;
after taking it out after a day and night, one should impregnate it with horse urine.
Thus.
As for "asafoetida and rock salt":
<s>Kulattha</s> is well known.

children.text: tadbhave kvāthe hiṅgusaindhavakalkena vajraṃ liptvāgnau saṃtāpya kulatthakvāthenaiva secayediti sampradāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The tradition is that, in a decoction produced from it, one should smear the diamond with a paste of asafoetida and rock salt, heat it in fire, and quench it with the decoction of <s>kulattha</s> itself.
As for "frog":
Here the prescription concerning the urine of frogs should be understood as clear.

children.text: tatrādau vajramagnau saṃtaptaṃ kṛtvā tanmaṇḍūkamūtre āvapet ||
children.translated_text: In that procedure, first the diamond should be heated in fire and placed into that frog urine.
The meaning is that one should quench it.

children.text: taptaṃ ca bahudhā iti ko'rthaḥ saptavāraṃ yāvatkuryādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is meant by "heated many times"? The meaning is that one should do it up to seven times.
As for "<s>vaikrānta</s>":
"It is to be purified like diamond."

children.text: yathā vajraṃ pūrvaṃ śodhitaṃ kulatthādikvāthena tathā vaikrāntamapi saṃśodhya paścānmārayedityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The purport is that, just as diamond was previously purified with decoctions of <s>kulattha</s> and the like, so <s>vaikrānta</s> too should be purified and afterwards incinerated.
Because:
<s>Vaikrānta</s> is a variety of diamond.
Thus.
In the opinion of some, it is of four kinds.

children.text: vajram atra dvividhameva grāhyaṃ śreṣṭhatvāt hayamūtreṇa ghoṭakamūtreṇa ||
children.translated_text: Here diamond should be understood as only twofold, because of superiority; "with horse urine" means with the urine of a horse.

children.text: taptaṃ taptamiti ko'rthaḥ taptvāgnau saṃtāpya mūtre āvaped ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is meant by "heated, heated"? The meaning is that, after heating it, one should make it hot in the fire and place it into urine.
This should be done up to fourteen times.

children.text: tataḥ paścāt vaikrāntaṃ meṣadugdhaṃ tasya pañcāṅgaṃ tasya golakaṃ kṛtvā tatra vaikrāntaṃ melayitvā paścānmūṣāpuṭe saṃrudhyāgnau pacet ||
children.translated_text: After that, one should take <s>meṣadugdha</s>, its five parts, make a ball from them, mix the <s>vaikrānta</s> into it, then seal it in a crucible-puṭa and cook it in fire.

children.text: meṣadugdhaṃ meṣadugdhikā tasyāḥ pañcāṅgamityarthaḥ pañcāṅgaṃ tvakpatrapuṣpaphalamūlāni ||
children.translated_text: <s>Meṣadugdha</s> means <s>meṣadugdhikā</s>; "its five parts" means the bark, leaves, flowers, fruits, and roots.
When this has been done seven times, it becomes ash.

children.text: kecit tu meṣadugdhasyetyasya sthāne latāstūttaravāruṇyā iti paṭhanti tasmāt pañcāṅgaṃ laghvindravāruṇyā grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: Some, however, read "the creepers of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>" in place of "of <s>meṣadugdha</s>"; therefore the five parts of <s>laghvindravāruṇī</s> should be taken.
And because this is seen in another text,
for so it says:
Then one should put it into a ball made of the five parts of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>;
having sealed it in a crucible-puṭa, one should then cook it, and after removing it from the ball,

children.text: kṣiptvā ruddhvā paceccaivaṃ saptadhā bhasmatāṃ nayet
children.translated_text: one should put it in, seal it, and cook it thus seven times, bringing it to the state of ash.
Thus.

children.text: vajrasthāne niyojayediti tadvaikrāntaṃ tasya kārye niyojayedityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "One should employ it in place of diamond" means that this <s>vaikrānta</s> should be employed for the work of that diamond.
For this very reason it was stated that <s>vaikrānta</s> is to be purified like diamond.
As for "one should steam it":
<s>Jayantī</s> is a kind of pot-herb.
As for "gems, pearls, and corals":
Gems are of many kinds, such as ruby, <s>puṣparāga</s>, blue gem, <s>vaidūrya</s>, and <s>gārutmata</s>.
<s>Muktā</s> means pearl.
They too are of many kinds.

children.text: pravālaṃ vidrumaṃ tadapi bahuvidham kumārī nārīśabdavācyā taṇḍulīyo meghanādaḥ stanyaṃ kṣīraṃ tena kimuktam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pravāla</s> is <s>vidruma</s>, coral, and that too is of many kinds; <s>kumārī</s> is denoted by the word "woman"; <s>taṇḍulīya</s> is <s>meghanāda</s>; <s>stanya</s> is milk. What, then, is stated by this?

children.text: ratnādīni pūrvaṃ dolāyantre jayantyāḥ svarasena saṃsvedya yāmaikaṃ yāvat paścāt tadagnau saṃtaptaṃ kṛtvā kumāryādīnām ekatamarasena niṣiñcayet ||
children.translated_text: Gems and the like should first be steamed in a <s>dolāyantra</s> with the fresh juice of <s>jayantī</s> for one <s>yāma</s>; afterwards, having heated them in fire, one should quench them with the juice of any one among <s>kumārī</s> and the others.
The meaning is that, when this has been done seven times, they become incinerated.
By using the plural "pearls," their eight varieties are stated.
They are as follows:
those from clouds, then those from conches, from boars, and from elephants,

children.text: mīnajaṃ vaṃśajaṃ caiva phaṇijaṃ śuktijaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: those born from fish, those born from bamboo, those born from serpents, and likewise those born from oysters.
These eight pearl-fruits are always used in the operation of <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion or assimilation),
and those endowed with good qualities are taken, while those with defects should be rejected.
Because:
Large, round, heavy, smooth, and possessed of rays, starry lustre, and watery clarity,
white, pleasing, and clear: these are the ten qualities of a pearl.
Thus.
By the plural "corals," here too he indicates varieties, qualities, defects, and the like.
For so it says:

children.text: atiriktaṃ ca dīptaṃ ca vidrumaṃ parimaṇḍalam
children.translated_text: Prominent, bright, and circular in shape,

children.text: snigdhaṃ ca svaccharūpaṃ ca baddhaṃ śuddhaṃ samaṃ guru ||
children.translated_text: smooth, clear in form, compact, pure, even, and heavy,
a mass like a live coal: these are the ten qualities in coral.
Pale, pervaded by colored fluid, minute, crooked, and hollow,

children.text: rūkṣaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ laghu śvetaṃ pravālam aśubhaṃ tyajet
children.translated_text: rough, black, light, or white coral is inauspicious and should be rejected,
and likewise all gems without exception.
Thus.
All of them, without exception, should be understood from the presence of an expert.
And their characteristics are written as follows:
<s>Padmarāga</s>, <s>kuruvinda</s>, <s>sugandha</s>, <s>nīlagandhaka</s>,
and <s>māṇikya</s> should be understood in the sequence beginning with <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
Smokeless, like blazing charcoal, with a lustre equal to the <s>indragopa</s> insect,
resembling the red color of <s>guñjā</s>: that is <s>māṇikya</s> for alchemical work.
That which is like the <s>cāmpeyaka</s> in color, gold-colored, very pure,
and exceedingly bright is called <s>padmarāga</s>.
Large, well-grown, honey-colored, brilliant, white, and shining...

children.text: guru snigdhaṃ tathā proktaṃ rasarājasya karmaṇi
children.translated_text: For the operation involving <s>Rasarāja</s>, it is likewise said to be heavy and unctuous.
There are <s>indranīla</s>, <s>mahānīla</s>, <s>nīla</s>, and <s>kṛṣṇanīlaka</s>.
These four blue stones are arranged in order beginning with the brāhmaṇa type.
It resembles an atasī flower and is like a blue rain-cloud.

children.text: yaḥ karoti payo nīlaṃ mahānīlaṃ taducyate
children.translated_text: That which makes milk blue is called <s>mahānīla</s>.
It resembles a cat's eye, is blue-yellow, and is very clear.
For <s>rasakarma</s> (alchemical processing), <s>vaidūrya</s> is mobile in luster and has a garlic-like center.
It should be known as <s>garuḍodgāra</s>; the second is <s>karipakṣa</s>.
The third is <s>vaṃśapattra</s>, and the fourth is dust-grey.
It resembles the glow of a firefly and is like the neck of a peacock.
Softness in the four is especially praised for <s>rasakarma</s> (alchemical processing).
Thus.
What need is there to say more?

children.text: pañcadoṣā guṇāḥ pañca chāyā caiva caturvidhā
children.translated_text: There are five defects, five qualities, and also four kinds of hue.

children.text: śvetā pītā tathā raktā kṛṣṇā caiva nigṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: White, yellow, red, and black are recognized.
All of them, bright like the sun, should be free from defects and surface films.
Endowed with their own proper colors, they are excellent for <s>rasakarma</s> (alchemical processing).
Thus.
Now he states another procedure, with the words 'as stated, like mākṣika,' and so on.

children.text: pūrvoktasvarṇamākṣikaśodhanavidhānavat muktāpravālāni śodhayet sarvaratnāni ca vajraśodhanamāraṇavidhivat samprasādhayedityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The intention is that pearls and corals should be purified according to the previously stated method for purifying <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>, and all gems should be prepared according to the method for purifying and incinerating diamond.
On the passage beginning '<s>śilājatu</s>,' and so on:

children.text: jaturlākṣā tatprakāśavat śilābhyaḥ prasrutaṃ dravaviśeṣaṃ tat śilājatuśabdavācyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jatu</s> is lac; a particular fluid exuding from rocks, having an appearance like that, is denoted by the word <s>śilājatu</s>.
In another tantra also it is said:

children.text: māsi śukre śucau caiva śilāḥ sūryāṃśutāpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the months called <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Śuci</s>, rocks heated by the rays of the sun
indeed let flow from themselves a natural juice of fourfold appearance.
It is famous as <s>śilājatu</s>, the destroyer of all diseases.
Thus.

children.text: nanu rūkṣakaṭhinānāṃ śilānāṃ kathaṃ snigdhadravaḥ svarasaḥ sambhavati ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, how can an unctuous liquid essence arise from rocks that are dry and hard?
True.
Here, because the word 'rock' is used indicatively, it is really the corresponding mountain metals or minerals that exude.
And so it has been said:
From the rocks, through the heat of the sun, comes the natural essence of a mountain mineral, appearing like lac-resin.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ bhavenmūtrasamānagandhi tadeva ramyaṃ tu śilājatu syāt
