children.translated_text: It should be black and have a smell like urine; that very pleasing substance is <s>śilājatu</s>.
Thus.
In another opinion also:
Mountain minerals beginning with gold, when heated by the sun, flow forth.
The residue that is resin-like, soft, and clear of earth is <s>śilājatu</s>.
Thus.
Thus this is well known in another tantra also.
That is as follows:
It should be understood as connected with one among the six metals beginning with the heated ones,
and also by its own smell; it is known on earth as having six sources.
Thus.
Because:
Since that resin-like <s>śilājatu</s> arises from a metal,

children.text: tasya lohasya yadvīryaṃ rasaṃ vāpi bibharti tat
children.translated_text: it bears the potency, or else the essence, of that metal.
Thus.
Incidentally, the fourfold classification is as follows:

children.text: hemno vai rajatāt tāmrāt tathā syād ayasād api
children.translated_text: It may come from gold, from silver, from copper, and also from iron.
All have the smell of cow's urine, and, in the order stated, each earlier one is unsurpassed.
Thus.
Elsewhere too it is said:
Tin, lead, iron, and the others are progressively principal, each succeeding one more so.

children.text: yathā tathā prayoge 'pi śreṣṭhāḥ śreṣṭhaguṇāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, in practical use too, the best are remembered as having the best qualities.
Thus.

children.text: caturṇāmapi mukhyānāṃ prasravaṃ śilājatu catuṣṭayam atra guṇakhyāpanāya cānyayonivāraṇāya ca bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: Here the exudate of the four principal metals constitutes the fourfold <s>śilājatu</s>, both to state its qualities and to exclude other origins.
In the expression 'having brought it properly,' the word 'properly' should be understood as indicating that the best is to be taken.
As to how its excellence is known, someone says:

children.text: teṣu kṛṣṇaṃ malaṃ snigdhaṃ laghu niḥśarkaraṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Among them, the black residue should be unctuous, light, and free from grit.
And it should have the smell of cow's urine; that they call the foremost.
Thus.

children.text: grīṣmataḥ praśilācyutam iti yadyapyanyasmin kāle śilājatuprasravaṃ dṛśyate tathāpi grīṣme kharatarakiraṇatāpitābhyaḥ śilābhyo guṇavattaraṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Although the exudation of <s>śilājatu</s> is seen at other times, because the text says 'fallen from the rocks in summer,' it is of better quality in summer, from rocks heated by harsher rays.
By the plural forms such as 'with cow's milk' and the rest, the intention is that it should be treated by <s>bhāvanā</s> repeatedly many times.
<s>Bhṛṅga</s> is <s>mārkava</s>, known in common speech as <s>ghamarā</s>.
Here the substance to be decocted should be taken in an amount equal to the substance that is to undergo <s>bhāvanā</s>.

children.text: kvathanīyadravyamaṣṭaguṇe jale niṣkvāthya caturbhāgāvaśiṣṭe kaṣāye bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: The decoction substance should be boiled in eight times as much water, and the material should be treated by <s>bhāvanā</s> with the decoction when one fourth remains.
That purified substance attains purity: such is the statement.

children.text: nanu pūrvaṃ yacchuddhaṃ syāttatkathaṃ paścācchuddhatāṃ vrajedityatra śuddhaśabdadvayaṃ ca kimartham ucyate pūrvaṃ śilājatupiṇḍaṃ dhūpādinā saṃśodhya paścādanena vidhinā śodhayedityadoṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it is asked, 'How can what was pure before later attain purity, and why are two words meaning pure used here?', there is no fault: first the lump of <s>śilājatu</s> is purified by fumigation and the like, and afterward it should be purified by this method.
For so it is said:
For the purpose of removing defects caused by bad herbs, worms, insects, bites, and contamination,
one should properly fumigate the two iron āḍhaka vessels with neem, <s>guḍūcī</s>, ghee, and barley.
Thus.
It is agreed by all that it has indeed been previously purified.
On the phrase 'the chief <s>śilājatu</s> stone':
'Chief' means the one shown earlier, the best among those varieties.

children.text: śilājatuśilāmiti śilājatoḥ śilāvat saghanapiṇḍaṃ saṃgṛhya paścāt pūrvoktavidhinā saṃśoṣya tadanu sūkṣmakhaṇḍaṃ yathā syāt prakalpyātyuṣṇapānīyaṃ prakṣipya yāmaikaṃ yāvat sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: By '<s>śilājatu</s> stone' he means a dense lump of <s>śilājatu</s>, like a stone. One should collect it, then dry it by the method stated earlier; after that, having made it into fine pieces, one should put it into very hot water and leave it for one <s>yāma</s>.
Then 'it is heated by the wise one' means: by a good physician.
The mention of 'the wise one' here is for the purpose of prescribing proper performance.
For its preparation requires attention to time and other factors.
As has been stated:
Now, in the hot season, with the heat of the sun, when it is cloudless and windless, on a level piece of ground,
one should cook it in vessels made of black iron, according to the prescribed method, in order to liquefy it.
How? As follows.

children.text: śilājatu śreṣṭhamavāpya pātre prakṣipya tasmād dviguṇaṃ ca toyam
children.translated_text: Having obtained excellent <s>śilājatu</s>, one should put it in a vessel and add twice as much water as that.

children.text: uṣṇaṃ tadarthaṃ bhṛśamatra dattvā viśoṣayettanmṛditaṃ yathāvat ||
children.translated_text: After applying strong heat there for that purpose, one should dry it after it has been properly crushed.

children.text: tatastu yatkṛṣṇam upaiti cordhvaṃ vilīyamānaṃ raviraśmitaptam
children.translated_text: Then whatever black portion rises upward, liquefying as it is heated by the rays of the sun,

children.text: tat kācapātre'nyatame vidhāya tatrāparaṃ koṣṇajalaṃ kṣipettu ||
children.translated_text: one should place that in some glass vessel and pour warm water into it.

children.text: punaśca tasmādaparaṃ tu pātrād asmācca pātrādaparaṃ tu bhūyaḥ
children.translated_text: Again from that vessel one should transfer it to another vessel, and from this vessel once more to another,

children.text: punastata ūrdhvaṃ tu nidhāya kṛṣṇaṃ yaduddhṛtaṃ tat punarāharecca ||
children.translated_text: and again, having placed above the black matter that has been lifted out, one should take it back again.

children.text: yadā viśuddhaṃ jalam acchaṃ mardya pracchannabhāvān malayet tu tasmāt
children.translated_text: When, after rubbing, the water is purified, clear, and free from hidden impurities,

children.text: tadā tyajet tacchrimalaṃ śilājatu syājjalamaśuddham evam iti bhūyāt ||
children.translated_text: then one should discard that impurity; thus the <s>śilājatu</s> becomes fit, while the water is impure.

children.text: kāryakṣamamiti anena prakāreṇa yacchilājatu snehaśuddhaṃ kṛtaṃ tat sarvakāryeṣu yojayedityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By 'fit for use' the intended meaning is that the <s>śilājatu</s> purified in this way, with oleaginous treatment, should be employed in all operations.
For so it is said:
A man who uses <s>śilājatu</s> that is purified and properly impregnated by this procedure
is freed from all diseases.
Thus.

children.text: vahnau kṣiptamiti evaṃ saṃkāritasyāsya śreṣṭhatvaṃ tadā syād yadāgnau kṣipte sati nirdhūmaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The phrase 'cast into fire' means this: the excellence of this substance, processed in this way, exists when, on being cast into fire, it becomes smokeless.
And it becomes like a <s>liṅga</s> in form.
For so it is said:

children.text: vahnau kṣiptaṃ tu nirdhūmaṃ yacca liṅgopamaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: That which, when cast into fire, is smokeless and becomes like a <s>liṅga</s>
has been declared by the great seers beginning with <s>Hārīta</s> to be pure and fit for use.
Now he states the procedure for making <s>maṇḍūra</s>, beginning with 'akṣa'.

children.text: akṣāṅgārair iti bahuvacanatvenānyakāṣṭhodbhavair api dhamediti na doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because 'with <s>akṣa</s> charcoals' is in the plural, there is no fault if it is blown with charcoals produced from other woods as well.
<s>Kiṭṭa</s> means the impurity or slag of iron; that which is many years old should be taken, because it is the best.
For so it is said:
Slag that is a hundred years old is best, and that which is eighty years old is middling;
that which is sixty years old is inferior, and anything below that is like poison.
Thus.

children.text: lohajam iti sāmānyalohagrahaṇena muṇḍādisamastalohasaṃbhavaṃ tadguṇamapi ca jñātavyam ||
children.translated_text: By 'born from <s>loha</s>,' since <s>loha</s> is taken in the general sense, it should be understood as produced from all forms of iron beginning with <s>muṇḍa</s>, and also as having their qualities.
Because:
Whatever irons there are, with their respective names, characteristics, and qualities,
<s>maṇḍūra</s> is seen to possess those qualities, whatever the qualities of that iron may be.
For that very reason:

children.text: kiṭṭād daśaguṇaṃ muṇḍaṃ muṇḍāt tīkṣṇaṃ śatonmitam
children.translated_text: <s>Muṇḍa</s> is ten times superior to <s>kiṭṭa</s>, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is reckoned a hundred times beyond <s>muṇḍa</s>,
and so on.
And another passage says:

children.text: ye guṇā mārite muṇḍe te guṇā muṇḍakiṭṭake
children.translated_text: The qualities that are present in incinerated <s>muṇḍa</s> are present in the slag of <s>muṇḍa</s>.
Therefore one should employ <s>maṇḍūra</s> everywhere for the pacification of disease.
Thus.
'With the waters of cows' means with cow urine.
And accordingly it says, 'after quenching it, one should soak it in abundant urine.'
One should do this seven times.

children.text: punaḥ punariti grahaṇenātra saptavāraṃ niyataṃ kiṃtu yāvat śīryate tāvannirvāpayedityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the expression 'again and again,' seven times is not fixed here; rather, the intended meaning is that one should quench it as long as it crumbles apart.
And so it has been said:

children.text: lohakiṭṭaṃ susaṃtaptaṃ yāvat tat śīryate svayam
children.translated_text: The iron slag should be very well heated until it crumbles by itself;

children.text: tacchīrṇaṃ grāhayet teṣāṃ maṇḍūraṃ tu prayojayet
children.translated_text: one should take that crumbled material and employ it as <s>maṇḍūra</s>.
Thus.
In this way one should do it seven times; here twice the amount of <s>triphalā</s> decoction is used.
One should powder the <s>maṇḍūra</s>; the word 'excellent' means the best kind.
Its excellence comes from its resemblance to collyrium.
Now, 'of the <s>kṣīravṛkṣa</s>'.

children.text: kṣīravṛkṣo'tra muṣkakaḥ kathitaḥ sa ca parvatajaḥ morava iti loke ||
children.translated_text: Here the <s>kṣīravṛkṣa</s> is said to be <s>muṣkaka</s>; it is mountain-born and is known in common usage as <s>morava</s>.

children.text: kecit sāmānyagrahaṇenaivānye kṣīravṛkṣā api gṛhyante ityāhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some say that, by taking the term generally, other latex-bearing trees too are included.
Such as:

One should burn <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>aśvakarṇa</s>, <s>pāribhadra</s>, <s>bibhītaka</s>, <s>āragvadha</s>, <s>bilvaka</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>snuhī</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>pāṭalā</s>, <s>naktamāla</s>, <s>vṛkṣakadalī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>pūtīkendra</s>, <s>vṛkṣāsphota</s>, <s>aśvamāraka</s>, <s>saptacchada</s>, <s>agnimantha</s>, the four kinds of <s>guñjā</s>, and <s>kośātakī</s>, together with their roots, fruits, leaves, and branches.
Thus.

children.text: kāṣṭhānīti bahuvacanenātra kṣīravṛkṣasya kāṣṭhānāṃ bahūn khaṇḍān kṛtvā pāṭya dahedityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the plural 'woods,' the intended meaning here is that one should make many pieces of the wood of the <s>kṣīravṛkṣa</s>, split them, and burn them.
Likewise, in another tantra:

children.text: taṃ cikīrṣuḥ śaradi girisānujaṃ śucirupoṣya praśaste'hani praśastadeśajātam anupahatamadhyamavayasaṃ mahāntam asitamuṣkakam adhivāsyāparedyuḥ pāṭayitvā khaṇḍaśaḥ prakalpyāvapāṭya nivātadeśe nicitaṃ kṛtvā tilanālair ādīpayet
children.translated_text: One who wishes to prepare it should, in autumn, pure and having fasted, on an auspicious day, consecrate a large black <s>muṣkaka</s> born on a mountain slope, grown in a suitable place, undamaged, and middle-aged; on the following day he should split it, cut it into pieces, chop it, pile it in a windless place, and kindle it with sesame stalks.
Then, when the fire has subsided, one should collect that ash separately.
Thus.
'Powder-like, to be rubbed on': <s>pratisārya</s> means something to be applied by rubbing.

children.text: yaḥ kvāthavat sthitaḥ peyaḥ sa pānīya iti saṃjñā ||
children.translated_text: That which remains like a decoction and is to be drunk has the designation <s>pānīya</s>.
Thus <s>kṣāra</s> is of two kinds.

children.text: iti yuktakāryeṣu yuktavyādhiṣu yathāyogyaṃ yojayed ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that it should be applied as appropriate in suitable procedures and in suitable diseases.
Among suitable diseases, for example, in those cases the rub-on form is prescribed.

It is taught for <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>kiṭibha</s>, <s>dadru</s>, <s>maṇḍala</s>, <s>kilāsa</s>, <s>bhagandara</s>, <s>arbuda</s>, <s>arśas</s>, foul ulcers, sinus tracts, skin tags, moles, dark spots, discolorations, freckles, external abscesses, parasites, poison, and the like.

children.text: saptasu ca mukharogeṣūpajihvādhijihvopakuśadantavaidarbheṣu tisṛṣu ca rohiṇīṣveteṣvanuśastravidhānam uktam ||
children.translated_text: And among the seven diseases of the mouth, namely <s>upajihvā</s>, <s>adhijihvā</s>, <s>upakuśa</s>, <s>dantavaidarbha</s>, and the three kinds of <s>rohiṇī</s>, the procedure using an auxiliary surgical instrument is stated for these.

The drinkable form, however, is used in <s>gulma</s>, abdominal disease, <s>gara</s> poisoning, pain of the digestive fire, indigestion, distension, gravel, urinary stone, internal abscess, parasites, poison, and hemorrhoids.
"Drinkable" means fit for drinking; the meaning is <s>kṣārodaka</s> (alkaline water).

children.text: ye cānye'pi pākyasvarjikāyavakṣārā yathāyogyaṃ vaktavyās teṣāṃ cūrṇavaṭakāvalehādiṣu prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And whatever other alkalis, such as <s>pākyakṣāra</s>, <s>svarjikākṣāra</s>, and <s>yavakṣāra</s>, are to be described as appropriate, their use should be made in powders, pills, linctuses, and so on.

children.text: dhīmāniti grahaṇaṃ kṣārakarmaṇi caturo bhiṣak tathā prayateta na yathā kṣāro'guṇo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The word "wise" means that a physician skilled in alkali-treatment should take care in such a way that the alkali does not become defective.
For example:

children.text: naivātitīkṣṇo na mṛduḥ śuklaḥ ślakṣṇo'tha picchilaḥ
children.translated_text: Neither too sharp nor mild, white, smooth, and also slimy,

children.text: abhiṣyandī śivaḥ śīghraḥ kṣāro hyaṣṭaguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: flowing, beneficial, and quick: <s>kṣāra</s> is remembered as having eight qualities.
Thus.
And its faults are as follows:
Excessive heat, excessive sliminess, excessive sharpness and spreading,

children.text: atyarthaṃ mārdavaṃ śaityam atyarthaṃ sāndrameva ca
children.translated_text: excessive softness, coldness, and also excessive density,
too little medicine and faulty cooking: these are remembered as the nine defects of <s>kṣāra</s>.
Thus.
As for "<s>pārada</s>."
It gives the far shore of the ocean of becoming; therefore it is called <s>pārada</s>.
For this very reason it is said in the praise of <s>rasa</s>:

children.text: tejo mṛgāṅkamauleḥ soḍhaṃ svenaiva tejasāṃ puñjaiḥ
children.translated_text: I praise that <s>Raseśvara</s>, the splendor of the moon-crested lord, borne by its own masses of brilliance,
the wish-fulfilling tree that bestows freedom from old age and death.
And another passage says:
Apart from the single <s>Rasarāja</s>, the boundless <s>pārada</s>, who through the eight powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> removes the fault of worldly existence,
what other remover of old age is there?
Thus.
Such <s>pārada</s> is to be prepared on an auspicious day.

children.text: sa ca dehalohayoḥ siddhiṃ kuryāditi tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the intended meaning is that it produces accomplishment in the body and in metals.
Bodily accomplishment consists in the removal of disease.
That is health of the body; and accomplishment of metal consists in purifying and making gold, silver, and the like.
Again, what sort of <s>rasa</s> is it?
It is the conqueror of all diseases.

children.text: sarve ca te rogāḥ śarīramano'bhipannā jvaramadamūrchādayaḥ teṣāṃ jetā vināśakara ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: All those diseases, such as fever, intoxication, and fainting, that have attacked body and mind: it is their conqueror, that is, their destroyer.
Again, what kind of <s>rasa</s> is it? It is nourishing.
<s>Puṣṭi</s> is the nourishment of the bodily constituents; because it brings that about, it is called nourishing.
For this very reason, because of nourishment and aphrodisiac power, this too is renowned.
As for "on an auspicious day":
It means on a good day, a day joined with a gentle lunar date, constellation, and so on as taught in <s>jyotiḥśāstra</s>.
And accordingly it is said:

children.text: natvā guruṃ bhairavakanyakābaṭuṃ dvīpānanaṃ siddhamamuṣya rakṣitam
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the guru, to <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Kanyā</s>, <s>Baṭu</s>, to the elephant-faced one, and to the protected <s>Siddha</s>,

children.text: antaḥ sunīlaṃ bahir ujjvalaṃ rasaṃ niveśayet khalvatale śubhe dine ||
children.translated_text: one should place the <s>rasa</s>, dark blue within and bright without, on the surface of the mortar on an auspicious day.
Elsewhere too it is said:

children.text: vijane pavanādivarjite vā deśe saumyadine dinādikāle
children.translated_text: In a solitary place free from wind and the like, or in a suitable region, on a gentle day at the beginning of the day and so forth,

children.text: balimatra vidhāya pūjanaṃ ca tadanuvidhiḥ pratimantritaṃ vidhijñaiḥ
children.translated_text: having made the offering there and the worship, the subsequent rite, empowered by mantra, is to be performed by those who know the rule.
Thus.
"Prepared" means processed according to measure and the other requirements.
For example:
<s>Rasa</s> should be obtained under a good constellation, in a measure of a hundred <s>palas</s>,
or fifty, twenty-five, ten, five, or even one.
For the excellent processing of <s>rasa</s>, it should not be made less than one <s>pala</s>.
Therefore, for the purification of <s>sūta</s>, accompanied by skilled assistants,
having taken all the implements, one should begin the operation with <s>rasa</s>.
And so on.
As for "complete accomplishment":
It is both worldly and otherworldly.
And it is said:

children.text: yataḥ baddhaḥ khecaratāṃ padaṃ nayeddharate vyādhisamūhaṃ mūrchitaḥ
children.translated_text: For when fixed it leads one to the state of moving in the sky; when stupefied it removes the mass of diseases;
when digested it destroys birth and old age; when made to penetrate and colored, it grants devotion and liberation.

children.text: yadi pañcatvagataṃ hi sūtakaṃ bhakṣitaṃ syādamaratvakārakam
children.translated_text: If <s>sūtaka</s>, having reached the fivefold state, is eaten, it becomes a cause of immortality;
when bound in leech-like form, all-born, and coagulated, it gives the essence of desire.
When reduced to the form of ash, the dark substance born of <s>Girīśa</s> gives the accomplishment of earthly and supernatural powers;
therefore what else is more compassionate than the shore-giving, boundless <s>pārada</s>?
Thus.
As for "of the body and of metals":

children.text: dehaṃ śarīraṃ tasya siddhir jarāvyādhirāhityaṃ lohaṃ suvarṇādi tasya siddhiḥ saṃskāratvamatra vistarabhayānna likhitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Deha</s> is the body; its accomplishment is freedom from old age and disease. <s>Loha</s> is gold and the like; its accomplishment here is its becoming processed. This has not been written in detail for fear of prolixity.
As for "<s>rasendra</s>":
The names beginning with <s>rasendra</s> and ending with <s>rasa</s> are to be understood as names of <s>pārada</s> in operations with <s>rasa</s>.
By whom? By the learned.
By taking "of that" to mean "of <s>rasa</s>," the abbreviated names have been stated.
There are also others in detail.
Thus indeed:
<s>Rasa</s>, <s>Mahārasa</s>, <s>Sūta</s>, <s>Trinetra</s>, and <s>Trilocana</s>,
<s>Harabīja</s>, <s>Cala</s>, <s>Bījendra</s>, and then <s>Rasāyana</s>,
<s>Pārada</s>, <s>Suvarṇākhya</s>, and likewise <s>Mahāvahni</s>,
<s>Lokeśa</s>, <s>Khecara</s>, <s>Divya</s>, <s>Saubhāgya</s>, and <s>Paramāmṛta</s>,
<s>Śaśihemanidhi</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, and also <s>Jñāna</s>,
<s>Sūkṣma</s>, <s>Śānta</s>, and <s>Prabhu</s>; it is also remembered as <s>Kalikāntakara</s>.
These are names of <s>rasa</s>, and likewise there are others, as in the doctrine of <s>Śiva</s>.
Thus.
As for "copper":

children.text: tāmrādayo navasaṃkhyā dhātavo matāste sūryādīnāṃ navagrahāṇāṃ nāmabhiḥ kṛtvā kramātkathitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The metals beginning with copper are regarded as nine in number, and they are stated in order by means of the names of the nine planets beginning with the sun.

children.text: etena kim uktam tāmramādityasaṃjñaṃ tāraṃ raupyaṃ somasaṃjñam āraṃ pītalohaṃ tanmaṅgalasaṃjñaṃ nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ tadbudhasaṃjñaṃ hemaṃ suvarṇaṃ tadbṛhaspatisaṃjñaṃ vaṅgaṃ śukrasaṃjñaṃ tīkṣṇakamayastacchanisaṃjñaṃ kāṃsyaṃ rāhusaṃjñaṃ vṛttalohaṃ ketusaṃjñamiti kramaḥ ete dhātavo navagrahanāmabhir boddhavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is said by this? Copper is called <s>Āditya</s>; <s>tāra</s>, silver, is called <s>Soma</s>; <s>āra</s>, yellow metal, is called <s>Maṅgala</s>; <s>nāga</s>, lead, is called <s>Budha</s>; <s>hema</s>, gold, is called <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; <s>vaṅga</s> is called <s>Śukra</s>; <s>tīkṣṇaka</s>, iron, is called <s>Śani</s>; <s>kāṃsya</s> is called <s>Rāhu</s>; <s>vṛttaloha</s> is called <s>Ketu</s>. This is the order. These metals should be understood by the names of the nine planets.
As for "rājī":
With the words beginning "<s>rājī</s>, <s>rasona</s>," the procedure for the first process, the sweating treatment, is begun.

children.text: yataḥ santi bhūyāṃsaḥ saṃskārāḥ te ke ityatrāha
children.translated_text: Since there are many processes, he says here what they are.

children.text: saṃsvedanaṃ mardanamūrchane ca utthāpanaṃ pātanabodhane ca
children.translated_text: Steaming, trituration, and <s>mūrchana</s> (stupefaction), raising, distillation, and awakening,

children.text: niyāmanaṃ dīpanameva cāṣṭau pūrvaṃ kṛtāḥ karmaṇi sūtakasya
children.translated_text: and <s>niyāmana</s> (regulation) and <s>dīpana</s> (kindling): these eight are to be done first as operations for <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury).
Thus.
This is said elsewhere as well:

children.text: aṣṭau ca rasasaṃskārā dravye rāsāyane samāḥ
children.translated_text: The eight <s>saṃskāras</s> (preparations) of mercury are the same for a <s>rasāyana</s> substance;

children.text: ete prathamaṃ kāryāḥ syuḥ paścāt sarvatra yojayet ||
children.translated_text: these should be done first, and afterwards one may employ it everywhere.

children.text: rasāditi rasaśodhanakarma yatpūrvamuktaṃ tatkarmaśabdaḥ upaskārādīn praśaṃsayati ||
children.translated_text: In the phrase beginning with "rasa," the mercury-purification operation stated earlier is meant; the word "operation" commends the implements and the rest.
Because:
Having gathered all the implements, one should begin the operation with mercury,
and similar statements are found.
So too:

children.text: upaskaraṃ na yo vetti tasya siddhiḥ kathaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: How could success belong to one who does not know the implements?
so also it is said.
Therefore some implements are being written down.
They are as follows:

children.text: tulābhājanaṃ tacca dvividhaṃ tulā ghaṇṭakaṃ ceti khalvabhājanaṃ tacca trividhaṃ pāṣāṇakhalvaṃ lohakhalvaṃ tāmrakhalvaṃ ca kaṇḍanī sā ca dvividhā śilākaṇḍanī pāṣāṇakaṇḍanī ca vicitrakharparāṇi tāmrādīnāṃ bhājanāni mṛṇmayāni ca koṣṭhikā sā ca trividhā jālakoṣṭhikā kharparakoṣṭhikā bhūmikoṣṭhikā ceti bhastrikā sā ca trividhā carmabhastrikā karparabhastrikā mukhabhastrikā ceti nalikā sā ca dvividhā nalikā vakranalikā ceti ||
children.translated_text: A weighing apparatus, which is twofold: a balance and a <s>ghaṇṭaka</s>; a mortar-vessel, which is threefold: a stone mortar, an iron mortar, and a copper mortar; a pounding implement, which is twofold: a slab-pounder and a stone-pounder; various potsherds; vessels made of copper and the like, and also earthen vessels; a furnace, which is threefold: a lattice-furnace, a potsherd-furnace, and a ground-furnace; a bellows, which is threefold: a leather bellows, a potsherd bellows, and a mouth bellows; and a tube, which is twofold: a straight tube and a curved tube.

children.text: nalikā lohamayī vakranalikā mṛṇmayī mūṣā sā ca dvividhā pakvā apakvā ca apakvāyā bhedo vajramūṣāyāḥ kumbhakāreṇa sumṛttikayā kṛtā sā pakvamūṣā tayorbhedā yathā mūṣā gostanā andhamūṣā nalikāmūṣā sampuṭīmūṣā ḍholīmūṣā iṣṭikāmūṣā kṣāramūṣā saindhavādilavaṇamūṣā kharparamūṣā kokilākhyamūṣā hematāratāmralohasīsakamūṣādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The straight tube is made of metal, and the curved tube is made of clay. A crucible is twofold, baked and unbaked. The <s>vajramūṣā</s> is a variety of the unbaked crucible; that which is made by a potter from good clay is the baked crucible. Their varieties are as follows: the ordinary crucible, the cow-udder crucible, the blind crucible, the tube-crucible, the covered crucible, the <s>ḍholī</s>-crucible, the brick crucible, the alkali crucible, the salt crucible made from rock salt and the like, the potsherd crucible, the crucible called <s>kokilā</s>, crucibles of gold, silver, copper, iron, and lead, and so on.
And tongs are twofold: leaf-tongs and crow-beak tongs.
Hand-hammers, striking implements, and all the implements of goldsmiths as well are included.

children.text: puṭaṃ taccaturvidhaṃ tuṣapuṭaṃ karīṣapuṭam upalapuṭaṃ khadirādikāṣṭhapuṭaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: A <s>puṭa</s> (heating enclosure) is fourfold: a chaff-<s>puṭa</s>, a dung-<s>puṭa</s>, an <s>upala</s>-<s>puṭa</s>, and a <s>puṭa</s> made with wood such as <s>khadira</s>.

children.text: yantrāṇi ca tadyathā śilāyantraṃ pāṣāṇayantraṃ bhūdharayantraṃ vaṃśanalikāyantraṃ gajadantabhājanayantraṃ dolāyantram adhaḥpātanayantram ūrdhvapātanayantraṃ niyāmakayantraṃ ḍamarukayantraṃ kaṭāhayantraṃ kāṃsyabhājanayantraṃ pātālayantraṃ tulāyantraṃ kacchapayantraṃ cakrayantraṃ cākīyantraṃ vālukāyantram agnisomayantraṃ gandhakaṭahikāyantraṃ mūṣāyantraṃ bāṇayantraṃ garuḍayantraṃ sāraṇayantraṃ jālikāyantraṃ cāraṇayantrādīni anyānyapi yathāyogyaṃ bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: And the apparatuses are as follows: the stone apparatus, the rock apparatus, the earth-support apparatus, the bamboo-tube apparatus, the elephant-tusk-vessel apparatus, the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus), the downward-distillation apparatus, the upward-distillation apparatus, the regulating apparatus, the <s>ḍamaruka</s> apparatus, the cauldron apparatus, the bronze-vessel apparatus, the subterranean apparatus, the balance apparatus, the tortoise apparatus, the wheel apparatus, the mill apparatus, the sand-bath apparatus, the fire-and-soma apparatus, the sulfur-pan apparatus, the crucible apparatus, the arrow apparatus, the <s>Garuḍa</s> apparatus, the <s>sāraṇa</s> apparatus, the net apparatus, the <s>cāraṇa</s> apparatus, and any others as suitable.
They are to be understood in their respective places.
Among these, he first states the procedure for steaming:
Having put the mercury into a crucible made of mustard and garlic, one should bind it up firmly,
and the traditional explanation of this and the following passage is written down.

children.text: yathā rājīkādikalkena mūṣāṃ kṛtvā tatra rasaṃ melayitvā upari kadalīdalairveṣṭayitvā tadupari caturguṇena vastreṇa poṭṭalikāṃ baddhvā kāñjikādipūrite bhāṇḍe dolāyantravidhānena svedayet ||
children.translated_text: That is, having made a crucible from a paste of mustard and the other ingredients, mixed the mercury into it, wrapped it on the outside with plantain leaves, and tied over that a pouch with fourfold cloth, one should steam it, by the procedure of the <s>dolāyantra</s>, in a vessel filled with sour gruel and the like.
This is done until three days have passed.

children.text: dinagrahaṇena rātrirapi gṛhyate tenāhorātraṃ svedayedityabhiprāyaḥ etadapi vidhānaṃ tantrāntare coktaṃ tadyathā
children.translated_text: By the mention of "day," night too is included; therefore the intention is that one should steam it for days and nights. This procedure too is stated in another <s>tantra</s>, as follows:
Mustard, salt, asafoetida, and <s>citraka</s>, combined with the three pungents,
all measured at one quarter of the mercury, together with <s>svarjikākṣāra</s> (alkaline salt),
having ground them with the juice of <s>śigru</s> leaves and made them into a coiled form,
one should arrange it properly on a birch leaf or else on a plantain leaf,

children.text: supakve ca dṛḍhe vāpi vastrakhaṇḍe caturguṇe
children.translated_text: on one well matured and firm, or in a fourfold piece of cloth;

children.text: rasaṃ madhye vinikṣipya badhnīyāt tu supoṭṭalīm ||
children.translated_text: placing the mercury in the middle, one should tie it into a very good pouch.
One should steam it for three days with the class of alkaline, sour, and urine liquids,

children.text: tathā svedaḥ prakartavyo majjitā poṭṭalī yathā ||
children.translated_text: and the steaming should be performed so that the pouch is submerged,
but never comes into contact with the bottom of the vessel.
Thus.
The measure of the <s>dolāyantra</s>:
When a vessel has been filled halfway with a liquid substance,

children.text: mukhe tiryakkṛte daṇḍe rasaṃ sūtreṇa lambitam
children.translated_text: and a rod has been placed crosswise over its mouth, with the mercury suspended by a thread,
one should steam it while it is situated in the middle; this is remembered as the <s>dolāyantra</s>.

children.text: atha pratyekasaṃskārānte mardanamuktaṃ tatkarma darśayannāha dinaikaṃ mardayet sūtaṃ kumārīsambhavairdravairityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, showing that operation called trituration, taught for the end of each individual <s>saṃskāra</s>, he says, "One should triturate the mercury for one day with fluids produced from <s>kumārī</s>," and so on.

children.text: eteṣāṃ vakṣyamāṇadravyāṇāṃ dravaiḥ kṛtvā khalve sūtaṃ mardayet tena pratyekarasena kṛtvā dinaikaṃ mardayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is, one should triturate the mercury in a mortar using the liquids of these substances that are about to be stated; the meaning is that, using each juice separately, one should triturate it for one day.

children.text: kumārī prasiddhā citrakaṃ citrakajaṭā kākamācī loke kāmaiyā śabdavācyā triphalā harītakyādikam ebhiryantrapūrvakaṃ saṃmardya paścāt kāñjikaiḥ prakṣālya śodhayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kumārī</s> is well known; <s>citraka</s> means the root of <s>citraka</s>; <s>kākamācī</s> is what is denoted in common speech by the word <s>kāmaiyā</s>; <s>triphala</s> consists of <s>harītakī</s> and the others. Having first thoroughly triturated with these by means of the apparatus, one should afterwards wash with sour gruel and purify it; this is the meaning.

children.text: kāñjikairiti bahuvacanatvena jalena takreṇa vā kṣālanīyam ||
children.translated_text: Because "with sour gruels" is expressed in the plural, it should also be washed with water or with buttermilk.
And likewise in another <s>tantra</s>:
At the end of each individual <s>saṃskāra</s> there should be firm trituration.
Having triturated it, one should place it in the heat until it becomes rather dry.
Then with buttermilk, with <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel), with vinegar, or with hot water,
the wise person should then bring it all together and wash it.

children.text: tathā yantraṃ prakurvīta yathā na kṣīyate rasaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise one should construct the apparatus so that the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is not diminished.
Thus.

children.text: atha svedanasaṃskāram abhidhāya samprati mardanasaṃskāraṃ darśayannāha tataḥ kṣiptvā rasaṃ khalve rasādardhaṃ ca saindhavamityādi ||
children.translated_text: Having explained the sweating procedure, he now shows the trituration procedure, saying, 'Then, having put the <s>rasa</s> in a mortar, and rock salt equal to half the <s>rasa</s>,' and so on.
On the word 'then':
After trituration preceded by sweating, having put that <s>rasa</s> into a mortar, one should triturate it: this is the meaning.

children.text: kaiḥ kṛtvā vakṣyamāṇasaindhavapramukhadravyaiḥ etanmardanaṃ taptakhalve'bhihitamiti sampradāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With what? With the substances beginning with the rock salt that will be stated. The tradition is that this trituration is prescribed in a heated mortar.

children.text: tathāhi yuktaṃ sūtasya sarvasya taptakhalve vimardanam ||
children.translated_text: For so it is said: the trituration of all <s>sūta</s> (mercury) in a heated mortar is proper.
One should put the triad of goat dung, husk, and fire into a pit in the ground.
The mortar placed over that becomes this heated mortar.
Thus.
Or else one should perform thorough trituration in intense heat from the sun.
Such is the tradition.

children.text: anāratamiti anālasyaṃ yathā bhavati tathā mardayediti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Unceasingly' means that one should triturate in such a way that there is no laziness; this is the intention.

children.text: anāratagrahaṇenāpi anyavihitadravyairapi mardanīyaṃ na doṣo granthāntare darśanāt ||
children.translated_text: By the mention of 'unceasingly' also, it may be triturated even with other prescribed substances; there is no fault, since this is seen in another treatise.
For so it is said:
With alkalis, acids, salts, urines, poisons, and also minor poisons,
and with a collection of divine herbs, one should triturate it for three days.

children.text: anuktamānānāṃ mardanārthadravyāṇāṃ ca parimāṇaṃ granthāntarād avagantavyam ||
children.translated_text: The quantities of the substances for trituration whose measures are not stated should be learned from another treatise.
For example:
One should thoroughly triturate <s>pārada</s> (mercury) with medicine amounting to a <s>kalā</s>-portion of it,

children.text: dravyeṇa yāvatā sarvaṃ plutaṃ bhavati mardane
children.translated_text: and with enough liquid that the whole becomes soaked during trituration.
Thus.

children.text: idānīṃ mardanasaṃskārādanantaraṃ mūrchanasaṃskāravidhim āha tato rājī rasonaścetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, after the trituration procedure, he states the method for the mūrchanā procedure, saying, 'Then <s>rājī</s> and <s>rasona</s>,' and so on.
Here 'then' means after the trituration procedure.

children.text: rājī rājikā rasonaḥ lasuna iti prasiddhaḥ mukhyaśca navasādara iti navasādaraś culikālavaṇaḥ mukhyaḥ śreṣṭho grāhya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rājī</s> is <s>rājikā</s>; <s>rasona</s> is well known as garlic. And the chief <s>navasādara</s>: <s>navasādara</s> is <s>culikālavaṇa</s>; 'chief' means that the best is to be taken.
Its excellence, denoted by the word <s>paigāmī</s>, is well known.
'Likewise' means as follows.
It is to be triturated by the procedure stated for trituration, with husk-water.

children.text: kāñjikena kṛtvā kṣālanaṃ svedanaṃ ca pūrvavat kāryaṃ rasasyotthāpanārthaṃ yato mūrchanānantaram utthāpanamapi kāryamiti sarvatra ||
children.translated_text: Washing with <s>kāñjika</s> and sweating should be done as before for the raising of the <s>rasa</s>, because after mūrchanā, utthāpana too must be performed in every case.
For so it is said:
When it has been raised by <s>kāñjika</s>-sweating, one should distill it joined with the mortar preparation.
Such is the tradition.
As in:
One should perform <s>dolā-sveda</s> (swing-bath sweating) with honey, alkalis, acids, and urines.

children.text: utthāpya mūrchayet paścāt trivāraṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having raised it, afterward one should make it undergo mūrchanā three times, again and again.
Thus.
Or else:
Then, with a heated mortar, one should raise the <s>rasa</s> by means of an acid.

children.text: kṣārā mukhakarāḥ sarve sarve hyamlāḥ prabodhakāḥ
children.translated_text: All alkalis make it receptive; all acids indeed awaken it.
Thus.

children.text: mūrchanotthāpanavidhim abhidhāya samprati pātanānyāha tataḥ saṃśoṣya cakrābhamityādi ||
children.translated_text: Having stated the method of mūrchanā and utthāpana, he now states the pātana procedures, saying, 'Then, having dried it, disk-shaped,' and so on.
Here 'then' means after mūrchanā and utthāpana.
On 'having dried':

children.text: eke saṃśoṣyetyanena mūrchitameva rasaṃ cakrābhaṃ kṛtvā pātayediti vyākhyānayanti tanna saṃmataṃ bahusampradāyeṣu mūrchitasyotthāpanaṃ kṛtvā paścāduktadravyaiḥ saha piṣṭikāṃ kṛtvā cakrikāṃ kuryādityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some explain 'having dried' as meaning that one should make the very <s>rasa</s> that has undergone mūrchanā into a disk and distill it; that is not accepted. In many traditions, the intention is that, after first carrying out the raising of what has undergone mūrchanā, one should then make a paste with the stated substances and form a small disk.
Elsewhere too it is said:
Three parts of <s>rasa</s>, combined with a quarter-part of powdered <s>arka</s>,
should be triturated, after adding acid, until a paste is produced.

children.text: yadā na jāyate piṣṭiḥ kiṃcit tutthaṃ tadā kṣipet
children.translated_text: When a paste is not produced, then one should add a little <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulfate).
Thus, in every case.
The disk of <s>rasa</s> made into paste should be smeared with <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) and kept.
The measure of <s>hiṅgu</s> too is one sixteenth of the quantity of <s>pārada</s>; the enclosure is with two dishes.
The well-known filling with salt should be understood from observation of the tradition.

children.text: dṛḍhatarāṃ mudrāmiti mudrātra sāmpradāyikī kāryā yathā gurusakāśādvā dṛṣṭvā ||
children.translated_text: As for 'a very firm seal,' here a traditional seal should be made, after seeing it, or after learning it in the presence of a teacher.

children.text: tathā athavā sadbuddhīnāṃ jñāpanārthaṃ sadābhyastā mudrātra likhyante tathā ca
children.translated_text: Likewise, or else, for the information of those with good understanding, the seals regularly practiced here are written down; and so:
Anthill clay, <s>ārapūraṇa</s>, iron slag,
and white stone: all that should be powdered in equal measure.
Burnt poison equal to all of it should be triturated with water.
One should make an enclosure for crucibles and the like, for smearing all the joints.
Or else:
Two parts of husk should be taken, and one part of pieces of cloth;
a portion of clay four times as large should be triturated after adding water.

children.text: narakeśaṃ śaṇaṃ kiṃcit dattvā tāvat prakuṭṭayet
children.translated_text: Having added a little human hair and hemp fiber, one should pound it so long
until the lump of clay then becomes like wax in appearance.

children.text: yathā na śuṣkatāṃ yāti tathā yantraṃ samācaret
children.translated_text: One should manage the apparatus so that it does not become dry.

children.text: evaṃ saptadinād ūrdhvaṃ mṛdaṃ yoge prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: Thus, after seven days, one should apply the clay in the preparation.
The physician should use it in sequence for coating bottles and the like, and for apparatus.
Another one also:

children.text: harītakīṭaṅkaṇaparṇacūrṇaṃ kharī guḍaṃ pāṃśu paṭuṃ samāṃśam
children.translated_text: Powder of <s>harītakī</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and leaves; <s>kharī</s>, jaggery, dust, and salt in equal parts;

children.text: valmīkamṛt sarvasamā tadardhaṃ vastraṃ tathā gomayakaṃ ca sarvam ||
children.translated_text: anthill clay equal to all of it, half as much cloth, and likewise cow dung, all together;

children.text: jalena mardyaṃ madanopamaṃ tad yantrādisandhau viniveśanīyam
children.translated_text: that should be triturated with water until it resembles wax and should be placed in the joints of apparatus and the like.
Thus.
There are other such recipes also.

children.text: lohakiṭṭaṃ tuṣaṃ dagdhaṃ śukticūrṇaṃ ca karkarā
children.translated_text: Iron slag, burnt husk, powdered oyster shell, and gravel,
these in equal parts, and clay in the same proportion:

children.text: karpaṭena samāyuktā sā hi vajropamā bhavet
children.translated_text: when combined with cloth scrap, that indeed becomes like diamond.
There should be one part of burnt husk and exactly three parts of clay;
mixed with cloth and hemp, it should be applied as <s>vajramṛtsnā</s> (diamond-hard clay).
There should be one part of brick powder, and clay in an equal part;
the sealing of a crucible should be done with it, and through bellows-heating it becomes diamond-hard.
One part of iron slag, and likewise two parts of burnt husk,
mixed with three parts of clay, should be supplied with a little <s>kūpya</s> material.
Pound everything together in one place; the clay will become like diamond.
One should sprinkle water over it from above.
Thus.

children.text: upari ambunā niṣiñcediti ko'rthaḥ tatsthālīsampuṭayantraṃ cullyāṃ nidhāyāgniṃ prajvālya tadupari śītaṃ jalaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kṣipedityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is meant by 'one should sprinkle water over it from above'? The intention is this: having placed that <s>sthālī-sampuṭa-yantra</s> (covered-pot apparatus) on the hearth and lit the fire, one should repeatedly throw cold water over it from above.
According to tradition, a piece of wet cloth too should be kept over it.
Elsewhere also it is said:

children.text: saṃrudhya bhāṇḍadvayagarbhamadhye piṣṭiṃ tataḥ sampuṭamavraṇaṃ tam
children.translated_text: After enclosing the paste between the interiors of two vessels, then that unbroken sealed vessel

children.text: niveśya cullyāṃ tu śanaiḥ pradīpapramāṇam asyādyatale vidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: should be placed on the hearth, and a fire of lamp-size should be made slowly beneath it.
On its top one should place a single cloth moistened with water, slightly warm or rather not hot.
Thus.

children.text: doṣavivarjita iti yadgrahaṇaṃ vṛntaṃ tatsarvaṃ doṣarahitaḥ pāradaḥ ebhiḥ pañcabhiḥ saṃskāropāyaireva bhavatītyasyābhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The inclusion of the phrase 'free from defects' is intended to mean that <s>pārada</s> (mercury), free from all defects, is produced only by these five means of processing.
Therefore he has accepted only five <s>saṃskāras</s> (processing rites) here.
What are those defects? As follows:

children.text: malaṃ viṣaṃ vahnigurutvacāpalaṃ naisargikaṃ doṣamuśanti tajjñāḥ
children.translated_text: Impurity, poison, fiery defect, heaviness, and volatility are what the knowers declare to be its natural defects.

children.text: upādhikau dvau trapunāgasambhavau rasendrarāje kathayanti vaidyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Physicians say that in the king <s>rasendra</s> (mercury) there are two adventitious defects, arising from tin and lead.

children.text: nanu pātanatrayeṇaiva nāgavaṅgakṛtadoṣo vinaṣṭo bhavati nānyaiḥ tathāhi
children.translated_text: Objection: surely the defect produced by lead and tin is destroyed by the three <s>pātanas</s> (distillations) alone, not by other procedures. For:
If lead and tin are mixed with <s>rasa</s> (mercury) for the sake of sale,
an artificial defect arises from those two; freedom from it comes from the threefold distillation.
Thus.

children.text: tatkatham atra pañcabhireva sarvadoṣavivarjito bhavati satyam ūrdhvapātanāntargatam adhastiryakpātanam astīti tasyābhiprāyaḥ tatpātanadvayaṃ tantrāntarād avagantavyam ||
children.translated_text: How then does it here become free from all defects by only the five? True. His intention is that downward and transverse distillation are included within upward distillation; those two distillations are to be learned from another tantra.
Or else:
Then the best <s>rasa</s>, adhering inside the upper pot, is to be collected.
Here, by the word 'then,' the remaining processing rites are indicated; and those are <s>pātana</s>, <s>bodhana</s>, and <s>niyāmaka</s>, so there is no fault.

children.text: atha keṣāṃcij jñāpanārthaṃ prasaṅgataḥ pātanatrayamāha ūrdhvapātanamatraiva kathitam ||
children.translated_text: Now, for the information of some, he incidentally states the three distillations; upward distillation has been taught right here.

children.text: adhaḥpātanaṃ tiryakpātanaṃ ca darśayannāha tathā ca tantrāntare
children.translated_text: Showing downward distillation and transverse distillation, he says; and so, in another tantra:
Having made a new pan, one should smear the <s>rasa</s> beneath it.
With twice as much sulphur, one should digest materials such as <s>bradhnaka</s>.

children.text: vastrāntāni mṛdā liptvā jalaṃ sthālyupari nyaset
children.translated_text: Having coated the cloth ends with clay, one should place water on top of the pot.
One should seal the joint of the pot and the pan very firmly with clay.
On top of the pan a fire of cow-dung cakes should be kindled.

children.text: jalamadhye raso yāti śuddhaṃ tiṣṭhati bradhnake ||
children.translated_text: The <s>rasa</s> goes into the water, while the pure part remains in the <s>bradhnaka</s>.
<s>Rasa</s> is to be distilled from copper, and copper, made separate, from <s>rasa</s>.
As with the mouth of a vessel containing <s>sūta</s> (mercury), another vessel too is joined to it.
In that way, in the three-distillation apparatus, the joint of the two should be made.
In place of water, sour gruel should be supplied; there is no doubt about this.
Thus.
He also states transverse distillation; for:
Having placed <s>rasa</s> in one pot and another pot containing water,

children.text: tiryaṅmukhaṃ dvayoḥ kuryāt tanmukhaṃ rodhayet sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: a wise person should make the mouths of the two face sideways and should seal those mouths.

children.text: rasādho jvālayedagniṃ yāvat sūto jalaṃ viśet
children.translated_text: He should kindle fire beneath the <s>rasa</s> until the <s>sūta</s> enters the water.
This is called transverse distillation by perfected masters such as <s>Nāgārjuna</s>.
Thus.
Now other procedures too are written incidentally, as follows:
In a bundle of coarse rock salt, two crucible-heatings should be made.
Having placed <s>rasa</s> there, one should add <s>navasāra</s> (sal ammoniac) in a sixteenth part.

children.text: sandhiṃ nirudhya yatnena veṣṭayet karpaṭaṃ mṛdā
children.translated_text: After sealing the joint carefully, one should wrap it with cloth and clay.
It should be placed in a <s>bhūdhara-yantra</s> and fire should be applied for three days.
After removing that <s>sūta</s> from the apparatus, one should steam it immediately afterward.
Or one should prepare it with a citron fruit, after discarding its stalk.

children.text: saindhavena samaṃ sūtaṃ tasya madhyaṃ vinikṣipet
children.translated_text: One should put <s>sūta</s>, equal to the rock salt, into its middle.
One should steam it in a <s>dolikā-yantra</s> (swing apparatus), in the class of sour liquids, for three days.
In this way <s>rasendra</s> becomes able to withstand fire in all operations.
This is the <s>niyāmaka</s> procedure.
Now he states <s>bodhana</s> (awakening).
Then, having taken out the <s>sūta</s>, one should place it in a glass bottle.
Then, having filled it with sour vinegar, one should apply a seal at the mouth.
It should be placed in a <s>bhūdhara-yantra</s> and steamed for seven days.
When it has cooled by itself, it should be taken out and steamed again with decoctions.
With the liquids of <s>karkoṭī</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, <s>vahni</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, and <s>ambuja</s>,
it should be steamed for three days with <s>sāranāla</s>, for the pacification of its restlessness.
This is <s>bodhana</s>.
Now he states <s>dīpana</s> (kindling).
Salt, mustard, asafoetida, aloe, and the four alkalis,
the three pungents and garlic, soaked in citron juice:

children.text: piṇḍamadhye rasaṃ kṛtvā svedayet saptadhā punaḥ
children.translated_text: having placed <s>rasa</s> in the middle of the bolus, one should steam it again seven times.
Through that it becomes free from belching; even when its morsel is undigested, it is digested.
By this very procedure it becomes purified, free from every defect.
Or else:

children.text: karituṇḍagaruḍī ṛṣicchaṭā kanyakā kumārikā ca vāyasī
children.translated_text: The <s>karituṇḍagaruḍī</s>, <s>ṛṣicchaṭā</s>, <s>kanyakā</s>, <s>kumārikā</s>, and <s>vāyasī</s>,

children.text: āsurī ca vijayā jayā tathā vahnidīpanakarāśca sūtake
children.translated_text: as well as <s>āsurī</s>, <s>vijayā</s>, and <s>jayā</s>, are fire-kindling agents for <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury).
Thus the eight <s>saṃskāras</s> (processes) have been stated in brief.
Now, while showing the purification of <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), he says, "in an iron vessel," and so on.
On the phrase "the <s>rajas</s> born as <s>gandhaka</s>":
It is <s>gandhaka</s> because it is born from <s>gandha</s> (fragrance).
That is as follows:

children.text: śvetadvīpe purā devyāḥ krīḍantyāḥ prasṛtaṃ rajaḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago on <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, the <s>rajas</s> (menstrual fluid) of the goddess, while she was playing, flowed forth.
When she had bathed in the Ocean of Milk, her silk garment was filled with that <s>rajas</s>.
That garment, washed and churned, fragrant as it was, is remembered as <s>gandhaka</s>.

children.text: caturdhā gandhakaḥ prokto raktaḥ pīto'sitaḥ sitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gandhaka</s> is said to be fourfold: red, yellow, black, and white.
The red is prescribed for operations involving gold, and the yellow for <s>rasāyana</s>.
The white is for applications to wounds and the like; the black is best, but extremely rare.
Thus the purification of <s>gandhaka</s> is accomplished; one may employ it in all operations.
Thus.

children.text: evam iti grahaṇena śodhanāntaramapi darśitaṃ tadgranthāntarād avagantavyam ||
children.translated_text: By the use of the word "thus," another purification too is indicated; it should be understood from another treatise.
As follows:
Having filled a vessel with milk and covered its mouth with cloth,
one should put the <s>gandhaka</s> in the middle of the cloth and carefully close the mouth.
Then, having set an earthen saucer above it and kindled a fire there,
one should keep feeding the fire until the <s>gandhaka</s> falls into the vessel.

children.text: kṛśānau tu svayaṃ nīte gandhakaṃ tu samuddharet
children.translated_text: But when the fire has gone out by itself, one should take out the <s>gandhaka</s>.
Thus.
On the phrase "with ewe's milk":
A <s>meṣī</s> is a ewe.
On the phrase "and with the sour group":
The group called the sour class is held to consist of <s>jambīra</s>, <s>mātuluṅga</s>, and the like.
Thus.
Here in "and with the sour group," the use of "and" suggests another purification.
And accordingly:
<s>Darada</s> (cinnabar) becomes purified when moistened seven times with lac-water.
No impurity, defect, and the like remains; one should employ it in all operations.
Thus.

children.text: asya jātyādikaṃ ca likhyate keṣāṃcit subodhārtham ||
children.translated_text: Its kinds and so forth are also written down for the easy understanding of some readers.
As follows:
The wise call <s>hiṅgula</s> that which is produced from mercury and sulfur.
And the <s>sūta</s> (mercury) to be taken from it is free from all defects.
<s>Darada</s> is to be known as threefold: <s>carmāra</s>, <s>śukatuṇḍaka</s>,
and the third, <s>haṃsapāda</s>; each successive one has better qualities.
Among these, one should employ <s>haṃsapāda</s>, the foremost, in operations with silver.
That resembles gold dross; the others are used for the calcination of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (steel/iron).
<s>Carmāra</s> is black in color, and <s>śukatuṇḍaka</s> is yellowish.
It is prescribed also for extracting the essence; it should be purified in sheep's milk.
And accordingly:
<s>Haṃsapāda</s>, resembling a hibiscus flower, is the very best.
It is used in <s>rasāyana</s>, in calcining all metals, and in coloring mercury.
Thus.
On the phrase "with <s>nimbū</s> juices":
The quantity of <s>nimbū</s> juice and <s>nimba</s>-leaf juice should be understood according to the usual method of <s>bhāvanā</s> (moistening/trituration).

children.text: kecit tu nimbūrasaiḥ nimbapatrarasairityasya sthāne jambīraiḥ pāribhadrarasair iti paṭhanti vyākhyānayanti ca granthāntaradarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: Some, however, in place of "with <s>nimbū</s> juices, with <s>nimba</s>-leaf juices," read and explain "with <s>jambīra</s> juices or <s>pāribhadra</s> juices," because they have seen it in another treatise.
For thus:
<s>Hiṅgula</s> should be ground for the duration of one <s>yāma</s> with <s>pāribhadra</s> juices,
or with the liquids of <s>jambīra</s> fruits; it should be distilled in a distillation apparatus.
Thus.

children.text: atra pāribhadraḥ phalahadā śabdavācyo na tu nimbakaṇṭakapālāśa ityapare ||
children.translated_text: Here <s>pāribhadra</s> is what is denoted by the word <s>phalahadā</s>, not <s>nimbakaṇṭakapālāśa</s>, according to others.

children.text: pātayet sūtayuktivad iti sūtayuktiḥ pūrvaṃ kathitā sā tu pātanayantrādhikṛtā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In "one should distill it as in the mercury method," the mercury method was stated earlier, and that pertains to the distillation apparatus.
Now, explaining the <s>rasamukhakaraṇa</s> (preparing the 'mouth' of mercury), he says "<s>kālakūṭa</s>," and so on.
The varieties of poison beginning with <s>kālakūṭa</s> should be learned from an expert who examines them.
Some characteristics too are written down, as follows:
Dense, dry, hard, and with a luster like split collyrium,
tuber-shaped: this is described as <s>kālakūṭa</s>, a great poison.

children.text: vatsanābhaṃ pāṇḍuraṃ ca kiṃcid rūkṣaṃ ghanaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Vatsanābha</s> is pale, somewhat dry, and dense.

children.text: ghanaṃ guru ca nibiḍaṃ śṛṅgākāraṃ ca śṛṅgikam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgika</s> is dense, heavy, compact, and horn-shaped.
<s>Pradīpana</s> is shaped like a flame-tip and is heavy and smooth.
<s>Hālāhala</s> is held to be wheel-shaped, curved, and blue.
<s>Brahmaputra</s> is pale; <s>haridraka</s> has the appearance of turmeric.
<s>Citra</s> resembles a lotus tuber; <s>saktuka</s> is like <s>saktu</s> flour.
<s>Saurāṣṭrika</s> is shell-colored; this should be known as the characteristic of the poisons.
Thus.

children.text: eteṣāṃ madhye ekadvitrisakalāni yathālābhaṃ saṃgṛhya rasasya ṣoḍaśāṃśena kṛtvā mardanīyāni ||
children.translated_text: Among these, one, two, three, or all of them should be gathered as available, made one-sixteenth of the amount of mercury, and triturated.
The meaning is that here the one-sixteenth measure applies to each individual substance.
Among the secondary poisons are <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>karavīraka</s>, and <s>ahiphena</s>.
<s>Ahiphena</s> should be known as arising from poisonous fish.
For thus:
And in the ocean four kinds of poisonous fish arise.
From them foam is produced; <s>ahiphena</s> is fourfold.
Some say that <s>ahiphenaka</s> is the foam of snakes.
As follows:

children.text: dhāraṇaṃ śvetavarṇaṃ ca raktavarṇaṃ ca jārakam
children.translated_text: <s>Dhāraṇa</s> is white in color, and <s>jāraka</s> is red in color.

children.text: sāraṇaṃ pītavarṇaṃ ca kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ ca māraṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sāraṇa</s> is yellow in color, and <s>māraṇa</s> is black in color.
Because it is like poison, the best foam is used in mercurial operations.
Thus.

children.text: kecit tu khākhasajaṃ kṣīraviśeṣamiti manyante tadabhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: Some, however, think it is a special latex produced from <s>khākhasa</s>, because that other substance is unavailable.
Thus the remainder everywhere is easy to understand.
The measure of these too is as before.
Or else, on the phrase "<s>kaṭuka</s> and <s>kṣāra</s>":

children.text: kaṭukaṃ trikaṭukaṃ kṣāro yavakṣāraprabhṛtikaḥ lavaṇapañcakaṃ prasiddham ||
children.translated_text: The pungent substance is <s>trikaṭuka</s>; the alkali is barley-alkali and the like; the group of five salts is well known.

children.text: rasona iti laśunaḥ navasāraścūlikālavaṇaḥ śigruḥ śobhāñjanam etatsakalaṃ samamātreṇa kṛtvā pāradasāmyaṃ grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasona</s> means garlic; <s>navasāra</s> is <s>cūlikā-lavaṇa</s>; <s>śigru</s> is <s>śobhāñjana</s>. Having made all this in equal measure, an amount equal to the mercury is to be taken.
The rest is easy to understand.
What is the meaning of "metal-moving"? The idea is "for the purpose of swallowing metals."
With the word "or else":
With these substances that are about to be stated, it should be triturated for three days.

children.text: raso yadā bhavati tadā tasya tvarā śīghraṃ dhātuhṛt suvarṇādidhātugrahaṇasamarthaṃ mukhaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) becomes such, then its mouth, a devourer of metals, quickly becomes capable of taking up metals such as gold.

children.text: bindulīti kīṭaviśeṣaḥ sa ca ṣaḍbinduriti prasiddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bindulī</s> is a particular insect, and it is known as <s>ṣaḍbindu</s>.
Thus:

children.text: ṣaḍbindukasya kīṭasya śvetāḥ syuḥ pañca bindavaḥ
children.translated_text: There should be five white spots on the <s>ṣaḍbinduka</s> insect,
and one of a different color; it is very glossy and of intense color.
Thus.
With the words "with salts and acids":

children.text: lavaṇaṃ pañcalavaṇam amlo'mlavargaḥ sa ca jambīramātuluṅgaprabhṛtikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Salt" means the five salts. "Acid" means the class of sour substances, such as <s>jambīra</s> and <s>mātuluṅga</s>.
With the word "now":
Here the word "now" has the sense of immediately after the making of the mouth.
The <s>kacchapa-yantra</s> (tortoise apparatus) is well known.
Its form has already been shown.
Its measure is as follows:
The <s>sūtakotpalaka</s> is remembered as having the measure called <s>prasūta-gopala</s>.
The <s>lāvaka</s> heating is to be known as a <s>puṭaka</s> supplied with seven <s>āḍhakas</s>.
The <s>kacchapa</s> is made with three times those; the <s>kaukkuṭa</s> with three <s>kacchapa</s>s.
The <s>siṃha</s> is made with five <s>kaukkuṭa</s>s, and the <s>meghanāda</s> with two of these.
The <s>gajapuṭa</s> is known in the pit; it is to be given with sixty potsherds.
And with those tripled, the strong fire, the <s>mahāpuṭa</s>, is to be known.
Thus.

children.text: cūrṇeneti śuktikācūrṇena samāṃśakamiti rasasāmyaṃ gandhakaṃ yojyam ||
children.translated_text: With the word "with powder": with oyster-shell powder. "In equal parts" means that sulfur equal to the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) should be added.
Here equality means one <s>puṭa</s> for each.

children.text: tena ṣaḍguṇagandhakaṃ ṣaṭpuṭaiḥ kṛtvā bhavati pāradaparimāṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Thus, after six <s>puṭas</s> have been done, the sulfur becomes six times the measure of the mercury.
With the expression "ash-seal":
The tradition is that it is made with sacred ash, dust, and salt.
Some think that the <s>śarāva</s> here is made of iron; for it has been stated as follows:
One should bring a firm, very broad vessel filled with water.

children.text: tadantaḥ kharparaṃ dadyāt suvistīrṇaṃ dṛḍhaṃ navam ||
children.translated_text: Inside it he should place a broad, firm, new potsherd.
After placing the drop on that, he should pour <s>bījapūra</s> juice over it.
Above it he should place <s>biḍa</s>, and then an iron bowl,
or one made of lodestone, or a brass one, of the <s>bhūtavigraha</s> form.
Having placed it on top with its mouth downward, he should smear it thoroughly.
After thoroughly grinding <s>khaṭīpuṭa</s> and <s>śivībhakta</s>, he should seal it.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ deyaṃ puṭaṃ tasya yantraṃ kacchapasaṃjñakam ||
children.translated_text: A <s>puṭa</s> should be given above it; the apparatus is called <s>kacchapa</s>.
It is prescribed for the <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestive processing) of <s>rasa</s> and of sulfur and the rest without exception.
Thus.

children.text: atra gandhakavidhānaṃ tu asyaiva sampradāyato vyākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: Here, however, the prescription concerning sulfur has been explained according to this very tradition.
Elsewhere it is said, "above and below the <s>rasa</s>."

children.text: tīkṣṇāgniriti atyarthaṃ bubhukṣito bhavati rākṣasasaṃjñaka ityapare sarvakarmasviti yojya ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Sharp-fired" means that it becomes exceedingly hungry; according to others it is called <s>rākṣasa</s>. The intention is that the phrase "in all operations" is to be supplied.
Now he states the method for killing mercury, with the words beginning "<s>dhūmasāra</s>."

children.text: dhūmasāraṃ gṛhadhūmaṃ rasaṃ pāradam torī sphaṭikā navasādaraṃ prasiddham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhūmasāra</s> is household soot; <s>rasa</s> is mercury; <s>torī</s> is <s>sphaṭikā</s>; <s>navasādara</s> is well known.
With the word "with acids":
The meaning is "with the juices of <s>jambīra</s> and <s>nimbūka</s>."
"An equal portion" means a part.

children.text: etena kimuktaṃ pūrvoktaṃ sakaladravyaṃ pratyekaṃ rasamānaṃ melayediti krama iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is said by this is that the whole set of substances mentioned earlier should each be mixed in an amount equal to the <s>rasa</s>; this is the procedure and the intended sense.
For it has been stated as follows:

children.text: pṛthak samaṃ samaṃ kṛtvā pāradaṃ gandhakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Having separately made the mercury and likewise the sulfur each equal in quantity,
and <s>navasāra</s>, <s>dhūmasāra</s>, and <s>sphaṭika</s> likewise, for the duration of a <s>yāma</s>,
having triturated them with lemon water, one should cook them in a glass bottle.
After putting stone-chalk at the mouth, he should apply a seal.
Having wrapped it with seven clay-smeared cloths, drying each separately, he should bind it.
He should set the bottle in a perforated earthen pot.

children.text: pūrayet sikatāpūrair ā galaṃ matimān bhiṣak
children.translated_text: The wise physician should fill it with a filling of sand up to the neck.
Having placed it on the stove, he should kindle the fire in the sequence mild, moderate, and fierce.
Having kept it burning for twelve <s>yāmas</s>, he should remove it when it has cooled by itself.

children.text: visphoṭayitvātha yuktyā ca ūrdhvalagnaṃ baliṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after breaking it open carefully, he should discard the crust adhering above.
The <s>rasasindūra</s> situated below should be employed in all operations.
Thus.

children.text: kecit tu dhūmasārasthāne sīsakaṃ paṭhanti tacca saṃgataṃ tantrāntaradarśanāt
children.translated_text: Some, however, read "lead" in place of <s>dhūmasāra</s>, and that is consistent, since it is seen in another <s>tantra</s>:

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak samaṃ kṛtvā pāradaṃ gandhakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Having separately made mercury and likewise sulfur each equal in quantity,
and <s>navasāra</s> and <s>sphaṭika</s> together with lead, for the duration of a <s>yāma</s>,
having triturated them with lemon water, one should place them in a glass bottle.
The learned man should cook it in a sand apparatus for twelve <s>yāmas</s>.
After it has cooled by itself and he has broken it open, he should discard the crust adhering above.
The <s>rasasindūra</s> situated below should be used in mercury operations.
Thus.
The rest is easy to understand.
With the word "<s>apāmārga</s>":

children.text: apāmārgaḥ prasiddhaḥ tasya bījāni jalena piṣṭvā sampuṭākārā mūṣā kāryā tatsampuṭamadhye sūtaṃ pāradaṃ malayūdugdhamardanaṃ kṛtvā nyased dhārayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Apāmārga</s> is well known. Its seeds, ground with water, should be made into a crucible shaped like a closed capsule. In the middle of that capsule, <s>sūta</s>, that is mercury, should be placed and held after being triturated with the milk of <s>malayū</s>.

children.text: malayūḥ kāṣṭhodumbarikā paścāduktadravyacūrṇaṃ tadupari adhaśca dattvā saṃmardya mṛṇmūṣāyāṃ mudrayet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Malayū</s> is <s>kāṣṭhodumbarikā</s>. The powder of the substance stated afterwards should be placed above and below it, and after trituration it should be sealed in an earthen crucible.
<s>Droṇapuṣpī</s> is well known as <s>nahula</s>.
In common speech it is denoted by the word <s>gūmā</s>.
The word "prasūnāni" means its flowers; <s>viḍaṅga</s> is well known.
Thus.

children.text: irimedako viṭkhadiraḥ tasya tvak grāhyā tadgolaṃ mardayediti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Irimedaka</s> is <s>viṭkhadira</s>; its bark is to be taken, and one should triturate that pellet with it, thus.

children.text: taṃ rasādijanitagolakaṃ samyagavarodhayet mūṣāyām iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should properly enclose that pellet made from mercury and the other ingredients; "in a <s>mūṣā</s> (crucible)" is to be supplied.
With the words "with the milks of <s>kāṣṭhodumbarikā</s>," and so on.
<s>Kāṣṭhodumbarikā</s> is what is denoted by the word <s>kuḍumbarī</s>.

children.text: taddugdhaghṛṣṭahiṅgośceti kāṣṭhoḍumbarikādugdhenaiva hiṅguṃ plāvya tena mūṣāṃ kṛtvā tanmadhye rasaṃ melayitvā sarvaṃ golakaṃ kṛtvā paścānmṛṇmayamūṣāyām andhayet avarodhayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And with "asafoetida rubbed with its milk": after soaking the <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) precisely in the milk of <s>kāṣṭhodumbarikā</s>, making a crucible from that, mixing the mercury in its middle, and making the whole into a pellet, one should afterwards seal it, that is, enclose it, in an earthen crucible.
"With a gentle <s>puṭa</s> (heating enclosure) alone" means with a <s>laghugajapuṭa</s> (light elephant-heating enclosure) alone.
The definition of the <s>laghugajapuṭa</s> is stated in another <s>tantra</s>.
As follows:

children.text: nipuṇavihitagartaḥ ṣoḍaśairaṅgulairyo mitasakalavibhāgas tasya madhye nidhāya
children.translated_text: A pit expertly made, whose every dimension is measured by sixteen finger-breadths; placing the mercury in its middle,

children.text: jvalanam ativiśuṣkair gomayaiḥ pāradasya laghugajapuṭametat proktamevaṃ munīndraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the heating of mercury with very dry cow-dung cakes: this has been declared by the great sages to be the <s>laghugajapuṭa</s>.
With the word "<s>nāgavallī</s>":

children.text: nāgavallī tāmbūlavallī tasyāḥ patrarasena ghṛṣṭo marditaḥ pāradaḥ karkoṭīkandagarbhitaḥ san mṛṇmūṣāsampuṭe nirudhya mudrayitvā gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nāgavallī</s> is the betel vine. Mercury, rubbed and triturated with the juice of its leaves, should be placed inside a tuber of <s>karkoṭī</s>, enclosed in a sealed earthen crucible-pair, and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
<s>Karkoṭī</s> means the tuber of the barren <s>karkoṭakī</s> creeper.
The rest is easy to understand.

children.text: idānīṃ saṃsiddharasānām adhyāyaṃ prakaṭayannāha tatrādau jvarāṅkuśanāmarasaṃ vyācaṣṭe khaṇḍitamiti ||
children.translated_text: Now, while setting forth the chapter on perfected <s>rasa</s> medicines, he first explains the medicine named <s>Jvarāṅkuśa-rasa</s>, saying "broken."

children.text: hariṇasyedaṃ hāriṇaṃ śṛṅgaṃ viṣāṇaṃ tacca khaṇḍitaṃ śakalīkṛtaṃ saṃkṣuṇṇamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hāriṇa</s> means belonging to a deer; <s>śṛṅga</s> is a horn, a <s>viṣāṇa</s>. Its being <s>khaṇḍita</s> means that it has been made into fragments, that is, crushed.

children.text: jvālāmukhyā rasairiti jvālāmukhī jayantī tasyāḥ patrāṇāṃ svarasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With "by the juices of <s>jvālāmukhī</s>": <s>jvālāmukhī</s> is <s>jayantī</s>, and the fresh juice of its leaves is meant.
That <s>jvālāmukhī</s> is of four kinds.
Namely:

children.text: śuklā pītā tathā raktā kṛṣṇā jvālāmukhī bhavet
children.translated_text: <s>Jvālāmukhī</s> may be white, yellow, red, or black.
Thus.
In common speech it is denoted by the word <s>khasinī</s>.

children.text: kecit tu jvālāmukhītyanena bhallātakam iti vyākhyānayanti tanna sarvasaṃmatam ||
children.translated_text: But some explain <s>jvālāmukhī</s> here as <s>bhallātaka</s>; that is not accepted by everyone.

children.text: samam ityatra samaśabdo militārthe vartata iti kecit ||
children.translated_text: At the word <s>samam</s>, some say the word <s>sama</s> is used in the sense of "mixed."

children.text: na tu samamatra sāmyaṃ yataḥ sampradāyeṣvapi jvālāmukhyā rasaiḥ kṛtvā mṛgaśṛṅgaṃ bahuśo bhāvayitvā jārayedityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But here <s>sama</s> does not mean equality, because even in the traditions the intention is that, after the deer horn has been repeatedly impregnated with the juices of <s>jvālāmukhī</s>, one should calcine it.
As it has been said:
The deer horn, crushed and repeatedly impregnated with the juices
of <s>jvālāmukhī</s>, should be cooked in a vessel; its ash should be powdered,
and so on.

children.text: aṣṭāṃśaṃ trikaṭuṃ dadyāditi śṛṅgabhāgānmilitakaṭutrayasya sarvajvarāpaha ityanenānvayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With the statement "one should add one eighth of <s>trikaṭu</s>," the syntactic connection is with "it removes all fevers": the three pungents are to be mixed in at one eighth of the measure of the horn.
By this the meaning is that it destroys even a fever arising from <s>sannipāta</s> (combined doṣic disorder).
Now he gives the explanation of <s>Jvarāri-rasa</s>, saying "mercury."

children.text: atra rasakaṃ kharparakaṃ tālaṃ haritālaṃ tutthaṃ prasiddham ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyakṣāram ||
children.translated_text: Here <s>rasaka</s> is <s>kharparaka</s>, <s>tāla</s> is <s>haritāla</s>, <s>tuttha</s> is well known, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgyakṣāra</s>.

children.text: eke tutthakaṃ kaṇā gandham iti paṭhanti
children.translated_text: Some read "<s>tutthaka</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, and <s>gandha</s>."
There <s>kaṇā</s> is <s>manaḥśilā</s>.
That reading does not circulate in many places, because another form is seen.

children.text: rasaṃ ca rasakaṃ tālaṃ śikhituṇḍaṃ ca ṭaṅkaṇam
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>tāla</s>, <s>śikhituṇḍa</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,

children.text: gandhakaṃ ca samaṃ piṣṭvā kāravellyā rasairdinam
children.translated_text: and <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) as well: after grinding equal quantities with the juices of <s>kāravellī</s> for one day,
and so on.
<s>Kāravellī</s> is denoted in common speech by the word <s>karelā</s>.

children.text: hastaparipāṭyāṃ ca pūrvoktaṃ sakaladravyaṃ samamātraṃ saṃgṛhya kāravellīpatrarasena trivāraṃ rasaṃ saṃmardya tatkalkena tāmrapātrodaram aṅgulārdhapramāṇaṃ pralipya haṇḍikāmadhye'dhomukhaṃ saṃsthāpya mudrāṃ kṛtvā tadanu vālukāyantre pacedyāvattadupari vrīhayaḥ sphuṭanti aṅgulam aṅguṣṭhodaramadhyam ||
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Hastaparipāṭī</s>: having taken all the substances mentioned earlier in equal measure, triturated the mercury three times with the juice of <s>kāravellī</s> leaves, coated the inside of a copper vessel to a depth of half an <s>aṅgula</s> with that paste, placed it face downward inside a small pot, sealed it, and then cooked it in a sand-bath apparatus until the rice grains above it burst; an <s>aṅgula</s> is the middle part of the inside of the thumb.
The <s>māṣa</s>-measure here is because of a severe intermittent fever; in other cases it is smaller.
For so:
This prepared <s>Jvarāri-rasa</s>, in a fever caused by <s>vāta</s>, in a dose of two <s>guñjās</s>,
is to be given with a piece of leaf; it destroys the fever at once,
thus.
Now, setting forth <s>Śītajvarāri</s>, he says "<s>tālaka</s>."

children.text: tālakaṃ haritālaṃ tāmramiti śuddhatāmrabhasma rasaṃ pāradam gandhaṃ gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tālaka</s> is <s>haritāla</s>; <s>tāmra</s> means purified ash of copper; <s>rasa</s> is mercury; <s>gandha</s> is sulfur.
Because "<s>karṣa</s>" is repeated, the meaning is that each is in the measure of a <s>karṣa</s>.
By "with <s>triphala</s> water": <s>triphala</s> consists of <s>harītakī</s> and the others; its decoction is meant.
One should give the <s>puṭa</s>, thus:

children.text: sakaladravyacūrṇaṃ triphalākvāthena saṃmardya golakaṃ kṛtvā tadanu śarāvasampuṭe dhṛtvā tadupari mṛttikāṃ liptvā gajapuṭe pacedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After triturating the powder of all the substances with a <s>triphala</s> decoction, making it into a pellet, placing it in a covered pair of saucers, and smearing clay over it, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; this is the meaning.
With care, thus:
Through skill in the procedure acquired from the teacher.

children.text: paścāt tadrasaṃ śarāvābhyantarāt saṃgṛhya arkadugdhena dantīmūlasvarasena śyāmārasena ca saptadhā bhāvyaṃ saptadhā bhāvanā pratyekenetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards, having collected that <s>rasa</s> from inside the saucers, it should be given seven impregnations with the milk of <s>arka</s>, with the fresh juice of <s>dantī</s> root, and with the juice of <s>śyāmā</s>; "seven impregnations" means seven with each.

children.text: vajrī sehuṇḍabhedaḥ dantīmūlasvarasabhāve kvātho grāhyaḥ śyāmā niśothaḥ tasyā mūlasvarasabhāve kvāthaṃ vā evaṃ siddho bhavati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vajrī</s> is a variety of <s>sehuṇḍa</s>. When fresh juice of <s>dantī</s> root is unavailable, its decoction should be taken; <s>śyāmā</s> is <s>niśotha</s>, and when its root juice is unavailable, its decoction may also be used. In this way it becomes prepared.

children.text: asmatsampradāye'pi dravyacatuṣṭayena bhāvanāṃ dattvā paścāt pūrvoktavidhānena gajapuṭe paktvā siddho bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: In our tradition also, after giving the impregnation with the four substances and then cooking it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> by the procedure stated earlier, it becomes prepared.
It is seen elsewhere also, as follows:
Afterward, with the milky sap of <s>vajrī</s> and <s>ravi</s>, and with the juice of <s>dantī</s> and <s>śyāmā</s>,
having triturated it seven times in the heat, one should cook it by the <s>śarāva-puṭa</s> (covered-dish firing) method,
and so on.

children.text: etanmāṣaparimitaṃ pañcāśanmaricaiḥ saha guḍagadyānakayutaṃ ca tulasīpatradvayaṃ ca saṃveṣṭya bhakṣayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that one should wrap up this, in a quantity of one <s>māṣa</s>, together with fifty <s>marica</s> peppers, joined with a <s>gadyānaka</s> of jaggery and two <s>tulasī</s> leaves, and eat it.
"Divine" means excellent, because it was taught by sages.
"With fifty <s>marica</s> peppers" is merely a numerical specification.
A <s>gadyānaka</s> is the term for six <s>māṣas</s>.
Some say that the jaggery and <s>tulasī</s> leaves are the adjuvant.

children.text: bhaktyeti pūrvaṃ dvijagurupūjanaṃ saṃbhāvya paścādāstikyapūrvakaṃ bhakṣayediti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "With devotion" means that, having first arranged worship of Brahmins and one's teacher, one should then eat it with faith; this is the sense.
Discoloration here may be caused by fever or by another disease.
Now he states a fever-destroying pill, beginning, "There should be one part of purified <s>rasa</s>."
Its purification has already been described earlier.
The <s>rasa</s> is <s>pārada</s> (mercury); of that there is one part.
<s>Elīya</s> is a particular exudate substance produced from the juice of <s>kumārī</s> (aloe); it is commonly known as <s>eluvā</s>.

children.text: tadabhāve kumārīpatrarasameva grāhyamityapare kecidelīyaśabdena elavālukaṃ vadanti ||
children.translated_text: If that is absent, the juice of the <s>kumārī</s> leaf itself should be taken; some others say that the word <s>elīya</s> denotes <s>elavāluka</s>.

children.text: tacca kuṣṭhagandhikaphalasadṛśaṃ bhavati loke prasiddhaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And that is similar to the fruit of <s>kuṣṭhagandhikā</s> and is also well known in common usage.
This is not the view of everyone.

children.text: śivā harītakī ākārakarabha iti ākallakaḥ prasiddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śivā</s> is <s>harītakī</s>; <s>ākārakarabha</s> is well known as <s>ākallaka</s>.
The supplied phrase is: sulfur purified with pungent oil.
Pungent oil is mustard oil.
Regarding "and the fruits of <s>indravāruṇī</s>":
<s>Indravāruṇī</s> is <s>cirbhaṭī</s>; the fruits are its fruits.

children.text: eke mūlāni cendravāruṇyā vadanti tadbahupustakeṣu na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Some say "and the roots of <s>indravāruṇī</s>," but that is not seen in many manuscripts.
Therefore this reading is unsuitable.
Regarding "these are measured as four parts":

children.text: amī elīyapramukhaṣaḍdravyaviśeṣāś caturbhāgamitā bhavanti bhāgo'tra pāradaparimāṇāt ||
children.translated_text: These six particular substances beginning with <s>elīya</s> are measured as four parts; here a part is reckoned from the quantity of <s>pārada</s>.
The meaning is that all this should be powdered and then triturated with the juice of the root of <s>indravāruṇikā</s>.
Here the amount of fresh juice to be added is whatever is suitable for impregnating the substances.

children.text: tacca yāvaccūrṇaṃ plāvitaṃ bhavati tāvaddeyamiti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That means it should be added until the powder has become soaked.
Regarding "with an adjuvant of <s>chinnā</s>-juice":
<s>Chinnā</s> is <s>guḍūcī</s>; the adjuvant is with its fresh juice.
The measure of the adjuvant here is to be learned from another treatise.
As follows:
For <s>rasas</s>, the adjuvant should be two <s>palas</s>, one <s>pala</s>, and a half <s>pala</s>,
respectively, as appropriate, when <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, or <s>kapha</s> predominates.
Thus.
"Fever-destroying" means, in general, that it removes all fevers.
Now, revealing <s>Lokanātharasa</s>, he says, "purified," and so on.

children.text: sūtaḥ pāradaḥ śuddhaḥ saṃskāritaḥ saṃskārā hyasya pūrvaṃ kathitāḥ bubhukṣitaḥ kṣudhitaḥ kāritaḥ dravyairiti śeṣaḥ sa ca bhāgadvayaparimitaḥ tathā gandhasya dvau bhāgau tatheti grahaṇena gandhakasyāpi śodhanaṃ darśitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> is <s>pārada</s>; "purified" means processed, for its processing has already been described earlier. "Made hungry" means made hungry, with "by substances" to be supplied. And it is measured as two parts; likewise there are two parts of <s>gandha</s> (sulfur). By the word "likewise," the purification of the sulfur too is indicated.
"Of the two" means of sulfur and mercury. In "only in <s>kapardakas</s> four times the <s>sūta</s>," "from the <s>sūta</s>" means from the quantity of <s>sūta</s>.
"In <s>kapardakas</s>" means in <s>varāṭakas</s> (cowries); and the characteristics of a <s>kapardaka</s> should be learned from another treatise.
As follows:

children.text: tulanāyāṃ gurutarān pañca gulmān daśa dvijān
children.translated_text: One should employ, in <s>rasa</s> work, <s>varāṭas</s> that are heavier on the scale,
with five bulges and ten teeth, and that are large and yellow.
Thus.

children.text: bhāgaikaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ dadyāditi ko'rthaḥ pāradaparimāṇādardhabhāgaṃ saubhāgyakṣāraṃ saṃgṛhya gokṣīreṇa saha kalkīkṛtyānenaiva kalkena tān rasagarbhitavarāṭān vimudrayed ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
