children.translated_text: What is the meaning of "one should add one part of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>"? The intention is this: taking a half-part of <s>saubhāgyakṣāra</s> relative to the quantity of mercury, making it into a paste with cow's milk, one should seal those <s>varāṭas</s> containing <s>rasa</s> with that very paste.

children.text: tathā śaṅkhasya khaṇḍānāmiti śodhitaśaṅkhasya khaṇḍānāṃ śakalānāṃ bhāgā aṣṭau grāhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, in "of the pieces of conch," eight parts of pieces, that is, fragments, of purified conch are to be taken.
That means in relation to one part of mercury.

children.text: saṃpradāyastu śaṅkhaśakalāni kṣīre saṃśodhya paścāttenaiva kṣīreṇa saha ślakṣṇāni sampiṣya paścādanenaiva kalkena tān varāṭān lepayedityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The tradition is that one should purify the conch fragments in milk, then grind them smooth with that same milk, and afterward smear those <s>varāṭas</s> with this very paste.

children.text: anye tu śaṅkhaśakalāni varāṭikābhiḥ saha puṭet ||
children.translated_text: Others, however, say that one should fire the conch fragments together with the small <s>varāṭikās</s>.
Regarding "of the two dishes smeared with powder":

children.text: cūrṇaṃ śuktikādisaṃbhavaṃ tacca kaliśabdavācyaṃ tenāliptaśarāvakau kṛtvā tābhyāṃ sampuṭaṃ kārayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The powder is produced from oyster shells and the like, and is denoted by the word <s>kali</s>. Having made two dishes smeared with it, one should make a covered enclosure with them; this is the meaning.
The practice is that the traditional sealing should be done at the joints of the pair of dishes.

children.text: tadupari ca mṛllepaḥ kārya ityapi vyavahāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The practice also is that a coating of clay should be applied over that.
Regarding "with a <s>gajapuṭa</s>":
The meaning is that it should be fired here just according to the procedure for a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
And that is made in a pit with cow dung and the like.

children.text: ekonatriṃśadūṣaṇairiti ekena yadūnaṃ maricānāṃ triṃśattena saha ṣaḍraktikapramāṇaṃ bhakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: "With twenty-nine <s>ūṣaṇas</s>" means that one should consume a dose of six <s>raktikās</s> together with thirty peppers minus one.
Regarding "in a <s>vāta</s> condition one should give it with ghee," and so on:

children.text: atra vātaje pittaje kaphaje ca atīsārādāvagre vakṣyamāṇā niyamā boddhavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, in <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> types of diarrhea and the like, the rules that will be stated later should be understood.

children.text: tasyopari ghṛtānnamiti pūrvaṃ rasaṃ bhakṣayitvā paścāttadupari kavalatrayaṃ ghṛtānnaṃ bhuñjīta ghṛtena yuktamannaṃ ghṛtānnam ||
children.translated_text: Regarding "above it, ghee-rice": after first consuming the <s>rasa</s>, one should then eat three mouthfuls of ghee-rice over it. Food mixed with ghee is <s>ghṛtānna</s>.
Here "food" means cooked rice.
"On a bed" means on a couch.

children.text: anupadhānake upadhānaṃ gendukaṃ tena rahite mañce iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Without a pillow": a pillow is a <s>genduka</s>; the supplied sense is "on a bed without that."
By this, the meaning is that one should lie down in such a way that one is properly supine.
Afterwards he states what is wholesome and unwholesome, beginning with 'not sour.'
'Not sour' means devoid of sour taste; 'sour' is citron and the like.
'Food' means prepared food; by that, cooked rice and the like are meant.
'Ghee' means mixed with ghee.
He says, 'sweet curd.'

children.text: madhuraṃ komalajīvitaṃ yadvā madhurayuktaṃ tattu rasālādi ||
children.translated_text: 'Sweet' means <s>komalajīvita</s>, or else something mixed with a sweet substance, namely <s>rasālā</s> and the like.

children.text: prāyeṇa jāṅgalaṃ māṃsamiti māṃsabhakṣaṇaṃ cātra vihitaṃ bāhulyena jāṅgalaṃ pradhānatamaṃ tadapi ghṛtapācitaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: By 'mostly <s>jāṅgala</s> meat,' eating meat too is prescribed here; for the most part <s>jāṅgala</s> meat is the foremost, and even that should be cooked with ghee.
Although the <s>jāṅgala</s> class is eightfold.

children.text: tadyathā jāṅgalā viṣkirāḥ pratudā guheśayāḥ prasahāḥ parṇamṛgā bileśayāḥ grāmyāśceti ||
children.translated_text: That is: <s>jāṅgala</s>, <s>viṣkira</s>, <s>pratuda</s>, cave-dwellers, <s>prasaha</s>, <s>parṇamṛga</s>, burrow-dwellers, and domestic animals.

children.text: tathāpyete tu rogāpekṣayā deyāḥ ghṛtapācitamiti tailaniṣedhāt guṇādhikyācca ||
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, these are to be given with regard to the disease. 'Cooked with ghee' is because oil is prohibited and because ghee has superior qualities.
For so it is said:
Meat that is cooked in oil is hot in potency, pitta-producing, and heavy;
but when cooked in ghee it is light, kindles the digestive fire, is absorbent, pleasing to the taste, and clears the sight.
Prepared with ghee, it is not hot in potency, pitta-pacifying, and agreeable.
Thus.

children.text: ghṛtāniti ghṛtasādhitān athavā sarpiṣā ghṛtena snānaṃ kuryāt koṣṇodakena snānaṃ tu adhaḥkāyasyeti ||
children.translated_text: 'With ghee' means prepared with ghee; or else one should bathe with <s>sarpis</s>, ghee. Bathing with lukewarm water, however, is for the lower body.
Because:
Washing the lower body with hot water brings strength;
but washing the head with that very same hot water takes away the strength of the hair and eyes.
Thus.

children.text: kvacit tailaṃ na gṛhṇīyāditi kvacit kutrāpi tailagrahaṇaṃ na kāryaṃ tena dīpādiṣvapi tailaṃ niṣiddhaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: 'One should not take oil anywhere': 'anywhere' means in any place at all; taking oil should not be done. Therefore oil would be prohibited even in lamps and the like.
Now he states what is to be avoided, beginning with 'bilva.'
Bilva fruit is to be avoided; <s>kāravellaka</s> is what is called <s>karelā</s> in ordinary speech.
He says, 'fruit.'

children.text: vārtākaṃ vṛntākaṃ śapharīṃ kṣudramatsyān ciñcā prasiddhā vyāyāmaṃ śarīrāyāsajananaṃ karma maithunaṃ strīsevā madyādikamiti sugamam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vārtāka</s> is <s>vṛntāka</s>; <s>śapharī</s> means small fish; <s>ciñcā</s> is well known; exercise is activity that produces bodily fatigue; <s>maithuna</s> is intercourse with women; liquor and the like are clear.
'And he should avoid improper sleep': improper sleep is daytime sleep and the like.

children.text: kakārādiyutaṃ sarvamiti sarvamāhāranimittaṃ kakārapūrvakaṃ śākaphalādikaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: 'Everything joined with the letter ka': one should avoid every food-related item, vegetables, fruits, and so on, that begins with the letter ka.
'In the bright fortnight' means in the white fortnight; 'fire-roasted' is meant.

children.text: jayācūrṇamiti jayā bhaṅgā barhipakṣabhasmeti barhī mayūraḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Powder of <s>jayā</s>': <s>jayā</s> is hemp. In 'ash of a peacock feather,' <s>barhin</s> means a peacock.

children.text: mṛgāṅke mṛgāṅkapoṭṭalike hemagarbhe hemagarbhapoṭṭalike mauktikākhye mauktikākhyapoṭṭalike apareṣvapi pañcaratnapoṭṭalikaprabhṛtiṣu eṣa vidhiḥ prayojya iti ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Mṛgāṅka</s>, that is, <s>Mṛgāṅkapoṭṭalī</s>; in <s>Hemagarbha</s>, that is, <s>Hemagarbhapoṭṭalī</s>; in the one called <s>Mauktika</s>, that is, <s>Mauktikākhyapoṭṭalī</s>; and also in others such as <s>Pañcaratnapoṭṭalī</s>, this procedure is to be applied.
Now he explains <s>Mṛgāṅkapoṭṭalīrasa</s>, beginning with 'like <s>bhūrja</s>.'

children.text: bhūrjo vṛkṣaviśeṣaḥ tasya tvak tadākārāṇi tanupatrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūrja</s> is a particular tree; its bark is meant. Thin sheets of that form are to be made.

children.text: tanugrahaṇena yathā aṅgādīnāṃ manoharārthaṃ svarṇakārāḥ kurvanti tadvadatrāpi kāryāṇītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the mention of 'thin,' the meaning is that they should be made here just as goldsmiths make thin pieces for beautifying limbs and the like.

children.text: sūkṣmāṇīti tāni tanupatrāṇi tilavat khaṇḍitāni kṛtvetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Fine' means that those thin sheets should be broken into pieces like sesame seeds.

children.text: sūtena pāradena samaṃ saṃgṛhya khalve kṣiptvā mardanīyam ||
children.translated_text: Taking them together with an equal amount of <s>sūta</s>, mercury, one should put them into a mortar and triturate them.
How? As he says, 'with the juice of <s>kāñcanāra</s>,' and so on.
It is fourfold.

children.text: kāñcanāro vṛkṣaviśeṣaḥ prasiddha eva jvālāmukhī jayantī sā caturvidhā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāñcanāra</s> is a well-known particular tree. <s>Jvālāmukhī</s> is <s>jayantī</s>; it is fourfold.
For so it is said:

children.text: śvetā raktā tathā pītā kṛṣṇā jvālāmukhī bhavet
children.translated_text: <s>Jvālāmukhī</s> may be white, red, yellow, and black.
Thus.

children.text: lāṅgalī kalahārikā yāvadbhavati piṣṭiketi ko'rthaḥ tat suvarṇarasadravyaṃ yāvad dravatvaṃ prāpya piṣṭikā syāt tāvadrasair mardanīyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lāṅgalī</s> is <s>kalahārikā</s>. What is the meaning of 'until it becomes a <s>piṣṭikā</s>'? That gold-and-mercury substance should be triturated with the juices until, having become fluid, it becomes a paste.

children.text: asmatsampradāye tu pūrvoktaśodhitarase suvarṇapatrāṇi dattvā tadanu īṣadgandharajo dattvā upari pātraṃ saṃsthāpya gāḍhaṃ mardayet yāvad ghanabhasmavad bhavati paścāduktarasaiḥ saha saṃmardya golakārthaṃ piṣṭikāṃ kārayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In our tradition, however, gold leaves are put into the previously purified <s>rasa</s> (mercury); then, after a little sulfur powder has been added, a vessel is placed over it and one should triturate it firmly until it becomes like compact ash. Afterwards, grinding it together with the stated juices, one should make a paste for forming a ball.

children.text: tato hemnaścaturthāṃśaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ tatra nikṣipet iti ||
children.translated_text: Then one should put <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) there, one fourth of the gold.

children.text: tataḥ piṣṭīkaraṇānantaraṃ tatra piṣṭīkṛtadravye ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyakṣāraṃ hemnaḥ suvarṇasya caturthāṃśaṃ kṣipet tena yadā suvarṇaṃ catuḥśāṇaṃ bhavati tadā ṭaṅkaṇaṃ śāṇamekamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is: after the paste-making, into that pasted substance one should put <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>saubhāgyakṣāra</s>, in a quantity one fourth of the gold. Thus, when the gold is four <s>śāṇa</s> units, the <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is one <s>śāṇa</s>.
He says, 'powder of ground pearl.'
The sense is: one should take purified pearl powder in twice the amount of the gold and mix it in.

children.text: teṣu pūrvoktadravyeṣu sarvasamaṃ samastadravyasāmyaṃ gandhakaṃ kṣiptvā sarvamekatra mardayed ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The intention is: after adding sulfur equal to all those previously mentioned substances, that is, equal to the whole mass of ingredients, one should triturate everything together.
Here the established practice is that the trituration is done with the previously mentioned juices.
'Equal to all' means all of them: mercury, gold, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and pearl.

children.text: teṣāṃ kṛtvā tato golaṃ vāsobhiḥ pariveṣṭayediti hastapāṭhyāṃ tu tadgolakarūpaṃ dravyaṃ pūrvaṃ śarāvasampuṭe kṛtvā tatsandhau sāmpradāyikīṃ mudrāṃ ca dattvā tadbhāṇḍaṃ gajapuṭavidhānena puṭet ||
children.translated_text: 'Having then made a ball of them, one should wrap it in cloths': in the manuscript reading, however, one first puts that ball-shaped substance in a sealed earthen-saucer capsule, applies the traditional seal at its joint, and heats that vessel by the <s>gajapuṭa</s> procedure.

children.text: paścāt svāṅgaśītatvaṃ dravyaṃ saṃgṛhya yāvatparimāṇaṃ pāradaṃ pūrvaṃ tāvatparimāṇam anyad gandhakaṃ ca dattvā saṃmardya ca pūrvavat puṭet mardanamatra pūrvoktarasair evaṃ siddho bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Afterward, when the substance has cooled naturally, one should collect it; after adding <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) equal in quantity to the amount of <s>pārada</s> (mercury) used before, and triturating it, one should fire it as before. The trituration here is with the previously mentioned juices; in this way it becomes perfected.
The rest is easy to understand.
Now, while making known the <s>rasa</s> named <s>Hemagarbhapoṭṭalī</s>, he says, "with a quarter-measure from the <s>sūta</s>," and so on.

children.text: sūtaḥ pāradaḥ sa ca śodhito grāhyastasya pādaścaturthāṃśastena samaṃ hema grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> means <s>pārada</s> (mercury), and it should be taken purified. A quarter of it, that is, a fourth part, is to be taken, and gold equal to that is to be taken.
By the mention of "of the gold," the meaning is that leaves of it are to be made.
Those are connected with what was stated earlier.
The procedure for making the <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste or amalgam) should be understood as before.
Regarding "the <s>gandha</s> should be twice those two":

children.text: tayoḥ pāradasuvarṇayordviguṇaḥ parimāṇāt tena pāradasuvarṇayoreko bhāgaḥ gandhakasya dvau bhāgau kāñcanāro vṛkṣaviśeṣaḥ tasya patrāṇāṃ svarasena mardayet yāvat piṣṭikākāraṃ bhavati mūṣāsampuṭe śarāvasampuṭe saṃdhau ca mudrāṃ kārayet mudrā sāmpradāyikī kāryā ||
children.translated_text: It is twice the quantity of those two, <s>pārada</s> and gold. Thus there is one part of <s>pārada</s> and gold, and two parts of <s>gandhaka</s>. <s>Kāñcanāra</s> is a particular tree; one should triturate with the juice of its leaves until it takes the form of a <s>piṣṭikā</s>. In the crucible enclosure, in the dish enclosure, and at the joint, one should make a seal; the seal should be the traditional one.

children.text: tata iti grahaṇena tatsampuṭaṃ mṛtkarpaṭakaiśca lepayediti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the word "then," the intention is that that enclosure should also be plastered with clay-cloths.
Regarding "the wise man should cook it with a <s>bhūdharayantra</s> for three days":
For as long as three days one should cook it after arranging it in a <s>bhūdharayantra</s>.

children.text: asmatsampradāye'pi gomayaiḥ kṛtvā punaḥ punaragniṃ prajvālayet yāvaddinatrayaṃ bhavati ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In our tradition too, after arranging it with cow-dung cakes, one should rekindle the fire again and again until three days have passed; this is the intention.
After that, the meaning is that six <s>puṭas</s> should be given.

children.text: puṭaṣaṭkaṃ ca gomayāgninā natu śarāvasampuṭaṃ ṣaḍvāraṃ kāryaṃ tadekavārameva ||
children.translated_text: And the six <s>puṭas</s> are with a cow-dung fire; but the dish enclosure is not to be made six times. It is only once.

children.text: paścātkāryam āha tata uddhṛtyetyādi tatsarvaṃ dravyaṃ gandhakena samaṃ kṛtvā paścādārdrakarasena citrakajaṭāsvarasena ca saṃmardya tena piṣṭadravyeṇa varāṭakān pūrayet paścāttanmukhāni ṭaṅkaṇaviṣaṃ sehuṇḍadugdhena piṣṭvā tena mudrayet ṭaṅkaṇamānaṃ pūrvadravyasambhārād aṣṭamāṃśaṃ grāhyaṃ viṣaṃ tu ṭaṅkaṇārdham ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward he states what is to be done, beginning with "then, having removed it." Having made that whole substance equal with <s>gandhaka</s>, one should then triturate it with ginger juice and the juice of <s>citraka</s> root. With that ground substance one should fill <s>varāṭakas</s> (cowries). Afterward, grinding <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and <s>viṣa</s> with the milk of <s>sehuṇḍa</s>, one should seal their mouths with that. The amount of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> should be taken as one eighth of the previous collection of ingredients; the <s>viṣa</s> is half of the <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>. This is the meaning.
The rest is easy to understand.

children.text: atha dvitīyā hemagarbhapoṭṭalī tāmapi darśayannāha rasasyeti ||
children.translated_text: Now, regarding the second <s>Hemagarbhapoṭṭalī</s>, while showing that too he says, "of the <s>rasa</s>," and so on.

children.text: vyākhyāyāmasyābhiprāyaḥ sakalaṃ svasvaparimitaṃ rasasuvarṇādikamekatra saṃmardya pacediti tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In explaining this, the intended meaning is that all the <s>rasa</s>, gold, and other substances, each in its own prescribed quantity, should be triturated together and cooked.

children.text: keṣāṃciddhastapāṭhyām eva yathā śuddhapāradaṃ prathamato mūrchitaṃ kṛtvā paścāttaduktadravyaiḥ golakaṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: In the practical reading of some, it is exactly as follows: first purified <s>pārada</s> should be made <s>mūrchita</s>; afterward, with the substances stated there, one should make a pellet.

children.text: asmatsampradāye tu lokanāthapoṭṭalīvat kartavyā sā ca pūrvaṃ kathitaiva muktāścātra śaṅkhavat prakṣiptā jñeyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But in our tradition it should be made like <s>Lokanāthapoṭṭalī</s>; that too has already been stated earlier. And here pearls should be understood as inserted in the same way as conch.
The rest is easy to follow.
Now he states the second <s>Jvarāṅkuśarasa</s>: "purified <s>sūta</s>," and so on.
"Purified" means processed.

children.text: saṃskārā hyasya pūrvaṃ kathitāḥ viṣamapi śuddhaṃ taccāpi pūrvaṃ vihitameva gandho gandhakastamapi śuddhaṃ kṛtvā grāhyam śāṇaṃ ṭaṅkaikaṃ pratyekamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For its processes have been described earlier. The <s>viṣa</s> too is purified, and that also has already been prescribed. <s>Gandha</s> is <s>gandhaka</s>; that too should be taken after purifying it. The meaning is one <s>śāṇa</s>, that is, one <s>ṭaṅka</s>, for each.

children.text: dhūrtabījamiti dhattūrabījāni tāni triṭaṅkamitāni hemāhvā svarṇakṣīrī sā ca cokaśabdavācyā ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Dhūrtabīja</s>" means seeds of <s>dhattūra</s>; these measure three <s>ṭaṅkas</s>. <s>Hemāhvā</s> is <s>svarṇakṣīrī</s>, and it is denoted by the word <s>coka</s>.

children.text: eṣā tu sarvebhyaścaturdravyebhyo dviguṇā grāhyā tena ṣaṭ śāṇadviguṇitetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This, however, is to be taken as twice the amount of all four substances; therefore it means twice six <s>śāṇas</s>.
The juice of the pulp of <s>jambīra</s> fruit and ginger juice also should be understood with regard to the <s>doṣa</s>.

children.text: parasparābhāve'pi tridoṣajam iti vyastaṃ samastaṃ viṣamajvaramiti punargrahaṇena prāyaśo viṣamajvaranāśanārthamasya prabhāvo na doṣaḥ kutaḥ vikhyātatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Even when they are not mutually present, by the repeated mention of "arising from the three <s>doṣas</s>, separately and collectively, and intermittent fever," this is mostly the efficacy of the medicine for destroying intermittent fever, not a fault. Why? Because it is well known.
Now, in order to show the explanation of <s>Ānandabhairavarasa</s>, he says, "<s>darada</s>," and so on.

children.text: daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ vatsanābhaṃ viṣaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyakṣāraṃ kuṭajasya phalamindrayavaṃ tvak challī kuṭajasyaiva militvā karṣamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Darada</s> is <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar); <s>vatsanābha</s> is <s>viṣa</s>; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>saubhāgyakṣāra</s>, the fruit of <s>kuṭaja</s>, namely <s>indrayava</s>, and the bark, that is, the bark of <s>kuṭaja</s> itself, together make a <s>karṣa</s>. This is the meaning.
This adjuvant and regimen too are generally recommended in diarrhea.

children.text: gavyājaṃ gosambhavam ajāsambhavaṃ ca takraṃ tattu tribhāgabhinnam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Takra</s> is produced from a cow and also from a goat; and that is divided into three parts.
As follows:
<s>Udaśvit</s> has half water.

children.text: takraṃ tribhāgabhinnaṃ tu kevalaṃ mathitaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: But <s>takra</s> is divided into three kinds; the plain one is remembered as <s>mathita</s> (churned).
Thus.

children.text: kevalo'yaṃ kaphāgnimadhye yojyaḥ iti vyavahāro vṛddhavaidyānāṃ dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Among elder physicians one observes the practice that this plain one should be used in the context of <s>kapha</s> and digestive fire.

children.text: pipāsāyāṃ satyāṃ śītalaṃ jalaṃ deyaṃ na tūṣṇaṃ rasanimittatvāt ||
children.translated_text: When there is thirst, cold water should be given, not hot water, because it is occasioned by the <s>rasa</s> medicine.

children.text: niśi rātrau vijayā bhaṅgā hitā pathyā atraiva prayoge tena prātarevāyaṃ rasaḥ śīlanīya iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At night, <s>vijayā</s>, that is, <s>bhaṅgā</s>, is beneficial and suitable in this very application; therefore this <s>rasa</s> should be taken in the morning only. This is the sense.
Now we shall explain <s>Laghusūcikābharaṇarasa</s>.
Regarding "<s>viṣa</s>":

children.text: viṣaṃ prasiddhaṃ palamitaṃ ṣoḍaśaśāṇamitaṃ sūtāḥ pāradaḥ śāṇikaṣṭaṅkaikaḥ prathamato'bhyantare kācaliptaṃ kṛtvā tayoḥ sampuṭe cūrṇaṃ melayitvā sāmpradāyikī mudrā tatsandhau kāryā tataścullyāṃ niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣa</s> is the well-known substance, measured as one <s>pala</s>, that is, sixteen <s>śāṇas</s>. <s>Sūta</s> is <s>pārada</s> (mercury), one <s>śāṇa</s>, one <s>ṭaṅka</s>. First, after coating the inside with glass, one should mix the powders in the enclosure of the two; the traditional seal should be made at its joint, and then it should be placed on the hearth.

children.text: iti ko'rthaḥ tadrasagarbhasampuṭaṃ vālukāyantre nidhāyādhaḥ śarāvalagnaṃ yathā syādvipacedityabhiprāyo'smatsāmpradāyikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is the meaning of this? According to our tradition, the intention is that, having placed that sealed vessel containing the <s>rasa</s> in a sand apparatus, one should cook it so that it remains attached to the lower dish.

children.text: yathā karpūrapākārthaṃ yantravidhis tadvad atrāpi uparisthasarāvakalagno dhūmasadṛśaḥ kajjalavadrasaḥ sūcī tu rasagrahaṇārthaṃ śalākā kathyate sā tu masūradalasaṃsthā mukhī bhavati tanmukhe yāvallagno raso bhavati tāvaddeyo rasa iti rasavādināṃ vyavahāraḥ mūrchite mṛtaprāye saṃnipātini puruṣe tathaiva sarpadaṣṭe'pīti ||
children.translated_text: Just as there is an apparatus procedure for preparing camphor, so here too the smoke-like, collyrium-like <s>rasa</s> adheres to the upper dish. A <s>sūcī</s>, however, is said to be a rod for collecting the <s>rasa</s>; it has a tip shaped like a lentil cotyledon. As much <s>rasa</s> as adheres to that tip is the amount to be administered. This is the practice of the <s>rasavādins</s>, for a person with <s>saṃnipāta</s> who has fainted and is almost dead, and likewise for one bitten by a snake.

children.text: yathā sannipāte bhakṣaṇaṃ mūrdhni mardanaṃ cābhihitaṃ tathaiva sarpadaṣṭe ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is: just as eating it and rubbing it on the head have been prescribed in <s>saṃnipāta</s>, so too in the case of snakebite.
<s>Tāpa</s> means burning heat produced by the <s>rasa</s>, and so on.
<s>Madhura</s>, 'sweet,' means products of sugarcane; according to the tradition it also includes grapes, pomegranates, dates, and the like.

children.text: idānīṃ jalabandhusaṃjñako nāma rasastamāha bhasmasūtasamaṃ gandhamiti ||
children.translated_text: Now he states the <s>rasa</s> called <s>Jalabandhu</s>: 'sulfur equal to the ash of <s>sūta</s>,' and so on.
The ash of <s>sūta</s>, that is, of mercury; sulfur equal to that is meant.
Here the fruits of <s>dhātrī</s> and <s>dantī</s> are to be added; this is pleasing.

children.text: atra gandhātpādaṃ manaḥśilā iti pāṭhaḥ saṃgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the reading 'one quarter of the sulfur is <s>manaḥśilā</s>' is appropriate.

children.text: tena gandhakaparimāṇasya caturthāṃśasamānā manaḥśilā grāhyā ata eva
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>manaḥśilā</s> equal to one fourth of the amount of sulfur should be taken; for this very reason
there is the statement, 'each equal to <s>śilā</s>.'
<s>Mākṣika</s> means <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>; <s>vyoṣa</s> is the group called dry ginger, black pepper, and long pepper.
Because <s>pippalī</s> is repeated, it should be taken in double quantity.

children.text: ekadravyaparimāṇāt eke jalapippalītyatra vyākhyānayanti tanna sarvamatam ||
children.translated_text: Some explain that here, from the measure of a single ingredient, the word is <s>jalapippalī</s>; that is not the view of everyone.

children.text: matsyo mīnaḥ sāmānyatvena parijñātamatsyo grāhyaḥ sa ca rohitastādṛśaścānyo'pi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Matsya</s> means fish. A fish known in the ordinary sense should be taken, namely a <s>rohita</s> or another of that kind.
<s>Mayūra</s> is <s>nīlakaṇṭha</s>, the peacock.

children.text: saptadhā bhāvayet iti pratyekaṃ saptavāram ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'One should impregnate seven times' means seven times with each substance.
'Wholesome' means that it is to be used with an adjuvant appropriate to the <s>doṣa</s>.
<s>Pañcakola</s> is as follows:
<s>Pippalī</s>, <s>pippalīmūla</s>, <s>cavya</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>nāgara</s>,
is known as <s>pañcakola</s>
and so on.
And the water regimen should be carried out.
By this, according to the tradition, cold water is to be drunk, and the cardiac region and eyes are also to be moistened with that water.
Now, presenting <s>Pañcavaktrarasa</s>, he says, 'purified,' and so on.

children.text: sūtaṃ pāradaṃ viṣaṃ prasiddham gandhaṃ gandhakam etattrayaṃ śuddhamapi boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> is mercury; <s>viṣa</s> is the well-known poison; <s>gandha</s> is sulfur. These three should also be understood as purified.
Their purification has already been stated before.

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyakṣāram etasyāpi śodhanaṃ vihitaṃ tadbharjitameke bhāṣante ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgyakṣāra</s>; purification is prescribed for it too. Some call it roasted.
<s>Dhūrta</s> is <s>dhattūra</s>; the meaning is 'with the fresh juices of its leaves.'
Or, some say, with the juices of <s>dhattūra</s> fruits.
This is because, in the <s>Unmattarasa</s> to be stated later, there is the statement 'with the juices of <s>dhattūra</s> fruits.'
And one should dry it for one day.

children.text: tatsakalaṃ dravyaṃ vastragālitaṃ kṛtvā paścāddhattūrarasena saptavāraṃ bhāvayedityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The intention is that all those substances should be strained through cloth and then impregnated seven times with the juice of <s>dhattūra</s>.
In each impregnation, trituration should also be performed.
Regarding <s>tryūṣa</s>:
<s>Tryūṣaṇa</s> is <s>trikaṭu</s>, and that is known as dry ginger, black pepper, and long pepper.
A decoction of <s>arka</s> root mixed with the powder of these is said to be the adjuvant.
The statement that properly prepared curd-rice is wholesome means that it should accord with the <s>doṣa</s>, digestive fire, strength, and the like.
Here too the water regimen should be carried out as with <s>Jalabandhurasa</s>.
That has already been explained before.
Regarding 'with honey':
<s>Kṣaudra</s> is honey; it is licked together with that.
Swellings, wasting diseases, and the like that arise from <s>kapha</s> are meant.
But for increasing the digestive fire, one should drink honey and fresh ginger juice after it.
The quantity of the <s>rasa</s> is just as stated before.

children.text: anena pāvako'gniḥ śaktaḥ samartho bhavati pākārthamiti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: By this, <s>pāvaka</s>, the digestive fire, becomes strong, that is, capable of digestion.
Now, as for <s>Unmattarasa</s>, presenting that too he says, 'equal parts of <s>rasa</s> and sulfur,' and so on.
This <s>rasa</s> should be used for <s>nāvana</s>, nasal administration.
That should be understood as being in the form of <s>pradhamana</s>, insufflation.
In severe <s>saṃnipāta</s>, according to our tradition, it has also been found effective to give it for oral consumption in a measure of two <s>raktikās</s>.
'One should add <s>trikaṭu</s> equal to that' means equal to that, namely equal to the <s>rasa</s> and sulfur.
<s>Trikaṭu</s> is dry ginger, black pepper, and long pepper.
The rest is easy to understand.
Now he explains the <s>Sannipātāñjana</s>: 'the seed of <s>jaipāla</s> without its skin,' and so on.
The seed of <s>jaipāla</s> means after making it skinless and huskless.
Such a substance should be taken in a quantity of ten <s>ṭaṅkas</s>.

children.text: maricapippalīsūtaṃ ca pratyekaṃ ṭaṅkaikaṃ sūtaṃ pāradaṃ taccātra mūrchitaṃ grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: Black pepper, long pepper, and <s>sūta</s> are each one <s>ṭaṅka</s>; <s>sūta</s> is mercury, and here it should be taken in a <s>mūrchita</s>, processed, state.
Regarding 'from <s>jambīra</s>':

children.text: jambīraphalarasaiḥ sannipātamiti sāmānyena sarvaṃ sannipātaṃ viśeṣeṇa tāndrike yojyo'yamityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With the juices of <s>jambīra</s> fruit. The word <s>saṃnipāta</s> means all <s>saṃnipāta</s> generally; the intention is that this should be used especially in the <s>tāndrika</s> type.
Now this is <s>Mahānārācarasa</s>.
Regarding <s>sūta</s>:

children.text: sūtaṃ pāradaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyakṣāraṃ tulyaṃ samaṃ maricamapi pāradasamam iti gandhakaḥ pippalī śuṇṭhī ca dvibhāgā jñeyā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> is mercury; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgyakṣāra</s>. 'Equal' means the same amount. Black pepper too is equal to the mercury; sulfur, long pepper, and dry ginger should be understood as two parts.

children.text: tenaikadravyabhāgāpekṣayā pratyekaṃ dvau bhāgau sarvatulyaṃ dantībījamiti pūrvoktaṣaḍdravyasāmyaṃ dantībījaṃ grāhyam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, relative to the part of one ingredient, each is two parts. 'Dantī seed equal to all' means that <s>dantī</s> seed equal to the six substances previously stated should be taken.
"<s>Nistuṣita</s>" means without husk, that is, <s>jaipāla</s>.
The word <s>recana</s> is synonymous with <s>bhedana</s> (purgation).

children.text: nanu recanabhedanayoḥ ko bhedaḥ ucyate tatraiva dīpanapācanādhyāye yadapakvaṃ cetyādi boddhavyam ||
children.translated_text: If it is asked, "What is the distinction between <s>recana</s> and <s>bhedana</s>?", it should be understood from that very chapter on kindling and digestion, in the passage beginning "what is undigested," and so on.
Now he states the rasa named <s>Icchābhedī</s>, with the word "<s>darada</s>."

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyakṣāraṃ hemāhvā svarṇakṣīrī loke coka iti prasiddhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgyakṣāra</s>; <s>hemāhvā</s> is <s>svarṇakṣīrī</s>, commonly known in the world as <s>coka</s>.
And the seed of <s>dantī</s> is equal to that.

children.text: svarṇakṣīrīparimāṇasamam etatsarvaṃ saṃcūrṇya godugdhena kṛtvā sādhayet ||
children.translated_text: All this, in a measure equal to the quantity of <s>svarṇakṣīrī</s>, should be powdered, made with cow's milk, and cooked.

children.text: sādhanaṃ tu vahnau tāvaduktaṃ yāvatkṣīrahīnaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The cooking on the fire is prescribed until it becomes free of milk.
The tradition is that the quantity of milk to be taken is four times the aggregate of the substances.
Now he states <s>Rājamṛgāṅkarasa</s>, with the words "ash of <s>sūta</s>."

children.text: atra mṛtapāradasya trayo bhāgāḥ mṛtasvarṇasya bhāgaikaṃ mṛtatāmrasya ca bhāgaikam ||
children.translated_text: Here there are three parts of calcined mercury, one part of calcined gold, and one part of calcined copper.
Some read, "one part of calcined mica."
That is not accepted by all.

children.text: śilāgandhakaṃ tālakamiti śilā manaḥśilā gandhakaṃ pratītaṃ tālakaṃ haritālaṃ śuddhānāmeteṣāṃ ca bhāgadvayaṃ pratyekam ||
children.translated_text: In the phrase "<s>śilā</s>, sulfur, and <s>tālaka</s>," <s>śilā</s> is <s>manaḥśilā</s>, sulfur is well known, and <s>tālaka</s> is <s>haritāla</s>; of these, purified, there are two parts each.
And the characteristics of the <s>varāṭī</s> should be seen in the previously stated <s>Lokanātharasa</s>.

children.text: tena pūrvoktasakaladravyacūrṇena ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyakṣāraṃ mṛdbhāṇḍe mṛtkarpaṭanirmite pātre gajapuṭopalakṣaṇatvāt ṣoḍaśāṅgulagarte pacediti sampradāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The tradition is that, with that powder of all the previously mentioned substances, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> or <s>saubhāgyakṣāra</s> should be cooked in an earthen vessel, a vessel made with clay-cloth, in a pit sixteen finger-breadths deep, since a <s>gajapuṭa</s> is indicated.

children.text: anyathā bahutarajvalanasamparkād dagdhena tvanarthakaro bhavati anupānaṃ doṣāpekṣayā pṛthageva tena daśapippalikākṣaudraiḥ sahāvaleho rasasya jñātavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, through contact with too much flame, it becomes harmful when burnt. The adjuvant is separate according to the <s>doṣa</s>; therefore the rasa should be understood as to be licked together with ten <s>pippalīs</s> and honey.
In the phrase "with twenty-nine <s>ūṣaṇas</s>," alternatively, it should be understood as to be licked with honey and with peppers numbering thirty minus one.

children.text: eke sājyena triṃśadūṣaṇairiti paṭhanti tatra ghṛtamaricaiḥ saha pracāraḥ sādhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some read, "with ghee and thirty <s>ūṣaṇas</s>." In that case administration together with ghee and peppers is proper.
According to someone else, it may also be taken with honey alone.

children.text: tathāca bhinnaṃ mṛgāṅkaṃ tantrāntare dṛṣṭvā pratipāditam ||
children.translated_text: Thus a variant <s>Mṛgāṅka</s>, seen in another treatise, has been set forth.
For:
It is combined with eight <s>marica</s> peppers, or else with the triad of <s>kṛṣṇā</s>.
After considering the <s>doṣa</s> and the rest, one <s>raktikā</s> of the rasa should indeed be given.
One should give it with ghee or with honey, according to the <s>doṣa</s> and the rest.
And so on.
Now he gives the explanation of <s>Agnirasa</s>, with the words "purified <s>sūta</s>."
The phrase is "sulfur in double amount."
That is, relative to the quantity of purified mercury.

children.text: gandhakam apyatra śodhitaṃ grāhyaṃ tayoḥ samaṃ tīkṣṇacūrṇamiti tīkṣṇacūrṇaṃ pāṣāṇādigharṣaṇānniṣpannaṃ mṛtalohacūrṇaṃ ceti tayoḥ samamiti gandhakapāradasāmyaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Sulfur too should be taken here purified. In "<s>tīkṣṇa</s>-powder equal to those two," <s>tīkṣṇa</s>-powder is calcined iron powder produced by grinding on stone and the like; "equal to those two" means that there is equality with sulfur and mercury.

children.text: kanyakā kumārī mardanasya yāvat ślakṣṇatvaṃ syāt bahutarāyāsenetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kanyakā</s> is <s>kumārī</s>. As for the trituration, it is to continue until smoothness occurs, meaning with very great effort.

children.text: hastapāṭhyāṃ tu pūrvoktadravyapiṇḍaṃ saṃgṛhya eraṇḍapatrairāveṣṭya paścāttāmrasampuṭake dhṛtvā tadanu sampuṭamapi patrairācchādya gharme dhārayedyāvaduṣṇaṃ bhavati paścāt tatsampuṭaṃ yathoktameva dhānyarāśau saṃsthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: In the hand-recension, however, one should gather the lump of the previously mentioned substances, wrap it with <s>eraṇḍa</s> leaves, then place it in a copper capsule; after that, cover the capsule too with leaves and keep it in heat until it becomes warm, and afterward place that capsule in a heap of grain exactly as stated.

children.text: ahorātraṃ yāvat sampradāye tu tridinaparyantaṃ dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: It should be kept for a day and night; in the tradition, however, one should keep it for up to three days.
Because this is prescribed in the <s>Loharasāyana</s> that will be stated later.

children.text: evaṃ siddho raso 'paradravyaiḥ saha sāmyo bhakṣyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rasa prepared in this way should be eaten together with other substances in equal measure.
That is as follows:

children.text: trikaṭukaṃ prasiddham triphalā harītakyādikam elā bṛhadelā jātīphalaṃ pratītam lavaṅgamapi vikhyātam etacca nava dravyaṃ pūrvarasasāmyaṃ saṃcūrṇya niṣkadvayaṃ ṭaṅkadvayaṃ kṣaudraiḥ sahāvalehyamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Trikaṭuka</s> is well known; <s>triphalā</s> consists of <s>harītakī</s> and the others; <s>elā</s> is <s>bṛhadelā</s>; <s>jātīphala</s> is familiar; and <s>lavaṅga</s> too is well known. These nine substances should be powdered in equal quantity to the preceding rasa, and two <s>niṣkas</s>, that is, two <s>ṭaṅkas</s>, are to be licked with honey; this is the meaning.

children.text: atha sūryāvartarasamāha sūtārdho gandhako mardya iti ||
children.translated_text: Now he states <s>Sūryāvartarasa</s>, with the words "sulfur should be triturated with half as much <s>sūta</s>."

children.text: sūtaḥ pāradaḥ sa ca gandhakaparimāṇād ardho grāhya ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> is mercury, and the intention is that it should be taken as half the quantity of sulfur.
And likewise in another treatise:
One part <s>sūta</s> and two parts sulfur, triturated for a <s>yāma</s> with <s>kanyā</s>,
one should enclose the two in a fitting copper vessel inside a pot,
and the wise man should cook it for four <s>yāmas</s>, properly with clay and salt.
And so on.
The rest is easy to understand.
Here too the adjuvant should be given according to the particular <s>doṣa</s>; there is no fault.
Now he states <s>Svacchandabhairavarasa</s>, with the words "purified <s>sūta</s>."
"Processed rasa" means <s>mūrchita</s> rasa.
<s>Tāpya</s> is <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>; this too should be taken purified.
Sulfur and <s>tālaka</s> too should be added here purified.

children.text: tālakaṃ haritālaṃ pathyā harītakī agnimantho'raṇibhedaḥ tryūṣaṇaṃ trikaṭukaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyakṣāraṃ taccātra bharjitaṃ grāhyaṃ viṣamapi ekadravyabhāgasāmyaṃ sakaladravyamapi samamātram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tālaka</s> is <s>haritāla</s>; <s>pathyā</s> is <s>harītakī</s>; <s>agnimantha</s> is a kind of <s>araṇi</s>; <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> is <s>trikaṭuka</s>; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgyakṣāra</s>, and here it should be taken roasted. <s>Viṣa</s> too is equal to the part of one substance, and all the substances are likewise in equal measure.

children.text: nirguṇḍikādravair iti nirguṇḍīpatrasvarasaiḥ muṇḍī kedāramuṇḍī vikhyātā asyāḥ svarasairapi dinaikaṃ mardanīyam ||
children.translated_text: "With the fluids of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s>" means with the fresh juices of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> leaves. <s>Muṇḍī</s> is the well-known <s>kedāramuṇḍī</s>; with its juices too it should be triturated for one day.

children.text: anupānamāha rāsnā surabhī amṛtā guḍūcī vātārijam eraṇḍamūlaṃ devadāru śuṇṭhī ca prasiddhā eteṣāṃ samānāṃ śṛtaṃ kvathitam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He states the adjuvant: <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>surabhī</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>vātārija</s>, <s>eraṇḍa</s>-root, <s>devadāru</s>, and <s>śuṇṭhī</s> are well known. "Boiled" means decocted from these in equal amounts.
They say that <s>guggulu</s> is to be added here as an admixture.
Now, the <s>Haṃsapoṭṭalīrasa</s>.
This concerns the phrase, "having burned the <s>kapardaka</s>."
A <s>kapardaka</s> is a <s>varāṭaka</s> (cowrie); if that is absent, conch may also be taken here.
The tradition is that trituration here lasts for four <s>yāmas</s> (watches).
The quantity of pepper and ghee should be understood with regard to the <s>doṣas</s>.
<s>Ājya</s> means ghee.
Regarding "buttermilk-rice": buttermilk is distinguished by a threefold division.
For so it is said:
Buttermilk with three quarters water and its fat removed is remembered as binding and light.
Thus.
"It destroys disease" means disease such as diarrhea and the like.
Now he explains <s>Trivikramarasa</s>, beginning "calcined copper with goat's milk."

children.text: mṛtaṃ tāmraṃ tāmrabhasma chāgīkṣīreṇa sāmyaṃ kṛtvā lohapātre mṛṇmayapātre vā saṃpācayet ||
children.translated_text: "Calcined copper" is copper ash; after making it equal with goat's milk, one should cook it thoroughly in an iron vessel or an earthen vessel.
By the phrase "until the liquid has gone away," the purification of calcined copper is taught; this is the intention.

children.text: tadgolaṃ saṃdhayed iti taddravyagolakaṃ mūṣāsampuṭe melayitvā tanmukhaṃ saṃmudrya vālukāyantre saṃpācya siddho bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Regarding "one should seal that ball": after combining the ball of those substances in a sealed crucible-pair, sealing its mouth, and cooking it in a sand apparatus, it becomes prepared.
The sand apparatus has been described in the chapter on the calcination of <s>rasa</s>.
Regarding "the edible dose is two <s>guñjās</s>": <s>bhojya</s> means what is to be eaten, namely two <s>guñjās</s>.
Here the adjuvant of paste from the root of <s>bījapūra</s> is to be used with regard to the <s>doṣa</s> and other factors.
Now he explains <s>Mahātāleśvararasa</s>, beginning "<s>tāra</s>."

children.text: tāraṃ raupyaṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ śilā manaḥśilā sūtaṃ pāradaṃ śuddhaśabdaḥ tārādibhiḥ pratyekamabhisaṃbadhyate ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyakṣāram eteṣāṃ sāmyamānamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāra</s> is silver; <s>tāpya</s> is <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>; <s>śilā</s> is <s>manaḥśilā</s>; <s>sūta</s> is mercury. The word "purified" is connected separately with <s>tāra</s> and each of the following substances. <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgyakṣāra</s>. The meaning is that these are in equal measure.
The sulfur is purified.
Calcined copper too is to be taken in twice the measure.
"With <s>jambīras</s>" means with the juices of <s>jambīra</s> fruits for five days.

children.text: punaḥ punarjambīrarasaṃ dattvā mardanīyaṃ gharme iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The supplied sense is that it should be triturated in the heat, repeatedly adding <s>jambīra</s> juice.

children.text: paścādbhūdharayantre mṛṇmayamūṣāsampuṭodare kṣiptaṃ mudritaṃ ca sakalaṃ dravyaṃ pācitamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward, all the substances are placed in the cavity of a sealed earthen crucible in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus, sealed, and cooked; this is the meaning.

children.text: evaṃ ṣaḍvāraṃ yāvat puṭaṃ deyaṃ pratipuṭe tu jambīrarasaiḥ kṛtvā mardanīyam ||
children.translated_text: In this way a <s>puṭa</s> (sealed heating) should be given up to six times, and at each <s>puṭa</s> it should be triturated with <s>jambīra</s> juices.

children.text: etanmardanaṃ yathākālaṃ nātra pañcadinamardanaṃ niyatamiti sampradāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The tradition is that this trituration is done for the proper length of time; here a five-day trituration is not fixed.
Or else, in view of the trituration that will be stated, it is for one day.
The <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus should be looked up under the previously stated <s>Hemagarbharasa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ saṃsiddhamidaṃ ṣaṭpalapramitaṃ saṃgṛhya vakṣyamāṇadravyaiḥ saha punarmardayet ||
children.translated_text: After collecting this preparation, fully accomplished in this way and measuring six <s>palas</s>, one should again triturate it together with the substances to be stated.
That means for one day with <s>jambīra</s> juice.
After that, a light <s>puṭa</s> should be given by the method stated earlier.
Others say it is a <s>kukkuṭapuṭa</s>.

children.text: punarapi evaṃ siddhasyāsya yattriṃśadbhāgaṃ tena samaṃ viṣaṃ yojyamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, poison equal to one thirtieth part of this substance prepared in this way should be added; this is the meaning.
Since it is a powder, buffalo ghee should also be given here in the amount appropriate for a lickable preparation.
Half a <s>ṭaṅka</s> is two <s>māṣakas</s>.

children.text: sadā śabdo'tra rasasaṃsevyaviṣayaṃ sūcayati tena sevyo'yaṃ rasa iti tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The word "always" here indicates the matter of using the <s>rasa</s>; therefore the intended meaning is that this <s>rasa</s> is to be consumed.

children.text: anupāne tu vākucī somarājīphalāni ājyamatrāpi māhiṣam ||
children.translated_text: For the adjuvant, there are the fruits of <s>vākucī</s> or <s>somarājī</s>; the ghee here too is buffalo ghee.
Now he explains <s>Kuṣṭhakuṭhārarasa</s>, beginning "sulfur equal to ash and mercury."

children.text: bhasmasūtasamo gandha ityanena rasādiśilājatuparyantaṃ dravyaṃ pṛthakṣoḍaśaśāṇamitaṃ grāhyaṃ tatra mṛtāyo māritalohacūrṇaṃ mṛtatāmracūrṇaṃ ca triphalāharītakyādikaṃ mahānimbo loke vakāina śabdavācyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the statement "sulfur equal to ash and mercury," the substances from <s>rasa</s> through <s>śilājatu</s> are each to be taken in a measure of sixteen <s>śāṇas</s>. There, <s>mṛtāyas</s> is powder of calcined iron, and there is also powder of calcined copper; <s>triphala</s> consists of <s>harītakī</s> and the others; <s>mahānimba</s> is called <s>vakāina</s> in common speech.

children.text: karañjo bṛhatkarañjaḥ asya bījaṃ phalaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭiśāṇamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Karañja</s> is the large <s>karañja</s>; its seed, that is, its fruit, is in a measure of sixty-four <s>śāṇas</s>.

children.text: madhu ghṛtaparimāṇaṃ tu yāvat sakalaṃ dravyam āloḍitaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: The quantity of honey and ghee is enough for all the substances to be mixed together.
That much measure should be added.

children.text: dviniṣkaṃ ṭaṅkadvayaṃ dviniṣkād adhikamānamapi deyaṃ na doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Two <s>niṣkas</s> are two <s>ṭaṅkas</s>; even a measure greater than two <s>niṣkas</s> may be given, and there is no fault.
The same is said elsewhere too:

children.text: raso balistāmram ayaḥ purāgnī śilājatuḥ syādviṣatindukaśca
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s>, <s>bali</s>, copper, iron, <s>purāgni</s>, <s>śilājatu</s>, and <s>viṣatinduka</s>,

children.text: varā ca tulyaṃ gaganaṃ karañjaṃ pṛthak pṛthak śāṇacatuṣṭayaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: and <s>varā</s>, <s>gagana</s>, and <s>karañja</s>, equal in amount, four <s>śāṇas</s> each separately;

children.text: saṃmardya sarvaṃ madhunā ghṛtena ghṛtasya pātre nihitaṃ prayatnāt
children.translated_text: having ground all of it with honey and ghee, it should be carefully placed in a vessel of ghee.

children.text: kathaṃ bhajet pratyahamasya yasya śālyodanaṃ dugdhamadhutrayaṃ ca
children.translated_text: One should partake of a portion of this every day; his regimen is <s>śāli</s> rice, milk, and the three sweet substances.
Even one whose ears, fingers, and nose have crumbled away would, by means of this, become like <s>Smara</s> in form.
Abandonment of sexual intercourse is prescribed here, and also in dropsy and in a condition whose root is obstructed by <s>vāyu</s>.
Thus.
Now he explains <s>Udayādityarasa</s>, beginning "purified <s>sūta</s>."

children.text: dvidhā gandhaṃ dviguṇitaṃ gandhakaṃ pāradabhāgāditi śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Twice <s>gandha</s>" means sulfur doubled from the portion of mercury; this is to be supplied.

children.text: kanyā kumārī dinaṃ dinamekaṃ yāvat piṭharī mṛdānirmitapātraviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kanyā</s> is <s>kumārī</s>; "a day" means for one day. A <s>piṭharī</s> is a particular vessel made of clay.
This concerns the phrase "three times the <s>sūtaka</s>."
By this, the copper saucer, in relation to the measure of mercury,
should be understood as fashioned in a threefold measure. Regarding "purified":
the meaning is that it is made of pure copper, or else that the saucer has been purified with sour substances and the like.
Pure copper is that which is excellent within its own class.
For that copper is of two kinds: one is known as <s>mleccha</s>,
and the other as <s>naipāla</s>.
For so it is said:
Copper is <s>mleccha</s> and <s>naipālaka</s>; of the two, <s>naipāla</s> is best.
Thus.

children.text: kartavyavidhir apyasya yathā tadgolakākāraṃ dravyaṃ dṛḍhatalahaṇḍikānte niveśya tadupari tāmrapidhānakaṃ dattvā paścāt saṃdhiṃ mudrayitvā viśoṣya tadanu mudropari aṅguladvayotsedhaṃ sarvato bhasmāvakīrya paścāt tāmraśarāvoparyeva sajalagomayaṃ kiṃcit kiṃciditi vāraṃvāraṃ dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: The procedure for making this too is as follows: having placed that ball-shaped substance in a firm-bottomed small pot, put a copper lid over it, sealed the joint, and dried it, then, after scattering ash all around over the seal to a height of two fingers, one should repeatedly apply a little wet cow-dung on top of the copper saucer itself.

children.text: yāvad yāmadvayaṃ bhavati tāvat kharāgninā pacedityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The intention is that it should be cooked with a strong fire until two <s>yāma</s>s have passed.

children.text: atha paścātkāryamāha evaṃ niṣpanno'yaṃ rasaḥ saṃcūrṇya paścāt kāṣṭhodumbarikādīnāṃ kvāthena bhāvayet tena siddho bhavati dinaikamiti pratyekaṃ dravyamekaikaṃ dinaṃ bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: Now he states the subsequent procedure: when this <s>rasa</s> has thus been produced, it should be powdered and then levigated with the decoction of <s>kāṣṭhodumbarikā</s> and the other substances; by that it becomes perfected in one day, meaning that each individual substance should be levigated for one day.
<s>Kāṣṭhodumbarikā</s> is called <s>kaṭgulari</s> in ordinary speech.
<s>Rājavṛkṣaka</s> is <s>kṛtamālaka</s>; its leaves are meant.

children.text: asyānupānam āha khadirasya khadirasārasya kaṣāyeṇa kvathitarūpeṇa samena vākucīphalacūrṇasamānamānena saha paripācitaṃ taditi vākucīcūrṇaṃ tacca triśāṇaṃ ṭaṅkatrayaṃ saṃgṛhya gavāṃ kṣīraiḥ traiphalaiḥ kvāthairvā pibet ||
children.translated_text: He states its <s>anupāna</s> (vehicle): this <s>vākucī</s> powder, cooked with a decoction of <s>khadira</s>, that is, of <s>khadira</s> heartwood, in decocted form and in an amount equal to the powder of <s>vākucī</s> fruit, should be taken in the amount of three <s>śāṇa</s>s, three <s>ṭaṅka</s>s, and drunk with cow's milk or with decoctions of <s>triphalā</s>.
The word <s>rasa</s> is used with reference to <s>kilāsaka</s>, a particular kind of <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease).
Or else <s>kilāsa</s> should be called a subtype of <s>śvitra</s>.

children.text: eke kilāsa ityasya sthāne na saṃśayamiti paṭhanti tathā vyākhyānayanti ca ||
children.translated_text: Some read 'without doubt' in place of '<s>kilāsa</s>,' and they explain it accordingly.

children.text: paścāt te sphoṭā vakṣyamāṇapralepāt āmūlaṃ yathā syāt tathā pralepitāḥ kāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards those eruptions should be smeared with the paste to be described, so that they are covered down to the root.

children.text: tena sakalasphoṭāḥ saghanaṃ pralepitāḥ kāryā iti bhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: The meaning is that all the eruptions should be thickly covered with paste.

children.text: kecit piṣṭvā mūlāt pralepayet ityasya sthāne tulyaṃ piṣṭvā pralepayet iti paṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: Some read 'having ground it equally, one should apply it' in place of 'having ground it from the root, one should apply it.'
He states the substances for the paste, beginning with '<s>nīlī</s>'.
In place of <s>nīlī</s>, some read <s>tila</s>.

children.text: kecit athāparau vakṣyamāṇapralepau kṣepakau iti manyamānāḥ paṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: Some read while thinking that the two further pastes to be stated are interpolated additions.
Now he states <s>Sarveśvararasa</s>, beginning with 'purified <s>sūta</s>'.
Purified mercury should be taken in the measure of a <s>pala</s>.
<s>Gandha</s> means sulfur; 'four' means four <s>pala</s>s, because the <s>pala</s> measure is mentioned below.
By that, the sense is that the <s>rasa</s> too is in the measure of a <s>pala</s>.

children.text: yāmaṃ vicūrṇayediti tayoḥ śuddharasagandhakayoḥ kajjalīṃ kuryādityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'One should pulverize for a <s>yāma</s>' means that one should make <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulfide mixture) from those two purified substances, mercury and sulfur.

children.text: mṛtatāmrābhralohānāmiti mṛtatāmraṃ mṛtamabhrakaṃ mṛtalohamiti mṛtagrahaṇena daradaṃ hiṅgulamapi śodhitaṃ grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: 'Of dead copper, mica, and iron' means dead copper, dead mica, and dead iron; and by the mention of 'dead,' <s>darada</s>, cinnabar, too should be taken after purification.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ caiveti cakāragrahaṇāt suvarṇaraupyamapi mṛtaṃ deyam ||
children.translated_text: In 'and also gold and silver,' because of the word 'and,' gold and silver too should be added in calcined form.
'Dead <s>vajra</s>' means calcined diamond; <s>tālasatva</s> is the essence of <s>haritāla</s>.
Now he states the substances for levigation, beginning with '<s>jambīra</s>'.

children.text: unmatto dhattūrakaḥ snuhyarkayoḥ patrarasaḥ snuhī sehuṇḍā viṣamuṣṭiḥ kucalabhedaśabdavācyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Unmatta</s> is <s>dhattūraka</s>; the leaf-juice of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s> is meant; <s>snuhī</s> is <s>sehuṇḍā</s>; <s>viṣamuṣṭi</s> is denoted by the word <s>kucalabheda</s>.

children.text: eke viṣamuṣṭiśabdena mahānimba iti manyante tanna sarvamatam ||
children.translated_text: Some think that the word <s>viṣamuṣṭi</s> means <s>mahānimba</s>; that is not the opinion of everyone.
<s>Hayāri</s> is <s>karavīra</s>. The phrase means that it is to be steamed in a <s>vālukāyantra</s> (sand apparatus).
The <s>vālukāyantra</s> is well known.

children.text: asmatsaṃpradāye tu tat poṭṭalīkam uktadravyakalkena pralepitaṃ kṛtvā paścād vālukāyāṃ bhūmigatāyāṃ madhye kṣiptvā tadupari saptāṣṭabhir gomayairādīpayet ||
children.translated_text: In our tradition, however, that pouch is coated with the paste of the stated substances; afterwards it is thrown into sand set in the ground, and seven or eight cow-dung cakes should be kindled over it.
By that it becomes perfected.
By the expression 'thus for three days,' the meaning 'three times' is explained.
The rest is easy to understand.

children.text: atha svarṇakṣīrīrasavivaraṇam āha hemāhvā svarṇakṣīrī coka iti prasiddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now he gives the explanation of <s>Svarṇakṣīrīrasa</s>: <s>hemāhvā</s>, <s>svarṇakṣīrī</s>, is well known as <s>coka</s>.
The procedure with a buttermilk pot and the like for its purification has been stated.
'<s>Mūrchita</s> <s>sūta</s>' is so called because it removes disease.
For so it is said:
When killed, it destroys old age and death; when stupefied, it destroys disease.

children.text: baddhaṃ khecaratāṃ dadyāt ko'nyaḥ sūtāt kṛpākaraḥ
children.translated_text: When bound, it grants movement through the sky. Who other than <s>sūta</s> is so compassionate?
Thus.

children.text: kṣālayitvā viśodhayedityasya sthāne jalaiḥ prakṣālya viśoṣayediti pāṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In place of 'having washed it, one should purify it,' there is the reading 'having rinsed it with water, one should dry it.'
Now he states <s>Mehabaddharasa</s>, beginning with '<s>bhasmasūta</s>'.

children.text: bhasmasūtaṃ pāradabhasma mṛtaṃ kāntamiti mṛtakāntalohacūrṇaṃ kāntalohaṃ lohamāraṇe pūrvaṃ darśitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhasmasūta</s> is ash of mercury; 'dead <s>kānta</s>' means powder of calcined <s>kāntaloha</s>, and <s>kāntaloha</s> was shown earlier in the killing of metals.
'<s>Muṇḍa</s> ash' means that <s>muṇḍa</s> too is a particular kind of iron.

children.text: etadapi pūrvaṃ kathitameva eke muṇḍamiti kiṭṭaviśeṣaṃ manyante tanna sarvamatam ||
children.translated_text: This too was stated earlier. Some regard <s>muṇḍa</s> as a particular kind of slag; that is not the opinion of everyone.
Some read '<s>uragabhasma</s>' in place of '<s>muṇḍa</s>'.
There, according to one opinion, <s>uragabhasma</s> means <s>nāgabhasma</s>.
'Purified <s>tāpya</s>.'

children.text: tāpyaṃ suvarṇamākṣikaṃ śilā manaḥśilā vyoma abhrakam eke vyomasthāne vyoṣam iti paṭhanti vyākhyānayanti ca tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpya</s> is <s>suvarṇamākṣika</s>; <s>śilā</s> is <s>manaḥśilā</s>; <s>vyoma</s> is <s>abhraka</s>. Some read <s>vyoṣa</s> in place of <s>vyoma</s>, and explain it in that way.

children.text: tatra vyoṣaṃ trikaṭukam triphalā harītakyādikaṃ kaṅkolabījaṃ prasiddhaṃ kapitthaṃ kapitthaphalaṃ rajanī haridrā bhṛṅgarājo mārkavaśabdavācyaḥ etat sakalaṃ dravyaṃ samamānaṃ grāhyamiti sampradāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In that case, <s>vyoṣa</s> is <s>trikaṭuka</s>; <s>triphalā</s> is <s>harītakī</s> and the others; <s>kaṅkola</s> seed is well known; <s>kapittha</s> is the fruit of <s>kapittha</s>; <s>rajanī</s> is <s>haridrā</s>; <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> is denoted by the word <s>mārkava</s>. According to the tradition, all this material should be taken in equal measure.

children.text: eke bhṛṅgarājena bhāvayed ityasya sthāne samaṃ bhāvyaṃ ca bhṛṅginām iti paṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: Some read 'it should be levigated evenly with <s>bhṛṅgin</s>' in place of 'it should be levigated with <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>'.
'In the measure of a <s>niṣka</s>.'
The dose is four <s>māṣas</s>. As for the adjuvant, <s>mahānimba</s>, called <s>vakāina</s>, is used.

children.text: tasya bījāni phalāni tāni ca ṣaṭsaṃkhyāni grāhyāṇi taṇḍulatoyaṃ palapramāṇam ||
children.translated_text: Its seeds and fruits, six in number, should be taken, and rice-water in the measure of one <s>pala</s>.
The rest is easy to understand.
Regarding the expression "of four parts of <s>sūta</s>":

children.text: sūtasya pāradasya catvāro bhāgāḥ gandhakasya cāṣṭau bhāgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are four parts of <s>sūta</s>, that is, mercury, and eight parts of sulfur.
The five substances beginning with <s>rajanī</s> are each to have two parts.

children.text: rajanī haridrā triphalā harītakyādikaṃ śivā harītakī anena harītakīdviruktena bhāgāt saiva dviguṇā kāryā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rajanī</s> is turmeric. <s>Triphalā</s> consists of <s>harītakī</s> and the others. <s>Śivā</s> is <s>harītakī</s>; because <s>harītakī</s> is mentioned twice in this way, that very substance should be made double in quantity.

children.text: kecicchivāsthāne śilā iti paṭhanti vyākhyānayanti ca ||
children.translated_text: Some read <s>śilā</s> in place of <s>śivā</s>, and explain it accordingly.

children.text: tatra śilā manaḥśilā trivṛjjaipālacitrakaṃ pratyekaṃ tribhāgayutaṃ grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: In that case, <s>śilā</s> is <s>manaḥśilā</s>; <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>jaipāla</s>, and <s>citraka</s> should each be taken with three parts.
<s>Trivṛt</s> is <s>niśotha</s>.

children.text: jaipālaṃ dantibījaṃ citrakaṃ citrakajaṭātvak tryūṣaṇaṃ dantī ca jīrakamapi pratyekamaṣṭabhāgaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jaipāla</s>, <s>dantī</s> seed, <s>citraka</s>, namely the bark of <s>citraka</s> root, <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and also white cumin should each be understood as eight parts.
<s>Tryūṣa</s> is <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, and that is known as dry ginger, black pepper, and long pepper.
<s>Dantī</s> is well known; <s>jīraka</s> is the white variety.
Now he states the substances for impregnation, beginning with "<s>jayantī</s>."

children.text: jayantī śākabhedaḥ jīvantītyapare snukpayaḥ sehuṇḍakṣīraṃ bhṛṅgaṃ mārkavaṃ tacca ghamarāśabdavācyam natu bhṛṅgamatra guḍatvak vahniścitrakaḥ vātāritailameraṇḍatailam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jayantī</s> is a kind of vegetable; others say it is <s>jīvantī</s>. <s>Snukpayaḥ</s> is the latex of <s>sehuṇḍa</s>. <s>Bhṛṅga</s> is <s>mārkava</s>, and that is denoted by the word <s>ghamarā</s>, not <s>bhṛṅga</s> in another sense here. <s>Vahni</s> is <s>citraka</s>; <s>vātāritaila</s> is castor oil.
The rest is clear.
Now, presenting <s>Vidyādhararasa</s>, he says "sulfur," and so on.
<s>Tāpya</s> here is <s>suvarṇamākṣika</s>.
Regarding "purified <s>sūta</s>":
It means processed <s>sūta</s>. All this, in equal measure, should be triturated.

children.text: bhāvayeddinamiti pūrvaṃ dravyaṃ sakalaṃ saṃmardya paścāduktadraveṇa bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: "One should impregnate for a day" means that first all the substances should be thoroughly triturated together, and afterward impregnated with the stated liquid.
"For a day" means for each one separately; the rest is easy to understand.

children.text: saubhāgyakṣāraṃ taccātra bharjitaṃ deyaṃ svarṇaṃ śulbamapi mṛtamatra deyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saubhāgyakṣāra</s> should be added here after being roasted. Gold and copper too should be added here in a calcined state.
Sealing here is the procedure of a covered earthen-saucer vessel; the heating here is a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
The rest is easy to understand.
Now, presenting <s>Gajakesarīrasa</s>, he says "purified <s>sūta</s>," and so on.
The intention is that here, by firm trituration, one should make a <s>kajjalī</s> of mercury and sulfur.

children.text: sampradāyastu amlarasaiḥ saha dṛḍhamardanaṃ kāryaṃ na doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The traditional practice, however, is that firm trituration should be performed together with acidic juices; there is no fault in this.
Regarding "purified copper equal to the two":
The two are mercury and sulfur; "purified copper" means calcined copper.

children.text: eke dvayostulye śuddhatāmrasampuṭe iti paṭhanti vyākhyānayanti ca ||
children.translated_text: Some read and explain it as "in a purified copper container equal to the two."
Because of the statement "one should powder the container," this very interpretation is correct.

children.text: tena tāmrasampuṭe eva rasagandhakabhasma rodhayedityartha iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the meaning is that the ash of mercury and sulfur should be sealed specifically in a copper container.

children.text: anupānaṃ hiṃgvādicūrṇaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ karṣamānaṃ saṃgṛhya caturguṇenoṣṇodakena saha pibet ||
children.translated_text: The adjuvant is the powder beginning with <s>hiṅgu</s>, to be stated later; one should take a measure of one <s>karṣa</s> and drink it with four times as much hot water.
Now, presenting <s>Agnituṇḍavaṭīrasa</s>, he says "purified <s>sūta</s>," and so on.

children.text: eke śuddhasūtasamaṃ gandhamiti paṭhanti viṣaṃ na paṭhanti tad asaṃgatam ||
children.translated_text: Some read "sulfur equal to purified <s>sūta</s>" and do not read "poison"; that is inconsistent.
For it is seen in many places.

children.text: viṣamuṣṭiḥ kucelāśabdavācyaḥ sa ca sakaladravyaparimāṇena sāmyo yojyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣamuṣṭi</s> is denoted by the word <s>kucelā</s>, and it should be added in a quantity equal to all the ingredients.

children.text: eke vahnimāndyapraśāntaye ityasyānte tadanupānaślokamekaṃ paṭhanti mānayanti ca
children.translated_text: Some, at the end of the phrase "for pacifying sluggish digestive fire," read and accept one verse concerning its adjuvant:

children.text: pathyā śuṇṭhī guḍaṃ cānu palārdhaṃ bhakṣayet sadā
children.translated_text: One should always eat <s>pathyā</s>, dry ginger, and jaggery afterward, in the amount of half a <s>pala</s>.
The pill called <s>Agnituṇḍā</s> is known as the destroyer of every family of diseases.
Now, presenting <s>Ajīrṇakaṇṭakarasa</s>, he says "purified <s>sūta</s>," and so on.

children.text: śuddharasaṃ śuddhaviṣaṃ śuddhagandhakaṃ ca etattrikaṃ ca samamātraṃ saṃgṛhya tadanu ebhistribhiḥ sāmyaṃ ca maricacūrṇaṃ kṛtvā khalve taccatuṣkaṃ saṃcūrṇya paścāduktadraveṇa bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: One should take this triad, namely purified mercury, purified poison, and purified sulfur, in equal quantity; then, after making black-pepper powder equal to these three and grinding those four together in a mortar, one should afterwards impregnate it with the stated liquid.
The meaning is that one should impregnate it until the number becomes twenty-one.
"With <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>" means with the fruits of small <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>.
Some read one verse for the sake of the adjuvant:
As the following adjuvant, one should administer the root of <s>īśvarī</s>, ground with water, for drinking.
Or else conch shell and the root of <s>aśvattha</s> with water; it becomes a conqueror of indigestion.
This is not in current use.

children.text: atha manthānabhairavarasam āha mṛtaṃ sūtam ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, presenting <s>Manthānabhairavarasa</s>, he says "calcined <s>sūta</s>," and so on.
Here, in the absence of <s>puṣkaramūla</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s> should be taken.
Sulfur and <s>tāla</s> too should be taken after being purified.
<s>Tāla</s> is <s>haritāla</s>; <s>taṇḍulīya</s> is <s>meghanāda</s>.
Now, presenting <s>Vātanāśanarasa</s>, he says "<s>sūta</s>, gold, and diamond," and so on.

children.text: sūtaṃ pāradaṃ hāṭakaṃ suvarṇaṃ vajraṃ hīrakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> is mercury; <s>hāṭaka</s> is gold; <s>vajra</s> is diamond.
Some read "sulfur" in place of <s>mākṣika</s>; this is an attractive reading.

children.text: tālaṃ haritālaṃ nīlāñjanaṃ prasiddhaṃ tadabhāve sīsakaṃ grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāla</s> is <s>haritāla</s>. <s>Nīlāñjana</s> is well known; in its absence, lead should be taken.
Because it can arise from that, <s>abdhiphena</s> is <s>samudraphena</s>, sea-foam.
All this is in equal measure.
The meaning is that the five salts are five parts.

children.text: sindhusauvarcalopetaṃ biḍaṃ sāmudrajaṃ gaḍam iti pañcalavaṇam ||
children.translated_text: The five salts are <s>sindhu</s>, <s>sauvarcala</s>, <s>biḍa</s>, sea-born salt, and <s>gaḍa</s>.
Regarding "having sealed it, he should cook it below in a <s>bhūdhara</s>":

children.text: tatsakalaṃ dinaikam ekadinaṃ saṃmardya paścādbhūdharayantre paced ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The intention is that, after triturating all of it for one day, he should then cook it in a <s>bhūdharayantra</s>.
The <s>bhūdharayantra</s> has already been shown before.
Regarding the adjuvant phrase "with <s>kṛṣṇā</s>," one should add powder of <s>pippalī</s>.
This very <s>rasa</s> is recited in another work for <s>bhūtonmāda</s>.
Here, in some places, a reversed reading is seen, as follows:

children.text: sūtāyastāmramabhraṃ ca mṛtaṃ svarṇaṃ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: Mercury, iron, copper, mica, and calcined gold are each in equal amounts;

children.text: sūtapādaṃ mṛtaṃ vajraṃ tālaṃ gandhaṃ manaḥśilām ||
children.translated_text: calcined diamond in a quarter measure of the mercury, and <s>tāla</s>, sulfur, and <s>manaḥśilā</s>;
<s>Tuttha</s>, purified <s>nīlāñjana</s>, and sea-foam, equal to the <s>rasa</s>;
and of the five salts, each share should be measured equal to the <s>rasa</s>.
One should triturate it with <s>citraka</s>, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, and the milk of <s>vajrī</s>;

children.text: dinānte golakaṃ kṛtvā ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: at day's end, after making it into a ball and sealing it, one should cook it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
The preparation named <s>Mahābhūtāṅkuśarasa</s> should be licked in a dose of two <s>guñjās</s>
with the juices of ginger alone, for pacifying <s>bhūtonmāda</s>.
Afterward one should drink a decoction of <s>daśamūla</s> mixed with <s>pippalī</s>. Thus.
Now he explains <s>Kanakasundararasa</s>, beginning with "of gold" and so on.

children.text: kanakādīnyatra mṛtāni grāhyāṇi śāṇopalakṣitatvād atra bhāga eva boddhavyaḥ yathāsambhavatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Here the substances beginning with gold are to be taken as calcined. Since the <s>śāṇa</s> is only indicated, here only a proportional part should be understood, because that is what is possible.

children.text: kanakamatra suvarṇaṃ sūtaḥ pāradaḥ gandho gandhakaḥ sauvīraṃ sauvīrāñjanaṃ lohaṃ sārasaṃjñam lāṅgalī kalihārikā amlaphalāni bījapūrajambīraprabhṛtīni ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kanaka</s> here is gold; <s>sūta</s> is mercury; <s>gandha</s> is sulfur; <s>sauvīra</s> is <s>sauvīrāñjana</s>; <s>loha</s> is what is called <s>sāra</s>; <s>lāṅgalī</s> is <s>kalihārikā</s>; sour fruits are <s>bījapūra</s>, <s>jambīra</s>, and the like.
The mild <s>puṭa</s> here is a particular form of <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
The rest is easy.

children.text: atha saṃnipātabhairavarasam āha raso gandhastrikarṣaḥ syādityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now he explains <s>Saṃnipātabhairavarasa</s>, beginning with "<s>rasa</s> and sulfur should be three <s>karṣas</s>" and so on.

children.text: rasaḥ pāradaḥ gandho gandhaka etaddvayaṃ militaṃ trikarṣaṃ syādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> is mercury, and <s>gandha</s> is sulfur; the meaning is that these two together should amount to three <s>karṣas</s>.
"Copper, <s>tāra</s>, <s>āra</s>, <s>vaṅga</s>, <s>ahi</s>, and <s>sāra</s> are each of one <s>karṣa</s>."
Copper is well known.

children.text: tāraṃ raupyam āraṃ pītalohaṃ vaṅgaṃ raṅgavācyam ahiḥ sīsakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāra</s> is silver; <s>āra</s> is brass; <s>vaṅga</s> is denoted by <s>raṅga</s>; <s>ahi</s> is lead.

children.text: sāro lohaḥ etattāmrādikaṃ sarvaṃ mṛtaṃ grāhyamiti sampradāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sāra</s> is iron. The tradition is that all this, beginning with copper, should be taken calcined.
"Each of one <s>karṣa</s>" means:
the intended sense is that each one is measured by a <s>karṣa</s>.

children.text: aparamapi śigru śobhāñjanaṃ jvālāmukhī jayantī bilvebhya iti
children.translated_text: Another point: <s>śigru</s> is <s>śobhāñjana</s>, <s>jvālāmukhī</s> is <s>jayantī</s>, and in the phrase "from <s>bilva</s>"...
the supplied words are "from the juices of <s>bilva</s> root."
<s>Taṇḍulīya</s> is denoted by the word <s>meghanāda</s>.
<s>Svarasa</s> here means either freshly prepared juice or boiled decoction.

children.text: atha prakṣepārthaṃ dravyāṇyāha tatra siddharase pravāṇacūrṇakarṣeṇeti ||
children.translated_text: Now he states the substances for addition: "There, in the perfected <s>rasa</s>, with a <s>karṣa</s> of <s>pravāṇa</s> powder" and so on.
One should mix in <s>pravāṇa</s> powder and poison powder.
<s>Pravāṇa</s> powder is in the measure of a <s>karṣa</s>, and poison powder is only a <s>śāṇa</s>.
"<s>Pravāṇa</s>" means especially <s>vāṇa</s>, that is, powder of lime.

children.text: eke pravālacūrṇaṃ paṭhanti tatra pravālacūrṇaṃ vidrumacūrṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: Some read <s>pravāla</s> powder; in that case <s>pravāla</s> powder is coral powder.
Others say shell powder; in its absence, conch-shell powder. That is our tradition.

children.text: bhāvanārthaṃ dravyāṇyāha kṛṣṇasarpasya garalaiḥ kṛtvā tatpūrvoktaṃ dravyaṃ dvivelaṃ yāvadbhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: He states the substances for trituration: with the poisons of a black snake one should triturate that previously mentioned substance for two rounds.
<s>Garala</s> is that particular poison.
And with <s>tagara</s> and the other substances one should triturate it once with each.
"Each separately" means separately, one by one.
<s>Tagara</s> is well known.

children.text: māṃsī jaṭākhyā hemāhvā svarṇakṣīrī vetaso jalavetasaḥ kaṇā pippalī nīlinīpatrakamiti nīlikāpatram eke nīlinī patrakaṃ ca dravyadvayaṃ vyākhyānayanti tacca na sarvamataṃ kuṭherakaḥ prasiddhaḥ devadālī vallīviśeṣaḥ muṇḍikā kedāramuṇḍī madhūkaṃ madhūkavṛkṣaḥ jātī mālatīraso'tra sadyaskaḥ kvathito vā yathālābhāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māṃsī</s> is the one called <s>jaṭā</s>; <s>hemāhvā</s> is <s>svarṇakṣīrī</s>; <s>vetasa</s> is <s>jalavetasa</s>; <s>kaṇā</s> is <s>pippalī</s>; <s>nīlinīpatraka</s> means the leaf of <s>nīlikā</s>. Some explain <s>nīlinī</s> and <s>patraka</s> as two substances, but that is not everyone's view. <s>Kuṭheraka</s> is well known; <s>devadālī</s> is a particular creeper; <s>muṇḍikā</s> is <s>kedāramuṇḍī</s>; <s>madhūka</s> is the <s>madhūka</s> tree; <s>jātī</s> is <s>mālatī</s>. The juice here is fresh or boiled, according to availability.

children.text: ayaṃ siddharaso dviguñjāpramitaḥ ṣoḍaśamaricānvito bījapūrārdrakarasena saha bhakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: This perfected <s>rasa</s>, measured at two <s>guñjās</s> and accompanied by sixteen peppers, should be consumed with the juice of <s>bījapūra</s> and ginger.
Now he explains <s>Grahaṇīkapāṭarasa</s>, beginning with "silver, pearl, and gold" and so on; it is easy.

children.text: madhyapuṭaṃ tu laghupuṭasaṃjñaṃ tacca ṣoḍaśāṅgulagarte pratipāditam ||
children.translated_text: But the middle <s>puṭa</s> is called the light <s>puṭa</s>, and it has been described in a pit of sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s>.
Thus:
A carefully made pit, all its dimensions measured by sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s>, having placed it in the middle,
with fire from very dry cow-dung cakes for the accomplishment of mercury: this is the light <s>gajapuṭa</s> previously taught by the great sages.
Thus.
The measure of pepper here too is only a <s>māṣa</s>.
Or else it should be given according to the <s>doṣa</s>.
Now he explains <s>Grahaṇīvajrakapāṭarasa</s>, beginning with "calcined mercury and mica" and so on.

children.text: mṛtasūtaṃ pāradaṃ bhavati tāvat parimāṇaṃ pṛthak ṣaḍdravyāṇi grāhyāṇi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛtasūta</s> is mercury; the six substances are to be taken separately in that same measure.

children.text: eke ṣaḍdravyaṃ tu pāradasāmyaṃ deyamiti manyante tanna sarvamatam ||
children.translated_text: Some think that the group of six substances should be given equal to the mercury; that is not everyone's view.
Rather, there is one part of calcined mercury,
and six parts of mica and the rest; this is everyone's view.
"<s>Tatas</s>" means "from that."
<s>Jayantī</s> is a kind of herb.
<s>Jambīra</s> means the juice of the <s>jambīra</s> fruit.
<s>Bhṛṅga</s> is <s>mārkava</s>.
By the expression "for three days," the intended sense is that trituration with each substance is to be given for one day only.

children.text: lohapātra ityādinā piṭharīyaṃ vālukābhiḥ prapūryetyasmadīyasampradāyāt kāryo na doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the phrase "in an iron vessel" and so on, according to our tradition the instruction "having filled the vessel with sand" should be supplied, and there is no fault.

children.text: yāmārdhamityanena ghaṭikācatuṣṭayaṃ yāvat etatsiddhaṃ bhavati tadā prativiṣāṃ mocarasaṃ ca pṛthaksiddhaṃ rasatulyaṃ melayitvā paścāduktadravyasya rasaiḥ kṛtvā bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: By "half a <s>yāma</s>," it is meant that when this has become perfected for four <s>ghaṭikās</s>, then one should mix in <s>prativiṣā</s> and <s>mocarasa</s>, separately prepared, in an amount equal to the <s>rasa</s>, and afterward triturate it with the juices of the substances stated.
The substance <s>prativiṣā</s> is what is denoted by the word <s>ativiṣā</s>.
<s>Mocarasa</s> is the exudate of <s>śālmalī</s>.
Some also say that <s>bhāvanā</s> (trituration or impregnation) should be done with <s>prativiṣā</s> and <s>mocarasa</s>.

children.text: vijayātra bhaṅgā saptadhā bhāvanā ekadravyeṇa kāryā anyeṣāṃ vakṣyamāṇānāṃ pṛthagekavāraṃ tatra dhātakī dhātakīkusumāni indrayavaṃ kuṭajabījaṃ rāsnā surabhī madhvatra lehane yāvattāvanmānaṃ deyam ||
children.translated_text: Here <s>vijayā</s> is <s>bhaṅgā</s>. A sevenfold <s>bhāvanā</s> should be done with one substance; with the other substances about to be stated, once each separately. There <s>dhātakī</s> means <s>dhātakī</s> flowers, <s>indrayava</s> is the seed of <s>kuṭaja</s>, and <s>rāsnā</s> is <s>surabhī</s>. Honey should be added in whatever quantity is needed here for a linctus.

children.text: anupānārthadravyeṣu vahniścitrakajaṭā viḍaṃ biḍalavaṇaṃ lavaṇaṃ saindhavam ||
children.translated_text: Among the substances for the adjuvant, <s>vahni</s> is root of <s>citraka</s>, <s>viḍa</s> is <s>biḍa-lavaṇa</s>, and <s>lavaṇa</s> is <s>saindhava</s>.
Now he explains <s>Madanakāmadevarasa</s>, beginning with <s>tāra</s>.

children.text: tāraṃ raupyaṃ vajraṃ hīrakaṃ tadabhāve vaikrāntaṃ grāhyamiti vyavahārāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāra</s> is silver; <s>vajra</s> is diamond. In its absence <s>vaikrānta</s> should be taken, according to practice.
<s>Sūtaka</s> is mercury, and <s>loha</s> is the metal known as <s>sāra</s>.

children.text: atra kramavṛddhistu pūrvadravyāduttaravṛddhirboddhavyā asmatsampradāye tu rajatādīni dravyāṇi atra mṛtāni deyānīti vyavahāro'pi dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Here gradual increase should be understood as each later substance being increased beyond the preceding substance. In our tradition, however, the practice is also seen that silver and the other substances are to be added here after being calcined.
<s>Kanyakā</s> is <s>kumārī</s>.
For the word <s>vimudrā</s>, the supplied expression is a glass bottle.
Powdered <s>saindhava</s> should be placed on both sides of the glass bottle.

children.text: siddharasasya bhāvanārthaṃ dravyāṇyāha arkadugdham arkabhavaṃ kṣīraṃ kākolī prasiddhā vānarī kapikacchūḥ muśalī kandaviśeṣaḥ ikṣukaḥ kokilākṣaḥ tālamūlī padmakandaḥ kamalakandaḥ kaseruko'pi vikhyātaḥ kāśatṛṇasaṃjñaḥ prasiddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He states the substances for <s>bhāvanā</s> of the perfected <s>rasa</s>: <s>arkadugdha</s> is the milk or latex produced from <s>arka</s>; <s>kākolī</s> is well known; <s>vānarī</s> is <s>kapikacchū</s>; <s>muśalī</s> is a particular tuber; <s>ikṣuka</s> is <s>kokilākṣa</s>; <s>tālamūlī</s> is <s>padmakanda</s>, the lotus tuber; <s>kaseruka</s> too is known, and what is called <s>kāśatṛṇa</s> is well known.
Afterward he states the substances for the powder, beginning with <s>kastūrī</s>.

children.text: kastūrī mṛganābhijā vyoṣaṃ trikaṭukaṃ pūrvacūrṇādbhāvanābhiḥ pratipāditadravyādaṣṭamāṃśaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kastūrī</s> is produced from the musk deer's navel; <s>vyoṣa</s> is <s>trikaṭuka</s>. The powder beginning with <s>kastūrī</s> should be added as an eighth part in relation to the previous powder indicated through the <s>bhāvanās</s>.
Thus the previous powder is seven parts, and the group beginning with <s>kastūrī</s> is one part.
And so forth.

children.text: sūtaḥ pāradaḥ vajraṃ hīrakaṃ ahiḥ sīsakaṃ muktā prasiddhā tāraṃ raupyaṃ hema suvarṇaṃ asitābhrakaṃ kṛṣṇābhrakaṃ etatsarvamapi māritaṃ grāhyam ityatra vyavahāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> is mercury; <s>vajra</s> is diamond; <s>ahi</s> is lead; <s>muktā</s> is well known; <s>tāra</s> is silver; <s>hema</s> is gold; <s>asitābhraka</s> is black mica. The practice here is that all this too should be taken after being calcined.
The measure of each of these too is one <s>karṣa</s>.

children.text: irimedo viṭkhadiraḥ sa ca loke reojaśabdavācyaḥ tasya tvak grāhyā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Irimeda</s> is <s>viṭkhadira</s>, and in common usage it is denoted by the word <s>reoja</s>. Its bark should be taken.
The other two substances also, for the purpose of mixing, should each be added in a measure of two <s>karṣas</s>.

children.text: tacca pravālacūrṇaṃ vidrumacūrṇaṃ gandhaṃ gandhakaṃ mṛgaśṛṅgake mṛgaśṛṅgasampuṭe tadauṣadhaṃ dhāryamityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those are powdered <s>pravāla</s>, that is, powdered coral, and <s>gandha</s>, that is, sulfur. By <s>mṛgaśṛṅgaka</s>, the intention is that this medicine should be kept in a capsule made of deer horn.
And a mild sealed heating means a light <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: paścādbhāvanārthaṃ dravyāṇyāha dhātakī dhātakīkusumāni kākolī svanāmakhyātā madhukaṃ madhukayaṣṭī māṃsī jaṭākhyaṃ sugandhadravyam ||
children.translated_text: Afterward he states the substances for <s>bhāvanā</s>: <s>dhātakī</s> means <s>dhātakī</s> flowers; <s>kākolī</s> is known by its own name; <s>madhuka</s> is <s>madhukayaṣṭī</s>; <s>māṃsī</s> is the fragrant substance called <s>jaṭā</s>.

children.text: balātrayaṃ prasiddham tacca balā atibalā nāgabaleti bisaṃ mṛṇālaṃ bhasīṇḍaśabdavācyaṃ loke iṅgudaṃ vṛkṣeṅgudaṃ drākṣā prasiddhā pippalavandākamiti pippalavṛkṣasya vandā vandā ca viṭapalagno gulmaviśeṣaḥ eke pippalavandākaṃ dravyadvayaṃ varṇayanti tatra pippalaḥ pippalatvak vandāvṛkṣaḥ vandā prasiddhā apare pippalīvandākamiti vyākhyānayanti vāṇaḥ sahacaraḥ eke vāṇasthāne varīti paṭhanti parṇīcatuṣṭayamiti ||
