children.translated_text: The three <s>balās</s> are well known, namely <s>balā</s>, <s>atibalā</s>, and <s>nāgabalā</s>. <s>Bisa</s> is <s>mṛṇāla</s>, called <s>bhasīṇḍa</s> in common usage. <s>Iṅguda</s> is tree <s>iṅguda</s>, and <s>drākṣā</s> is well known. <s>Pippalavandāka</s> means the <s>vandā</s> of the <s>pippala</s> tree, and <s>vandā</s> is a particular shrub attached to a branch. Some describe <s>pippalavandāka</s> as two substances: <s>pippala</s>, meaning <s>pippala</s> bark, and the <s>vandā</s> tree, the well known <s>vandā</s>. Others explain it as <s>pippalīvandāka</s>. <s>Vāṇa</s> is <s>sahacara</s>; some read <s>varī</s> in place of <s>vāṇa</s>. The four <s>parṇīs</s> are as follows.

children.text: māṣaparṇī mudgaparṇī śālaparṇī pṛṣṭhiparṇī ceti parūṣakaṃ phālasāśabdavācyaṃ kaserukaṃ prasiddham ||
children.translated_text: They are <s>māṣaparṇī</s>, <s>mudgaparṇī</s>, <s>śālaparṇī</s>, and <s>pṛṣṭhiparṇī</s>. <s>Parūṣaka</s> is denoted by the word <s>phālasā</s>, and <s>kaseruka</s> is well known.

children.text: madhūkaṃ madhūkavṛkṣapuṣpāṇi vānarī kapikacchūḥ eteṣāṃ svarasena pratyekaṃ bhāvayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Madhūka</s> means the flowers of the <s>madhūka</s> tree, and <s>vānarī</s> is <s>kapikacchū</s>. The meaning is that one should carry out <s>bhāvanā</s> with the fresh juice of each of these separately.
Now he states the substances for the powder, beginning with <s>elā</s>, <s>tvak</s>, and <s>patraka</s>.

children.text: vāṃśī tvakkṣīrī vaṃśarocanā iti prasiddhā agaru prasiddham keśaraṃ nāgakeśaraṃ mustaṃ prasiddham mṛgamadaḥ kastūrī kṛṣṇā pippalī jalaṃ vālakaṃ candraḥ karpūraḥ etatsakalaṃ śāṇamitaṃ ṭaṅkapramāṇaṃ bhakṣaṇārthaṃ rātrau niśāmukhe ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāṃśī</s> is <s>tvakkṣīrī</s>, well known as <s>vaṃśarocanā</s>; <s>agaru</s> is well known; <s>keśara</s> is <s>nāgakeśara</s>; <s>musta</s> is well known; <s>mṛgamada</s> is <s>kastūrī</s>; <s>kṛṣṇā</s> is <s>pippalī</s>; <s>jala</s> is <s>vālaka</s>; and <s>candra</s> is camphor. All this, measured by the <s>śāṇa</s>, is a <s>ṭaṅka</s> in quantity, for consumption at night, at the beginning of the night.

children.text: anupānamāha dvipalaṃ kṣīraṃ pibet kathambhūtam sitādīnāṃ dravyatrayāṇāṃ cūrṇaṃ melayitvā karṣamātraṃ saṃgṛhya karṣamānena ca ghṛtena saha saṃmardya tanmiśritam ||
children.translated_text: He states the adjuvant: one should drink two <s>palas</s> of milk. What kind? Milk mixed with the powder of the three substances beginning with <s>sitā</s>; after combining that powder, one should take a <s>karṣa</s> of it, rub it together with ghee in a <s>karṣa</s> measure, and mix the milk with that.

children.text: sitā matsyaṇḍī dhātrī āmalakī vidārī vidārīkandaḥ sukhitamānasaḥ svasthaḥ natu āturaḥ tasya vihitatvāt na hāniṃ kvāpi gacchatīti sa puruṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sitā</s> is <s>matsyaṇḍī</s>; <s>dhātrī</s> is <s>āmalakī</s>; <s>vidārī</s> is the tuber of <s>vidārī</s>. Happy in mind means healthy, not ill, because it is prescribed for such a person. The statement that he never comes to harm anywhere refers to that man.
The meaning is that he does not incur loss of virility.
Now he explains <s>Loharasāyana</s>, beginning with one part of purified <s>rasendra</s>.

children.text: śuddhaṃ saṃskāritaṃ rasendraḥ pāradaḥ tasyaiko bhāgaḥ śuddhagandhakasya dvau bhāgau gandhakaśuddhiśca pūrvaṃ kathitaiva ||
children.translated_text: Purified means processed; <s>rasendra</s> is mercury. Of it there is one part, and of purified sulfur there are two parts. The purification of sulfur has already been described before.
There, in the <s>kajjalikā</s>, the phrase means powder produced from <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron.
Some say that it is purified iron powder, the powder of calcined <s>sāra</s> metal.
And that should be taken equal to the preceding <s>kajjalikā</s>.

children.text: praharaikaṃ mardanaṃ kevalaṃ kajjalikālohacūrṇayoreva kathitaṃ natu svarasādinā vakṣyamāṇasvarasaireva tridinaṃ yāvadityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Trituration for one <s>prahara</s> is stated only for the <s>kajjalikā</s> and the iron powder, not with fresh juices and the like. Rather, with the fresh juices to be stated, it is intended to continue for three days.

children.text: gharma iti kharatarasūryāṃśutāpite ata eva tasya soṣṇo mahān dhūmodgamo bhavati iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gharma</s> means that which is heated by the very fierce rays of the sun; for that very reason, a great emission of smoke, along with heat, occurs from it.
Some say that by that method <s>lohamṛti</s> (the calcination of iron) would occur in this way.

children.text: svamate tu dhānyakuśūloṣitaṃ trirātraṃ yāvadbhavati paścād yaduddharet tatkālameva gharme dhāraṇena mṛtiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: In my own view, however, when it has remained in a grain-bin for as long as three nights, then whatever is taken out afterward undergoes calcination by being kept in the sun's heat at that very time.
By the phrase 'extremely compacted into a lump,' wrapping it in castor leaves and the like is intended.
He states the subsequent procedure with 'with juices' and so on.
<s>Kuṭhāracchinnā</s> is, in common usage, denoted by the word <s>tipānī</s>.
Others call it <s>kurejā</s>.
The expression <s>trivela</s> ('three times') is to be connected with the other substances as well.
Therefore the meaning is that one should triturate it three times with each individual juice.

children.text: gharme ca pratyekaṃ śoṣaṇam api vihitam ||
children.translated_text: And drying in the sun's heat is also prescribed separately after each one.

children.text: trikaṭoḥ tryūṣaṇasya śuṇṭhīmaricapippalyas trikaṭus tryūṣaṇaṃ smṛtam iti ||
children.translated_text: Regarding <s>trikaṭu</s>, that is <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>: dried ginger, black pepper, and long pepper. Thus it is remembered: <s>trikaṭu</s>, consisting of <s>śuṇṭhī</s>, <s>marica</s>, and <s>pippalī</s>, is <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>.
<s>Vāsā</s> is <s>āṭarūṣaka</s>; <s>amṛtā</s> is <s>guḍūcī</s>.

children.text: lohapātre tat kṣiptveti pūrvaṃ mṛtpātre dhāryamiti prāptam ||
children.translated_text: When it says, 'having put that in an iron vessel,' the earlier expectation was that it should be kept in an earthen vessel.

children.text: pāṣāṇakhalve vā triphalājalaiḥ triphalākvāthaiḥ triphalā harītakyādi dāḍimatvak valkalaṃ vāsā āṭarūṣakaḥ bhṛṅgo mārkavaḥ kuraṇṭakaḥ sahacaraḥ palāśakadalīdrāvairiti palāśaḥ prasiddhaḥ tasya drāvaḥ svaniryāsaḥ kadalīdrāvaḥ kadalīkandaniryāsaḥ bījako vijayasāro vṛkṣaviśeṣas tasya śṛtena kvāthena nīlikā nīlī alambuṣā muṇḍī babbūlaphalikā babbūlavṛkṣasya phalānītyarthaḥ nāgabalā gāṅgerukī śatāvarī gokṣurakau prasiddhau pātālagaruḍī chirahaṇṭiśabdavācyā ||
children.translated_text: Or, in a stone mortar, 'with <s>triphala</s> waters' means with decoctions of <s>triphala</s>. <s>Triphala</s> is <s>harītakī</s> and the others; <s>dāḍimatvak</s> is pomegranate bark; <s>vāsā</s> is <s>āṭarūṣaka</s>; <s>bhṛṅga</s> is <s>mārkava</s>; <s>kuraṇṭaka</s> is <s>sahacara</s>. In 'with the liquids of <s>palāśa</s> and <s>kadalī</s>,' <s>palāśa</s> is well known, and its liquid is its own exudate; <s>kadalī</s>-liquid is the exudate of the banana rhizome. <s>Bījaka</s> is <s>vijayasāra</s>, a particular tree; 'with its boiled liquid' means with its decoction. <s>Nīlikā</s> is <s>nīlī</s>; <s>alambuṣā</s> is <s>muṇḍī</s>; <s>babbūlaphalikā</s> means the fruits of the <s>babbūla</s> tree; <s>nāgabalā</s> is <s>gāṅgerukī</s>; <s>śatāvarī</s> and <s>gokṣura</s> are well known; <s>pātālagaruḍī</s> is denoted by the word <s>chirahaṇṭi</s>.
For the <s>anupāna</s> (vehicle), <s>varā-kvātha</s> means <s>triphala</s> decoction, and <s>chinnā-sattva</s> means <s>guḍūcī</s> extract.
The rest is easy to understand.
